def get_basis_index(self, label: object) -> int:
    """Return the index of the basis state of a label or an index.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of a basis state, or its index.

    Returns:
        index:
            The index of the basis state.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The label names no basis state.
    """
    space = self.space
    if isinstance(label, str) and label in space.basis:
        return space.basis[label]
    if isinstance(label, int | np.integer) and not isinstance(label, bool) and 0 <= label < space.dimension:
        return int(label)
    labels = ', '.join(map(repr, space.basis)) or 'none'
    error_msg = (
        f'{type(self.element).__name__} {self.label!r}: {label!r} is no basis state. Use a label ({labels}) or an '
        f'index from 0 to {space.dimension - 1}.'
    )
    raise ValidationError(error_msg)

def get_initial_vector(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
    """Return the initial state of the element as a normalised vector.

    Returns:
        vector:
            The initial state.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The initial state names no basis state, or is a vector of the wrong size or norm.
    """
    initial = getattr(self.element, self.state)
    if isinstance(initial, str | int | np.integer):
        vector = np.zeros(self.dimension, dtype=complex)
        vector[self.get_basis_index(initial)] = 1.0
        return vector
    vector = np.asarray(initial, dtype=complex).ravel()
    norm = float(np.linalg.norm(vector))
    if vector.size != self.dimension or abs(norm - 1) > NORM_TOLERANCE:
        error_msg = (
            f'The initial vector of {self.label!r} has {vector.size} components and norm {norm:.6g}, but its '
            f'space has dimension {self.dimension} and states have norm 1. Normalise the vector.'
        )
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    return vector

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Define systems, which compose elements and interactions on a space, in a time.

CompositeSystem composes parts given as data, and BaseSystem is the base of a system class that builds its parts from model parameters.

docs.title: BaseSystem(label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BasePart[BaseSpace, SimpleNamespace]

An abstract system that builds its parts from the parameters of its model.

A subclass takes the parameters of its model as arguments of its __init__, such as the rates of an epidemic, and stores each under the same name, as a scikit-learn estimator does, so get_params, set_params, and clone work. It builds its parts in the hook _build_system, which returns the CompositeSystem of its elements, interactions, nested systems, space, and time. prepare builds the parts again when a parameter has changed since the last build, and prepares them as system_. The tags of a system come from its parts and are never declared. The type parameter CompositeT names the class of the composite, so BaseSystem[CompositeSystem] types system_ as CompositeSystem.

A subclass may give tuned run settings as class variables, which simulate reads for the arguments a call leaves out:

  • until and dt: the end time and the time between frames.
  • solver, backend, and compiler: how the system runs.
  • observables and invariants: what to record, and the tolerance of each observable that must stay constant.
  • initial_state and schedule: the initial values by dotted state name, and the functions of time that drive parameters.

Unlike CompositeSystem, which takes its parts as data, it writes them in terms of named model parameters. Choose it when a model has parameters that users set, sweep, or calibrate, as every system of the catalog does.

It appears in many fields. The SIR model of an epidemic, the Lotka-Volterra model of predators and prey, the Ising model of a magnet, and the Kuramoto model of oscillators are system classes.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The composite of the parts built from the model parameters at the last prepare.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import BaseSystem, CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> class TankElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.x = x
>>> class DecaySystem(BaseSystem):
...     def __init__(self, label='decay', k=1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.k = k
...
...     def _build_system(self):
...         decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='tank', state='x', rate=lambda s: -self.k * s.target.x)
...         return CompositeSystem(self.label, elements=[TankElement('tank')], interactions=[decay])
>>> system = DecaySystem(k=0.5).prepare()
>>> system.get_params()
{'k': 0.5, 'label': 'decay'}
>>> sorted(system.get_tags().laws)
['rate']

def get_run_settings(self) -> RunSettings:
    """Return the tuned run settings of the system.

    `simulate` uses them for every argument a call leaves out. The settings are the class attributes `until`, `dt`,
    `solver`, `observables`, `initial_state`, `invariants`, `schedule`, `compiler`, and `backend`. A system whose
    settings depend on its model parameters or on its built parts overrides this method.

    Returns:

            The tuned run settings by name.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.chemistry.pattern_formation import GrayScottSystem
        >>> sorted(GrayScottSystem().get_run_settings())
        ['backend', 'compiler', 'dt', 'initial_state', 'invariants', 'observables', 'schedule', 'solver', 'until']
    """
    return RunSettings(
        until=self.until,
        dt=self.dt,
        solver=self.solver,

docs.title: CompositeSystem(label='system', *, elements=(), interactions=(), systems=(), space=None, time=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem['CompositeSystem']

A system that composes elements, interactions, and nested systems as data.

The system lives on a space, in a time, and says nothing about how it runs. An interaction refers to an element by its path relative to the system that holds the interaction, so forest/foxes names the element foxes of the nested system forest. Groups and nested systems without a space of their own live on the space of the system.

The tags of a system come from its parts: its own time, or the time its parts agree on, every space of its parts, the union of their domains, law kinds, and structures, and a stochastic randomness when any part is stochastic. prepare rejects an element bound to a role that does not accept the domains of the states the role reads.

Unlike BaseSystem, which builds its parts from model parameters, it takes the parts themselves. Choose it when composing a model from parts once, or when nesting systems inside a larger one.

It appears in many fields. A predator and its prey on a lattice, a savings account with interest and withdrawals, a circuit of resistors and capacitors, and an economy of nested regions are composite systems.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The system itself, prepared.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> class DecayElement(Element):
...     law_classes = (RateLaw,)
...
...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.x = x
...
...     def _get_laws(self, namespace):
...         return [RateLaw(namespace.x, -namespace.x)]
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[DecayElement('decay')]).prepare()
>>> namespace = SimpleNamespace(decay=SimpleNamespace(x=var('x')))
>>> [type(law).__name__ for law in system.run(namespace).laws_]
['RateLaw']
>>> tags = system.get_tags()
>>> sorted(tags.time), sorted(tags.space), sorted(tags.laws), tags.randomness
(['continuous'], ['none'], ['rate'], 'deterministic')

def __init__(
    self,
    label: str = 'system',
    *,
    elements: Sequence[BaseElement] = (),
    interactions: Sequence[BaseInteraction] = (),
    systems: Sequence[BaseSystem] = (),
    space: BaseSpace | None = None,
    time: BaseTime | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the label and the parts of the system.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

        elements:
            The elements and groups.

        interactions:

            The nested systems, composites or system classes such as the ready-made systems of the catalog, each

    """

    self.interactions = interactions
    self.systems = systems
    self.space = space
    self.time = time

docs.title: JaxBackend
docs.text:
Bases: BaseBackend

A backend that writes discrete maps and differential equations as JAX functions.

The ODEs are ordinary differential equations. The functions return new arrays instead of writing into buffers, so JAX traces, compiles, and differentiates them. Reductions lower to sums, means, and matrix products, and a reduction weighted by a shaped parameter to the product with its block of the parameter vector reshaped into a matrix. The forward functions in functions_ take and return NumPy arrays and compute in double precision. Rule, noise, and jump laws, reductions over neighbourhoods, and laws given as Python callables have no JAX form.

Choose it when a run must be differentiated, as in gradient-based calibration, or run on a GPU. It appears in many fields, such as fitting the rates of an epidemic by gradients and training a neural differential equation.

Attributes:

Name Type Description functions_ LoweredFunctionsSpec

The forward functions of the form of the kernels of the last run, on NumPy arrays.

traced_ TracedFunction

The pure JAX function f(t, x, p) of the form of the kernels of the last run, the drift of ordinary differential equations or the update of a discrete map.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.backends import JaxBackend
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import PopulationElement
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[PopulationElement('a', x=2.0)])

docs.text:
Return the state after one step of a pure function, traced by JAX.

A discrete map applies its update once, and ordinary differential equations are solved from t to t1 by diffrax.diffeqsolve with Tsit5, a PID step size controller, and recursive checkpointing, so gradients flow through the step.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default function TracedFunction

The pure function f(t, x, p), the update of a map or the drift of ordinary differential equations.

required t TracedArray

The time of the state.

required t1 TracedArray

The time after the step.

required x TracedArray

The state.

required p TracedArray

The parameter vector.

required form FormKind | str

The form of the function, a discrete map or ordinary differential equations.

required throw bool

Whether a solve that fails, such as one that reaches its largest number of steps, raises an error, or else returns states that are not finite, as samplers that reject such proposals need.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description state TracedArray

The state at t1.

Source code in src/skcomplex/core/engine/backends/_jax.py 
@staticmethod
def advance(
    function: TracedFunction,
    t: TracedArray,
    t1: TracedArray,
    x: TracedArray,
    p: TracedArray,
    *,
    form: FormKind | str,
    throw: bool = True,
) -> TracedArray:
    """Return the state after one step of a pure function, traced by JAX.

    A discrete map applies its update once, and ordinary differential equations are solved from `t` to `t1` by
    `diffrax.diffeqsolve` with `Tsit5`, a PID step size controller, and recursive checkpointing, so gradients flow
    through the step.

    Args:
        function:
            The pure function `f(t, x, p)`, the update of a map or the drift of ordinary differential equations.

        t:
            The time of the state.

        t1:
            The time after the step.

        x:
            The state.

        p:
            The parameter vector.

        form:
            The form of the function, a discrete map or ordinary differential equations.

        throw:
            Whether a solve that fails, such as one that reaches its largest number of steps, raises an error, or
            else returns states that are not finite, as samplers that reject such proposals need.

    Returns:
        state:
            The state at `t1`.
    """
    if form == FormKind.DISCRETE:
        return function(t, x, p)
    solution = diffrax.diffeqsolve(
        diffrax.ODETerm(function),
        diffrax.Tsit5(),
        t0=t,
        t1=t1,
        dt0=None,
        y0=x,
        args=p,
        saveat=diffrax.SaveAt(t1=True),
        stepsize_controller=diffrax.PIDController(rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10),
        adjoint=diffrax.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint(),
        max_steps=100000,
        throw=throw,
    )
    if throw:
        return solution.ys[-1]
    return jnp.where(solution.result == diffrax.RESULTS.successful, solution.ys[-1], jnp.nan)

docs.text:
Return the pure function that maps an initial state and parameters to states.

The states are those at the given times.

A discrete map is unrolled over every whole step up to the last time with jax.lax.scan, and ordinary differential equations over the intervals between the times, each solved by advance. A map that draws takes a JAX key, splits one key per step, and writes the uniform and normal values of the step after the parameters, where the draw kernel writes them in NumPy runs, so the run is a pure function of the key.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default function TracedFunction

The pure function f(t, x, p), the update of a map or the drift of ordinary differential equations.

required form FormKind | str

The form of the function, a discrete map or ordinary differential equations.

required times Array

The increasing times, at least 0, whole numbers for a map.

required throw bool

Whether a failed solve raises an error, or else gives states that are not finite.

True draws DrawKernel | None

The draw kernel of a map that draws, or None.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description run Callable[..., TracedArray]

The function run(x0, p, key=None) that returns one row of states per time, which needs a key when the map draws.

Raises:

Type Description BackendError

The draws hold draws from scipy.stats distributions or random orders, which have no JAX form, or ordinary differential equations draw.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.backends import JaxBackend
>>> from skcomplex.core.types import FormKind
>>> run = JaxBackend.unroll(lambda t, x, p: p * x, FormKind.DISCRETE, np.array([0.0, 2.0]))
>>> np.asarray(run(jnp.array([1.0]), 3.0)).ravel().tolist()
[1.0, 9.0]
Source code in src/skcomplex/core/engine/backends/_jax.py 
@staticmethod
def unroll(
    function: TracedFunction,
    form: FormKind | str,
    times: Array,
    *,
    throw: bool = True,
    draws: DrawKernel | None = None,
) -> Callable[..., TracedArray]:
    """Return the pure function that maps an initial state and parameters to states.

    The states are those at the given times.

    A discrete map is unrolled over every whole step up to the last time with `jax.lax.scan`, and ordinary
    differential equations over the intervals between the times, each solved by `advance`. A map that draws takes
    a JAX key, splits one key per step, and writes the uniform and normal values of the step after the parameters,
    where the draw kernel writes them in NumPy runs, so the run is a pure function of the key.

    Args:
        function:
            The pure function `f(t, x, p)`, the update of a map or the drift of ordinary differential equations.

        form:
            The form of the function, a discrete map or ordinary differential equations.

        times:
            The increasing times, at least 0, whole numbers for a map.

        throw:
            Whether a failed solve raises an error, or else gives states that are not finite.

        draws:
            The draw kernel of a map that draws, or `None`.

    Returns:
        run:
            The function `run(x0, p, key=None)` that returns one row of states per time, which needs a key when the
            map draws.

    Raises:
        BackendError:
            The draws hold draws from `scipy.stats` distributions or random orders, which have no JAX form, or
            ordinary differential equations draw.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.backends import JaxBackend
        >>> from skcomplex.core.types import FormKind
        >>> run = JaxBackend.unroll(lambda t, x, p: p * x, FormKind.DISCRETE, np.array([0.0, 2.0]))
        >>> np.asarray(run(jnp.array([1.0]), 3.0)).ravel().tolist()
        [1.0, 9.0]
    """
    times = np.asarray(times, dtype=float)
    if form == FormKind.DISCRETE:
        steps = np.arange(round(float(times.max()))) if times.size else np.arange(0)
        starts, ends, indices = steps.astype(float), steps + 1.0, np.rint(times).astype(int)
    else:
        ends = np.unique(times[times > 0])
        starts = np.concatenate([[0.0], ends[:-1]])
        indices = np.searchsorted(np.concatenate([[0.0], ends]), times)
    drawn = JaxBackend._get_drawn(draws, form)

    def run(x0: TracedArray, p: TracedArray, key: TracedArray | None = None) -> TracedArray:
        if drawn is not None and key is None:
            error_msg = 'The map draws at every step, so its run takes a JAX key, `run(x0, p, key)`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        keys = jax.random.split(key, starts.size) if drawn is not None else jnp.zeros(starts.size)

        def body(x: TracedArray, item: tuple[TracedArray, ...]) -> tuple[TracedArray, TracedArray]:
            t, t1, step_key = item
            q = p if drawn is None else drawn(p, step_key)
            following = JaxBackend.advance(function, t, t1, x, q, form=form, throw=throw)
            return following, following

        scanned = jax.lax.scan(body, x0, (jnp.asarray(starts), jnp.asarray(ends), keys))[1]
        states = jnp.concatenate([x0[None, :], scanned])
        return states[jnp.asarray(indices)]

    return run

docs.title: NumbaBackend(cache_dir=None, parallel=True)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseBackend

A backend that compiles fused kernels and stepper loops with Numba.

They are cached on disk. Kinds of laws that contain a plain Python callable fall back to the NumPy functions, and the problem then has no compiled stepper loops.

Choose it for large lattices, networks, and agent groups, where compiled loops run much faster than NumPy. It appears in many fields, such as long runs of spin lattices, sandpiles, and epidemics on large networks.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cache_dir str | Path | None

The directory of the generated kernel sources and Numba's cache, or None for ~/.cache/skcomplex.

None parallel bool

Whether member and pair loops over groups of at least 1000 members run in parallel threads. Kernels that the compiled loops of jump processes and discrete maps call once per event always run serially.

True

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import ExponentialGrowthInteraction, PopulationElement
>>> system = CompositeSystem(
...     elements=[GroupElement('herds', element=PopulationElement, size=2, values={'x': [1.0, 2.0]})],
...     interactions=[ExponentialGrowthInteraction('growth', target='herds', r=3.0)],
... )
>>> problem = simulate(system, until=0, backend=NumbaBackend()).problem
>>> problem.drift(0.0, problem.initial_state, problem.initial_parameters).tolist()
[3.0, 6.0]

Bases: BaseConfig[Compilation, InputT]

An abstract lowering of one family of laws.

One pass creates the lowering, later passes finish it, and the compilation keeps it. The constructor stores what the lowering reads, prepare(compilation) sets the prepared attributes the lowering gathers, and run(laws) sets lowered_, the laws lowered. A subclass implements the hooks _prepare and _run, and names the type of the laws it lowers and of the laws it runs on, which are the same for most lowerings.

A lowering that reads new symbols into laws notes their references with _add_reference, reads them back with _reference_of, and _apply_references replaces every spec it noted references for by a copy that holds them, in every field of the compilation.

The compilation the lowering serves.

The spec and the references the lowering added to it, by the identity of the spec.

lowered_ LoweredT

The laws the last run lowered, in the shape of its input.

docs.title: BaseKernel
docs.text:
Bases: BaseConfig[object, RunStateSpec]

An abstract kernel, a compiled piece of a problem that a solver evaluates.

Kernels are laws lowered to numbers, the parts of a problem that a solver runs at a state. A kernel stores in its constructor what the compiler lowered, such as compiled functions and the indices they read. prepare(problem) validates them and sets what a run needs, such as the first renewal times, and run(state) acts at a RunStateSpec, the time, the state vector, the parameters, and the random number generator, and keeps what the kernel computes, such as the next state or a matrix, in values_.

A developer adds a law kind by subclassing it, together with the pass that builds the kernel and a solver that runs it. A kernel takes any context to prepare on, since the problem that holds it is built from its kernels.

Attributes:

Name Type Description values_ object

What the last run computed. Each kernel narrows its type.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.problems import BaseKernel
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import RunStateSpec
>>> class DecayKernel(BaseKernel):
...     def __init__(self, rate=1.0):
...         self.rate = rate
...
...     def _run(self, inputs):
...         self.values_ = -self.rate * inputs.x
>>> DecayKernel(0.5).prepare().run(RunStateSpec(0.0, np.array([2.0]), np.zeros(0))).values_.tolist()
[-1.0]

def get_lattice(self, name: str) -> AnyArray:
    """Return the values of a lattice state in lattice shape.

    Args:
        name:
            The dotted name of a state of a lattice group, such as `cells.alive`.

    Returns:
        values:
            The array of the lattice shape, with the components of a vector or a tensor state on a last axis.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The name is not a state of a lattice group.
    """
    shape = self.problem.get_lattice_shape(name)
    if shape is None:
        error_msg = f'{name!r} is not a state of a lattice group.'
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    member = self.problem.states.get_entry(name).member_shape
    return np.reshape(self.get_value(name), (*shape, *member))

def get_value(self, name: str) -> npt.ArrayLike:
    """Return the value of a state or a parameter by dotted name.

    Args:
        name:
            The dotted name, such as `rabbits.n` or `growth.r`.

    Returns:
        value:
            A number for a scalar and an array for a vector.
    """
    if self.problem.states.has(name):
        return self.problem.states.read(self.state, name)
    if name in self.reporters:
        return self.reporters[name]
    if name in self.observables:
        return self.observables[name]
    return self.problem.parameters.read(self.parameters, name)

def get_lattice_shape(self, name: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    """Return the lattice shape of a state that lattice laws read or change.

    Other states return `None`.

    Args:
        name:
            The dotted name of the state.

    Returns:
        shape:
            The number of sites along every dimension.
    """
    for step in self.lattice:
        for state in step.targets:
            if state.name == name:
                return state.shape
    owner = name.rpartition('.')[0]
    for element in self.elements:
        if element.path == owner and element.lattice_shape is not None:
            return element.lattice_shape
    return None

docs.title: BaseObserver
docs.text:
Bases: BaseConfig[BaseProblemSpec, FrameSpec]

An abstract observer, which receives the frames of a simulation.

An observer follows the common API of the engine. A simulation checks it, calls prepare(problem) with the compiled problem before the first frame, run(frame) with every frame, and run(final=True) without a frame once the run stops, which releases what preparing acquired. Subclasses override any of the hooks _prepare, _run, and _release.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import BaseObserver, simulate
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import PopulationElement
>>> class CountingObserver(BaseObserver):
...     def _prepare(self, context):
...         self.count_ = 0
...
...     def _run(self, inputs):
...         self.count_ += inputs is not None
>>> observer = CountingObserver()
>>> _ = simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[PopulationElement('a')]), until=3, dt=1, observers=[observer])
>>> observer.count_
4

docs.title: ConservationObserver(*, rtol=1e-06, atol=1e-09)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseObserver

An observer that checks the conservation of every quantity at every frame.

Each quantity may change only by its flows with the environment. The total of a quantity is the sum of the states that hold it. The monitor compares its change since the first frame with the accumulated net inflow from the environment, which the compiler integrates as a hidden state, and raises an error when they differ by more than the tolerance, such as after a boundary law clips a state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rtol float

The relative tolerance, a fraction of the largest absolute total seen.

1e-06 atol float

The absolute tolerance.

1e-09

Attributes:

Name Type Description problem_

The compiled problem of the run.

transfer_network_

The quantities of the problem, with the states that hold them and their flows with the environment.

totals_

The total of every quantity at the latest frame.

initial_

The total of every quantity minus its inflow from the environment at the first frame, or None.

scale_

The largest absolute total of every quantity seen so far.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import ConservationObserver, simulate
>>> from skcomplex.systems.engineering.processes import BathtubSystem
>>> monitor = ConservationObserver()
>>> _ = simulate(BathtubSystem().prepare().system_, until=10, dt=1, observers=[monitor])
>>> round(monitor.totals_['water'], 6)
25.0

def get_agent_locations(self, group: str) -> list[AnyArray]:
    """Return the locations of the agents of a group.

    There is one array per frame with one row per agent alive.

    Args:
        group:
            The path of the agent group.

    Returns:
        locations:
            The locations at every frame, empty arrays for frames without locations.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.collective_behaviour import BoidsSystem
        >>> trajectory = simulate(BoidsSystem().prepare().system_, until=2, random_state=0)
        >>> [locations.shape[1] for locations in trajectory.get_agent_locations('flock')]
        [2, 2, 2]
    """
    frames = [self.get_agents(group, frame) for frame in range(len(self.times))]
    return [
        np.asarray(snapshot.locations) if snapshot.locations is not None else np.zeros((0, 0))
        for snapshot in frames
    ]

def get_agents(self, group: str, frame: int) -> AgentSnapshotSpec:
    """Return the agents of a group alive at a frame.

    They come with their ids, states, and locations.

    Args:
        group:
            The path of the agent group.

        frame:
            The index of the frame.

    Returns:
        agents:
            The agents of the group at that frame.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The trajectory has no agent group of that path.
    """
    groups = self.agents_by_frame[frame] if self.agents_by_frame else {}
    if group not in groups:
        error_msg = f'No agent group {group!r}. Available groups are: {", ".join(groups)}.'
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    return groups[group]

def get_lattice(self, name: str) -> AnyArray:
    """Return the values of a lattice state over time in lattice shape.

    Args:
        name:
            The dotted name of a state of a lattice group, such as `cells.alive`.

    Returns:
        values:
            One array of the lattice shape per frame, with the components of a vector or a tensor state on a last
            axis.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The name is not a state of a lattice group.
    """
    shape = self.problem.get_lattice_shape(name)
    if shape is None:
        error_msg = f'{name!r} is not a state of a lattice group.'
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    return self.get_values(name).reshape(len(self.times), *shape, *self.problem.states.get_entry(name).member_shape)

def get_member(self, index: int, problem: BaseProblemSpec) -> 'Trajectory':
    """Return the trajectory of one member of a replicated system.

    It is a trajectory of the original system.

    Args:
        index:
            The member index, the same in every group of the replicated system.

        problem:
            The compiled original system, whose single elements the replicated groups hold.

    Returns:
        trajectory:
            The times, states, and parameters of the member, laid out as the original problem lays them out.

    Examples:
        Three logistic maps run as one group, and the second member is the map that starts at 0.2.

        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.mathematics.dynamical_systems import LogisticMapElement, LogisticMapSystem
        >>> system = LogisticMapSystem().prepare().system_
        >>> group = GroupElement('map', element=LogisticMapElement, size=3, values={'x': [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]})
        >>> ensemble = CompositeSystem(elements=[group], interactions=system.interactions)
        >>> trajectory = simulate(ensemble, until=2, dt=1)
        >>> trajectory.get_member(1, simulate(system, until=0).problem).get_values('map.x').round(3).tolist()
        [0.2, 0.592, 0.894]
    """
    frames = len(self.times)
    states = np.zeros((frames, problem.states.size))
    parameters = np.zeros((frames, problem.parameters.size))
    for layout, source, target, values in (
        (problem.states, self.problem.states, states, self.states),
        (problem.parameters, self.problem.parameters, parameters, self.parameters),
    ):
        for entry in layout.entries:
            origin = source.get_entry(entry.name)
            if origin.size == entry.size:
                target[:, entry.start : entry.start + entry.size] = np.asarray(values)[
                    :,
                    origin.start : origin.start + origin.size,
                ]
                continue
            columns = np.asarray(values)[:, origin.start : origin.start + origin.size].reshape(
                frames,
                -1,
                entry.size,
            )
            target[:, entry.start : entry.start + entry.size] = columns[:, index]
    return Trajectory(problem, self.times, states, parameters)

def get_network(self, frame: int, nodes: str | None = None, layer: str | None = None) -> NetworkSnapshotSpec:
    """Return the nodes and edges of a changing network at a frame.

    The network is one whose topology changes.

    Args:
        frame:
            The index of the frame.

        nodes:
            The path of a variable group on the nodes of the network, or `None` for the first such network.

        layer:
            The layer, or `None` for the graph of the network.

    Returns:
        snapshot:
            The rows of the nodes present and the ends and rows of the edges present.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The system has no network whose topology changes.
    """
    topology = self.problem.topology
    if topology is None:
        error_msg = 'The system has no network whose topology changes. Give its groups `variable=True`.'
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    return topology.read_network(self.parameters[frame], nodes, layer)

def get_structure(self, path: str, frame: int) -> object:
    """Return the word or patch of a rewritten element at a frame.

    Args:
        path:
            The path of the rewritten element.

        frame:
            The index of the frame.

    Returns:
        structure:
            The structure recorded at that frame, which later generations do not change.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The path is not a rewritten element of the system.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.mathematics.fractals import CantorSetSystem
        >>> trajectory = simulate(CantorSetSystem(), until=4, random_state=0)
        >>> trajectory.get_structure('cantor', 2).parts
        4
    """
    structures = self.structures[frame] if self.structures else {}
    if path not in structures:
        names = ', '.join(structures) or 'none'
        error_msg = f'No rewritten element {path!r}. The rewritten elements of the system are: {names}.'
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    return structures[path]

def get_values(self, name: str) -> AnyArray:
    """Return the values of a state or a parameter over time by dotted name.

    Args:
        name:
            The dotted name, such as `rabbits.n` or `growth.r`.

    Returns:
        values:
            One value per frame for a scalar, or one row per frame for a vector, NaN in the rows of a variable
            group on a network that hold no member at a frame.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The name is neither a state nor a parameter.
    """
    if self.problem.states.has(name):
        entry = self.problem.states.get_entry(name)
        return self._get_present(name, entry.read(np.asarray(self.problem.states.read(self.states, name))))
    if self.problem.parameters.has(name):
        entry = self.problem.parameters.get_entry(name)
        values = entry.read(np.asarray(self.problem.parameters.read(self.parameters, name)))
        return self._get_present(name, values)
    if self.reporters and name in self.reporters[0]:
        found = [frame[name] for frame in self.reporters]
        if all(isinstance(item, numbers.Real) for item in found):
            return np.asarray(found, dtype=float)
        return np.fromiter(found, dtype=object, count=len(found))
    if self.observables and name in self.observables[0]:
        return np.asarray([frame[name] for frame in self.observables])
    reporter_names = list(self.reporters[0]) if self.reporters else []
    observable_names = list(self.observables[0]) if self.observables else []
    names = [*self.problem.states.names, *self.problem.parameters.names, *reporter_names, *observable_names]
    error_msg = f'No state or parameter named {name!r}. Available names are: {", ".join(names)}.'
    raise KeyError(error_msg)

docs.text:
Simulate a system until a time and return its trajectory.

A solver takes the role of a splitter in scikit-learn, a backend the role of n_jobs, observables the role of scoring, and observers, such as a Rerun recording, the role of callbacks. An argument left out comes from the tuned run settings of the system, which get_run_settings returns. A system brings a form of its own through its tuned compiler, the one hook to the compiled form. Without a solver, the tags of the system choose the default solver, or the compiled form chooses it when the tags fit several, when the system brings its own compiler, or when it nests systems that run as partitions. The tags are read before any compiling, so a solver or a backend that does not support them is rejected first.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system BaseSystem

The system to simulate.

required until float | None

The end time of the run, or None for the tuned end time of the class of the system.

None dt float | None

The time between frames, or None for the tuned time of the class of the system, or else the default of its form.

None initial_state Mapping[str, object] | None

Initial values that replace those of the elements, by dotted state name, such as {'rabbits.n': 20}, or None for the tuned initial state of the class of the system.

None solver BaseSolver | None

The solver, or None for the tuned solver of the class of the system, or else the default solver.

None backend BaseBackend | None

The backend, or None for the tuned backend of the system, or else the default backend.

None observables Sequence[ObservableSpec]

The observables to compute and record at every frame, or none for the tuned observables of the class of the system.

() observers Sequence[BaseObserver]

The observers that receive every frame, such as a RerunObserver.

() invariants Mapping[str, float] | None

The tolerance of every observable that must stay constant, by the path of the observable, or None for the tuned invariants of the system. The run raises a ConservationError that names the first observable and frame that leave the tolerance of their value at the first frame.

None schedule Mapping[str, Callable[[float], float | ArrayLike]] | None

A mapping from dotted parameter name to a function of time, such as a ramp of a control parameter, or None for the tuned schedule of the system. At every frame the parameter takes the value of its function at the frame's time. A scheduled value is checked against the domain of its parameter, as an initial value is, and a value outside it, or one that would make a transition or emission matrix negative or its rows not sum to 1, such as a transition probability of 1.5, raises an error that names the parameter and the time.

None compiler BaseCompiler | None

The compiler of the system, or None for the tuned compiler of the system, or else the compiler of the library's form the system holds, such as the rewriting form of words and patches or the operator form of quantum elements. A system package that brings a form of its own tunes a compiler it defines on BaseCompiler, the one documented hook to the compiled form.

None random_state int | Generator | None

The seed or generator of stochastic solvers.

None checked bool

Whether to check after every frame that every state lies in its domain, such as an alphabet of labels or a nonnegative count, and raise an error naming the state and the time when it does not.

False clock BaseClock | None

The clock that paces frames against wall time, or None to run as fast as possible. A RealTimeClock paces the run in real time, to watch it in a Rerun viewer as it runs.

None record_draws bool

Whether to record in the trajectory every named draw of the run by name and step, with the arguments of its distribution, and every firing of a jump law with its time and law. Draws of the laws of stochastic maps and named draws of agent rules are recorded, and the run uses the NumPy backend unless one is given.

False replay Trajectory | None

A trajectory recorded with its draws, or None. The run forces every named draw and every jump firing to its recorded value, computes the arguments of each distribution from its own parameters and states, and holds the total log-probability of the forced values as log_probability of its trajectory. Replay with the random state of the recorded run, so the draws that are not named, such as the order of agents, stay the same.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description trajectory Trajectory

The trajectory of the system from time 0 until the end time.

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The system is not a system, no end time is given or tuned, a state leaves its domain in a checked run, or a scheduled value is outside the domain of its parameter.

ParameterError

A scheduled name is not a parameter of the system, or scheduled values would break a transition or emission matrix.

TagError

The parts of the system disagree on a tag, or the solver or the backend does not support a tag of the system, named in the message.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import LogisticGrowthInteraction, PopulationElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> system = CompositeSystem(
...     elements=[PopulationElement('rabbits', x=10)],
...     interactions=[LogisticGrowthInteraction('growth', target='rabbits', r=1.0, K=100)],
... )
>>> round(simulate(system, until=20).get_values('rabbits.x')[-1])
100

def simulate(
    system: BaseSystem,
    *,
    until: float | None = None,
    dt: float | None = None,
    initial_state: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    solver: BaseSolver | None = None,
    backend: BaseBackend | None = None,
    observables: Sequence[ObservableSpec] = (),
    observers: Sequence[BaseObserver] = (),
    invariants: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    schedule: Mapping[str, Callable[[float], float | npt.ArrayLike]] | None = None,
    compiler: BaseCompiler | None = None,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = None,
    checked: bool = False,
    clock: BaseClock | None = None,
    record_draws: bool = False,
    replay: Trajectory | None = None,
) -> Trajectory:
    """Simulate a system until a time and return its trajectory.

    A solver takes the role of a splitter in scikit-learn, a backend the role of `n_jobs`, observables the role of
    `scoring`, and observers, such as a Rerun recording, the role of callbacks. An argument left out comes from the
    tuned run settings of the system, which `get_run_settings` returns. A system brings a form of its own through its
    tuned `compiler`, the one hook to the compiled form.
    Without a solver, the tags of the system choose the default solver, or the compiled form chooses it when the tags
    fit several, when the system brings its own compiler, or when it nests systems that run as partitions. The tags
    are read before any compiling, so a solver or a backend that does not support them is rejected first.

    Args:
        system:
            The system to simulate.

        until:
            The end time of the run, or `None` for the tuned end time of the class of the system.

        dt:
            The time between frames, or `None` for the tuned time of the class of the system, or else the default of
            its form.

        initial_state:
            Initial values that replace those of the elements, by dotted state name, such as `{'rabbits.n': 20}`, or
            `None` for the tuned initial state of the class of the system.

        solver:
            The solver, or `None` for the tuned solver of the class of the system, or else the default solver.

        backend:
            The backend, or `None` for the tuned backend of the system, or else the default backend.

        observables:
            The observables to compute and record at every frame, or none for the tuned observables of the class of
            the system.

        observers:
            The observers that receive every frame, such as a `RerunObserver`.

        invariants:
            The tolerance of every observable that must stay constant, by the path of the observable, or `None` for the
            tuned invariants of the system. The run raises a `ConservationError` that names the first observable and
            frame that leave the tolerance of their value at the first frame.

        schedule:
            A mapping from dotted parameter name to a function of time, such as a ramp of a control parameter, or
            `None` for the tuned schedule of the system. At every frame the parameter takes the value of its function
            at the frame's time. A scheduled value is checked against the domain of its parameter, as an initial value
            is, and a value outside it, or one that would make a transition or emission matrix negative or its rows
            not sum to 1, such as a transition probability of 1.5, raises an error that names the parameter and the
            time.

        compiler:
            The compiler of the system, or `None` for the tuned compiler of the system, or else the compiler of the
            library's form the system holds, such as the rewriting form of words and patches or the operator form of
            quantum elements. A system package that brings a form of its own tunes a compiler it defines on
            `BaseCompiler`, the one documented hook to the compiled form.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of stochastic solvers.

        checked:
            Whether to check after every frame that every state lies in its domain, such as an alphabet of labels or a
            nonnegative count, and raise an error naming the state and the time when it does not.

        clock:
            The clock that paces frames against wall time, or `None` to run as fast as possible. A `RealTimeClock`
            paces the run in real time, to watch it in a Rerun viewer as it runs.

        record_draws:
            Whether to record in the trajectory every named draw of the run by name and step, with the arguments of
            its distribution, and every firing of a jump law with its time and law. Draws of the laws of stochastic
            maps and named draws of agent rules are recorded, and the run uses the NumPy backend unless one is given.

        replay:
            A trajectory recorded with its draws, or `None`. The run forces every named draw and every jump firing to
            its recorded value, computes the arguments of each distribution from its own parameters and states, and
            holds the total log-probability of the forced values as `log_probability` of its trajectory. Replay with
            the random state of the recorded run, so the draws that are not named, such as the order of agents, stay
            the same.

    Returns:
        trajectory:
            The trajectory of the system from time 0 until the end time.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The system is not a system, no end time is given or tuned, a state leaves its domain in a checked run, or
            a scheduled value is outside the domain of its parameter.

        ParameterError:
            A scheduled name is not a parameter of the system, or scheduled values would break a transition or
            emission matrix.

        TagError:
            The parts of the system disagree on a tag, or the solver or the backend does not support a tag of the
            system, named in the message.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import LogisticGrowthInteraction, PopulationElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> system = CompositeSystem(
        ...     elements=[PopulationElement('rabbits', x=10)],
        ...     interactions=[LogisticGrowthInteraction('growth', target='rabbits', r=1.0, K=100)],
        ... )
        >>> round(simulate(system, until=20).get_values('rabbits.x')[-1])
        100
    """
    return _simulate(
        system,
        None,
        until=until,
        dt=dt,
        initial_state=initial_state,
        solver=solver,
        backend=backend,
        observables=observables,
        observers=observers,
        invariants=invariants,
        schedule=schedule,
        compiler=compiler,
        random_state=random_state,
        checked=checked,
        clock=clock,
        record_draws=record_draws,
        replay=replay,

def create(self, group: str | None = None, location: object = None, **values: object) -> 'AgentView':
    """Create an agent of a group.

    By default, it is of the agent's own group at the agent's location.

    Args:
        group:
            The path of the group, or `None` for the agent's group.

        location:
            The location of the new agent, or `None` for the agent's location.

        **values:
            The initial values of states, with the element type's defaults for the others.

    Returns:
        agent:
            The new agent.

    Raises:
        SimulationError:
            The group is not variable, so its size cannot change.
    """
    stepper = self._stepper
    target = stepper._resolve_group(group, self.group) if group is not None else self.group
    place = location if location is not None else self.location
    return MesaSolver._get_view_of(stepper._create_agent(target, place, values))

def get_displacement_to(self, other: 'AgentView | object') -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Return the vector from the agent to another agent or a location.

    On a torus, it is the shortest one.

    Args:
        other:
            An agent, or grid coordinates or a position.

    Returns:
        displacement:
            One component per axis of the space.

    Raises:
        SpaceError:
            The agents live on a network or in no space.
    """
    system = SystemView(self._stepper)
    dimensions = system.dimensions
    if dimensions is None:
        error_msg = (
            'Displacements need a grid or a continuous space, and the agents live on a network or in no space. '
            'Use `distance_to` for the number of hops on a network.'
        )
        raise SpaceError(error_msg)
    target = other.location if isinstance(other, AgentView) else other
    delta = np.asarray(target, dtype=float) - np.asarray(self.location, dtype=float)
    if not system.torus:
        return delta
    size = np.asarray(dimensions, dtype=float)
    return delta - size * np.round(delta / size)

def get_distance_to(self, other: 'AgentView | object') -> float:
    """Return the distance to another agent or a location.

    On a network, it is the number of hops.

    Args:
        other:
            An agent, or a network node, grid coordinates, or a position.

    Returns:
        distance:
            The Euclidean length of the shortest displacement, or the length of the shortest path on a network.

    Raises:
        SpaceError:
            The agents live in no space.
    """
    space = self._stepper.problem_.agent_space
    if isinstance(space, NetworkSpace):
        target = other.location if isinstance(other, AgentView) else other
        return float(nx.shortest_path_length(space.graph, self.location, target))
    return float(np.linalg.norm(self.get_displacement_to(other)))

def get_lags(self, state: str, window: int | None = None) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Return the past values of a state of an agent.

    They are the values at the ends of the last steps, the last one last. An agent remembers a state declared with
    lags, `StateSpec(lags=m)`: the agent stepper keeps its last `m` values in the companion states `<state>_lag1` to
    `<state>_lag<m>`, which rules may also read one by one. Before the first steps the lags hold their initial
    values, the `initial` of the spec or else the initial value of the state.

    Args:
        state:
            The name of a state with lags.

        window:
            The number of last values, or `None` for every kept value.

    Returns:
        values:
            The values, the oldest first.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The state of the agent keeps no lags.
    """
    spec = self._stepper._get_spec_of(self._agent)
    declaration = declarations_of(MesaSolver._get_agent_type(spec), VariableKind.STATE).get(state)
    if declaration is None or not declaration.lags:
        error_msg = (
            f'The agents of {spec.path} do not remember {state!r}. Declare the state with lags, such as '
            '`StateSpec(lags=3)`, to keep its last values.'
        )
        raise KeyError(error_msg)
    lags = declaration.lags if window is None else min(window, declaration.lags)
    return np.asarray([getattr(self, f'{state}_lag{index}') for index in range(lags, 0, -1)], dtype=float)

Return the agents around the agent.

They are the agents in the cells or nodes around it, within a radius, around it in a layer, or joined to it by an edge of the Delaunay triangulation of the positions of its group, or of group, in a continuous space. The triangulation is that of the positions when the group is first read in a step, or after agents of the group are created or removed, so the agents of a step read the same one, and in a periodic box it covers the periodic images. Agents of a variable group placed on the nodes of a network make a set of members per node that grows and shrinks during a run, such as the balls of an urn on every node, and an agent on a node reads the sets of the neighbouring nodes as the neighbours of one group.

None group str | None

None over DelaunayNeighborhood | None

The neighbouring agents.

def get_neighbors(
    self,
    radius: float | None = None,
    layer: str | None = None,
    group: str | None = None,
    over: DelaunayNeighborhood | None = None,
) -> list['AgentView']:
    """Return the agents around the agent.

    They are the agents in the cells or nodes around it, within a radius, around it in a layer, or joined to it by
    an edge of the Delaunay triangulation of the positions of its group, or of `group`, in a continuous space. The
    triangulation is that of the positions when the group is first read in a step, or after agents of the group are
    created or removed, so the agents of a step read the same one, and in a periodic box it covers the periodic
    images. Agents of a
    variable group placed on the nodes of a network make a set of members per node that grows and shrinks during a
    run, such as the balls of an urn on every node, and an agent on a node reads the sets of the neighbouring nodes
    as the neighbours of one group.

    Args:
        radius:
            The distance within which agents are neighbours in a continuous space.

        layer:
            The layer of a network space whose edges join the agent to its neighbours, or `None` for the graph of
            the network.

        group:
            The path of a group whose agents alone are returned, or `None` for every group.

        over:
            A Delaunay neighbourhood of a continuous space, or `None`.

    Returns:
        agents:
            The neighbouring agents.

    Raises:
        SpaceError:
            A Delaunay neighbourhood is read outside a continuous space.
    """
    stepper = self._stepper
    if over is not None:
        triangulated = stepper._resolve_group(group, self.group) if group is not None else self.group
        return [
            MesaSolver._get_view_of(agent)
            for agent in stepper._get_delaunay_neighbors(self._agent, triangulated, over)
        ]
    if layer is not None:
        graph = getattr(stepper.problem_.agent_space, 'graphs_', {})[layer]
        cells = stepper._get_cells()
        agents = [
            agent
            for node in graph.neighbors(self.location_key)
            for agent in cells[MesaSolver._get_cell_key(node)].agents
        ]
    elif radius is not None:
        found, _ = self._agent.get_neighbors_in_radius(radius)
        agents = [agent for agent in found if agent is not self._agent]
    else:
        agents = list(self._agent.cell.neighborhood.agents)
    path = stepper._resolve_group(group, self.group) if group is not None else None
    return [
        MesaSolver._get_view_of(agent)
        for agent in agents
        if path is None or stepper._get_spec_of(agent).path == path
    ]

def get_referenced(self, state: str) -> 'AgentView | None':
    """Return the member of another group that a reference state of the agent names.

    The state names it by its id. A state declared with `StateSpec(reference=group)` holds the id of a member of the
    group, or a negative value for none, such as the bank of a customer or the employer of a worker.

    Args:
        state:
            The name of a reference state.

    Returns:
        agent:
            The member the state names, or `None` when it names none or the member was removed.

    Raises:
        KeyError:
            The state of the agent names no member of a group.
    """
    stepper = self._stepper
    path = stepper._get_reference_of(stepper._get_spec_of(self._agent), state)
    value = float(getattr(self._agent, state))
    if value < 0 or path is None:
        return None
    agent = stepper.members_.get(int(value))
    if agent is None or getattr(agent, 'removed_', False) or stepper._get_spec_of(agent).path != path:
        return None
    return MesaSolver._get_view_of(agent)

def move_to(self, location: object) -> None:
    """Move the agent to a cell, a node, or a position.

            The cell coordinates, network node, or position, or a polygon in a continuous space.

def remove(self) -> None:
    """Remove the agent from the system.

    The agent is first checked to hold none of a conserved quantity.

    Raises:
        ConservationError:
            A state tagged with a quantity is not zero, so removing the agent would destroy it. Settle the
            holdings with transfers first.

        SimulationError:
            The agent's group is not variable, so its size cannot change.
    """
    spec = self._stepper._get_spec_of(self._agent)
    MesaSolver._check_variable(spec, 'remove')
    held = {
        name: value
        for name in self._stepper._quantities[spec.path]
        if (value := float(getattr(self._agent, name))) != 0.0
    }
    if self.alive and held:
        error_msg = (
            f'Agent {self.id} of {spec.path} is removed while holding {held}. Settle its holdings with transfers '
            'to other agents before removing it, so conserved quantities are not destroyed.'
        )
        raise ConservationError(error_msg)
    if self.alive:
        self._stepper._recount(self._agent, -1)
        self._agent.removed_ = True
        self._agent.remove()

docs.text:
Bases: BaseConfig[P, StepSpec]

An abstract solver, which advances a compiled problem in time.

A solver advances a problem of one form through time. A solver stores its settings in its constructor, among them the random state of stochastic solvers and the end time of the run it prepares for. prepare(problem) prepares it for a problem and run(step) advances the state of a StepSpec from its time to its end time and keeps the state vector there in state_. The last call run(step, final=True) releases what preparing acquired, such as an external process.

Subclasses implement the hooks _get_form, the form they solve, _get_support, what they solve, and _advance, and solvers that keep events, agents, or other state outside the state vector also implement _collect. Solvers that also solve other forms list them in _get_forms. Solvers that treat diffusion implicitly answer _is_implicit, so they do not warn about the stability limit of explicit steps. Solvers that fire renewal laws answer _is_renewing, solvers that integrate fractional noise _is_fractional, and solvers that read external inputs _reads_inputs. A solver is generic over the problem it advances, so one written for the compiler's problem reads its fields. A solver that draws random numbers whatever the laws it solves, such as a Monte Carlo simulation of particles, declares it with the class attribute draws, so its runs of a deterministic system are stochastic.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default random_state int | Generator | None

The seed or generator of stochastic solvers. A seed starts a stream spawned from np.random.SeedSequence(random_state), so the dynamics never repeat the numbers that np.random.default_rng(random_state) gives a factory or a user for initial states. A generator is used as it is.

None until float

The end time of the run the solver prepares for, infinite for a run that goes on until it is stopped, which solvers that plan or draw a whole run read.

inf

Attributes:

Name Type Description problem_ P

The problem the solver is prepared to.

rng_ Generator

The random number generator of stochastic solvers.

initial_state_ Array

The state vector of the first frame, which solvers that derive states fill in.

events_ list[BaseRecordSpec]

The events of the last run, in the order they happened.

stopped_at_ float | None

The time at which a terminal event ended the run, or None while it goes on.

snapshot_ object | None

The state the solver keeps outside the state vector, such as agents, after the last run, or None.

agents_ Mapping[str, list[object]]

The views of the agents alive after the last run, as rules receive them, by path of their agent group.

state_ Array

The state vector at the end time of the last step.

The recorder that keeps or replays the named draws and jump firings of the run, which the simulation sets after preparing the solver, or None for a run that neither records nor replays.

docs.text:
Bases: Solver

A solver that advances every partition of a co-simulation with its own solver.

Every partition is advanced to each synchronisation point. Between synchronisation points a partition holds the states of the other partitions at their last values, so a split adds an error of the order of sync_dt. A discrete partition that holds a linear program takes one step per synchronisation interval, whatever its length, so the program solves at every synchronisation point. A law of one partition that reads a reduction of the agents of another, such as count(s.farmers), reads the value the scheduler computes at every synchronisation point and holds until the next. Gauss-Seidel advances the partitions in system order, each reading the values the partitions before it already advanced. Jacobi advances every partition from the same values.

Choose it when parts of a system need different solvers, such as agents beside a field. It appears in many fields, such as cars on a road network beside their emissions, and cells beside the nutrients they eat.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default solvers Mapping[str, BaseSolver] | None

The solver of a partition by its name, with the default solver of its form for the others.

None sync_dt float | None

The time between synchronisation points, which must divide the frame duration, or None for one synchronisation per frame.

None scheme str

'gauss-seidel' or 'jacobi'.

'gauss-seidel' split bool

Whether to split a problem of one form into one partition per subsystem.

False random_state int | Generator | None

The seed or generator of stochastic solvers.

None until float

The end time of the run the solver prepares for, infinite for a run that goes on until it is stopped.

inf

Name Type Description steppers_

The stepper of every partition by partition name.

>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.common.populations import ExponentialGrowthInteraction, PopulationElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import CoSimulationSolver
>>> system = CompositeSystem(
...     systems=[
...         CompositeSystem(
...             'a',
...             elements=[PopulationElement('x', x=1)],
...             interactions=[ExponentialGrowthInteraction('g', target='x')],
...         ),
...         CompositeSystem(
...             'b',
...             elements=[PopulationElement('y', x=1)],
...             interactions=[ExponentialGrowthInteraction('g', target='y')],
...         ),
...     ],
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1, solver=CoSimulationSolver(split=True), dt=0.5)
>>> [round(float(trajectory.get_values(name)[-1]), 2) for name in ('a/x.x', 'b/y.x')]

docs.text:
Bases: OptimalControlSolver

A solver of optimal control by direct collocation.

Collocation is a transcription of the problem solved by nonlinear programming. The states and the controls at the points of a grid are the variables of a nonlinear programme. The trapezoidal scheme requires the states of neighbouring nodes to differ by the trapezoidal integral of their rates, and the Hermite-Simpson scheme adds a midpoint to every interval, with a cubic interpolation of the states and Simpson's integral. The cost is the quadrature of the running cost over the points plus the terminal cost. The controls lie within their bounds and the states of nonnegative domains stay nonnegative. SciPy's minimize solves the programme with the gradient of the cost and the Jacobian of the constraints derived symbolically. An objective to maximise is minimised with its sign changed.

Choose it when the controls of a run must minimise a cost under constraints. It appears in many fields, such as the timing of vaccination in an epidemic, the harvest of a fishery, and the trajectory of a rocket.

A solver that steps the linear part by Crank-Nicolson, the rest by Heun.

The predictor-corrector handles the remainder, and the scheme is of second order. The predictor takes a Crank-Nicolson step with the remainder at the start, and the corrector repeats it with the remainder averaged over the start and the predicted end. For linear fields it is the trapezoidal rule.

It is for spectral fields. Choose it for stiff fields with a linear part on a periodic grid. It appears in pattern formation, such as the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and Swift-Hohenberg equations.

docs.text:
Bases: CaputoSolver

A solver of fractional equations by the Adams-Bashforth-Moulton method.

It is the scheme of Diethelm, Ford, and Freed. It is of order 1 + alpha. The scheme solves the equivalent Volterra equation x(t) = x_0 + (1 / Gamma(alpha)) int_0^t (t - s)^(alpha - 1) f(s, x(s)) ds. A rectangle rule over the drifts of the whole run predicts the next state, and a trapezoidal rule with the drift at the prediction corrects it. States of order 1 take Heun steps.

Choose it for Caputo fractional equations of moderate size, which remember their whole past. It appears in models of viscoelastic materials, anomalous diffusion, and epidemics with memory.

docs.text:
Bases: Solver

A solver of stochastic equations driven by fractional and ordinary noise.

SDEs are stochastic differential equations. The stepper draws the correlated increments of every fractional noise row for the whole run when it first advances, on the grid t0 + k dt up to the horizon, and adds the stored increment of each step times the amplitude. Ordinary noise rows take independent Wiener increments. A simulation passes the end time of its run as the horizon when the stepper has none.

Choose it when the noise has long memory, set by a Hurst index. It appears in models of rough volatility in finance, river flows, and network traffic.

docs.title: GillespieSolver(*, random_state=None, until=math.inf)
docs.text:
Bases: Solver

A solver that simulates jump processes exactly by the Gillespie direct method.

An event that would fire after until is discarded, which is exact because waiting times are memoryless. A run that records its draws keeps the time and the law of every firing, and a run that replays them fires the recorded laws at the recorded times and sums the log-likelihood of the path under its own propensities.

Choose it when the units are few and each event matters. It appears in many fields, such as molecules in a cell, small outbreaks of an epidemic, and queues.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import JumpInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import GillespieSolver
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec, StepSpec
>>> class PopulationElement(Element):
...     def __init__(
...         self, label, i: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 10.0, r: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.i = i
...         self.r = r
>>> recovery = JumpInteraction('recovery', target='pop', changes={'i': -1, 'r': 1}, rate=lambda s: s.target.i)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[PopulationElement('pop')], interactions=[recovery])
>>> problem = simulate(system, until=0).problem
>>> stepper = GillespieSolver(random_state=0).prepare(problem)
>>> stepper.run(StepSpec(0.0, problem.initial_state, problem.initial_parameters, 100.0)).state_.tolist()

docs.title: GradientDescentSolver(precision='float64', *, random_state=None, until=math.inf)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSolver[LearningProblemSpec]

A solver of the learning form, which takes optimizer steps per epoch.

It trains the parameters of a nested system by gradient steps on JAX and Optax. Every unit of time is one epoch. The solver shuffles the sequences of the dataset with its random number generator, splits them into batches, and for every batch unrolls the nested system from its initial states over each sequence, writing the values of the dataset into its parameters before every inner step. A discrete map unrolls with jax.lax.scan, and ordinary differential equations with one diffrax.diffeqsolve per inner step, with Tsit5, a PID step size controller, and recursive checkpointing. The loss is the weighted mean of the loss observable over the steps and sequences, its gradient comes from jax.value_and_grad, and an Optax optimizer updates the trained parameters. Truncated backpropagation through time stops the gradient of the carried inner states every truncation steps. The optimizer reads its hyperparameters from the parameter vector before every frame, so a schedule takes effect at the next frame, and its state persists across frames until the solver is prepared again. The solver records the mean batch loss of every epoch and every metric over the whole dataset at the end of the epoch as reporters <interaction path>/loss and <interaction path>/<metric>.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default precision str

'float64' to compute in double precision, inside jax.enable_x64(True), so the unrolled runs agree with NumPy within 1e-10, or 'float32' for speed.

The seed or generator of the shuffling of the sequences.

None until float

The trained parameters after the last epoch, as a JAX array.

docs.text:
Bases: SDESolver

A solver of stochastic differential equations by a predictor and corrector.

It averages the drift over the step and keeps the Itô noise. The predictor X~ = X + f(X) h + g(X) dW gives the corrector X + (f(X) + f(X~)) h / 2 + g(X) dW, which has strong order 1 for additive noise and integrates the Itô form for any noise.

Choose it for noise in the Stratonovich convention. It appears in models of physical noise, such as Brownian particles and noisy oscillators.

docs.text:
Bases: SplitSolver

A solver of second order that steps stiff parts implicitly, the rest explicitly.

It has a trapezoidal linear part and an extrapolated remainder. Every step solves (I - h L / 2) x_{n+1} = (I + h L / 2) x_n + h (3 N_n - N_{n-1}) / 2, starting with one Crank-Nicolson step with an Euler remainder. A call that does not continue the time, state, and step of the previous call starts the scheme again.

Choose it for fields with stiff diffusion and nonlinear reactions. It appears in reaction diffusion models, such as the Gray-Scott and FitzHugh-Nagumo equations.

docs.title: KineticSolver(n=10000, dt=0.01, *, random_state=None, until=math.inf)
docs.text:
Bases: Solver

A solver that simulates encounter laws with finite particles by Monte Carlo.

The particles live on activity grids. Every density is held as counts of particles of one common mass, chosen so that the largest initial density has n particles. Every step of length at most dt applies the encounter laws in turn. A candidate particle at activity h encounters with probability 1 - exp(-lambda_h dt), where lambda_h = sum_k eta[h, k] g_k over the field density g, and picks its field activity and outcome in proportion to eta[h, k] A[h, k, i] g_k. A proliferation adds a Poisson number of particles and a destruction removes a binomial number. The state holds the empirical densities, so the trajectories match those of the gain and loss equations, which the particles approach as n grows.

Choose it when a kinetic model needs the noise of a finite population. It appears in kinetic models of wealth exchange, of opinion, and of rarefied gases.

docs.text:
Bases: ExternalSolver

A solver that runs systems of points in the LAMMPS program.

It uses LAMMPS velocity Verlet integration. An element or group whose members declare a vector position state of order 2, such as a point, becomes an atom type, whose atoms move with the first derivative of the position as their velocity. The mass of an atom type is the parameter that the divisor of the interactions on its members names, and 1 without a divisor. Boxes become LAMMPS boundaries and fix wall/reflect. A PairInteraction with a potential becomes the native pair style pairs gives for its class, or a Lepton expression potential otherwise. An interaction whose class fixes gives a native fix becomes that fix. Any other interaction that only changes the derivatives of the positions runs through fix external, evaluated by the framework.

Choose it for large systems of particles with standard potentials. It appears in molecular dynamics of liquids, solids, and polymers.

docs.text:
Bases: OperatorSolver

A solver of the Lindblad master equation with the MESolver of QuTiP.

Pure closed systems are solved with SESolver. It is the default solver of the operator form. A system without dissipators that starts in a pure state follows the linear evolution dx/dt = -i H x, which is the master equation without dissipators.

Choose it for open quantum systems small enough to hold the density matrix. It appears in quantum optics and in the decoherence of qubits.

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import local_operator

>>> QUBIT = HilbertSpec(2, operators, basis={'up': 0, 'down': 1})

Bases: ExternalSolver

A solver that runs agent-based problems in Mesa, one step per unit of time.

The agents are the members of the elements and groups whose laws include RuleLaws, and of the variable groups. Every step advances Mesa's clock by one, activates all agents in random order, or by the phases of the system's discrete time, and each agent runs the rules of its element type in declaration order. Interaction rules run once after the agents. Rules add and remove members of variable groups only. The class variable supports declares what the backend runs, which validation checks systems against: discrete time, no space or a lattice, network, or continuous space, rule, boundary, transfer, and matching laws, and elements and fixed and variable groups with any domain but Hilbert spaces. It runs a continuous space as a box of two or three sides.

Bases: SDESolver

A solver of stochastic differential equations by the Milstein scheme of Platen.

It is of strong order 1. It takes a supporting value Y = X + f h + g sqrt(h) and corrects the noise with (g(Y) - g(X)) (dW^2 - h) / (2 sqrt(h)), which needs no derivative of the noise.

docs.text:
Bases: Solver

An abstract solver that computes the optimal controls of a run.

The controls minimise or maximise an objective over the run. The solver reads the bounded adaptive parameters of the system as its controls. Its objective is the running cost objective integrated over the run plus the terminal cost terminal at the horizon, the time until of the run. Each cost is a function of the namespace s of the states, parameters, and time of the system by dotted name, such as lambda s: s.plant.x**2 + s.plant.u**2, or a number. The solver minimises the objective for the sense 'min' and maximises it for 'max'. It solves the problem over the whole run from the initial state and the initial parameters at the start of the run, and then follows the solution frame by frame. Subclasses take objective, terminal, and sense as arguments, implement _solve, and may implement _prepare.

docs.title: PontryaginSolver(objective=None, *, terminal=0.0, sense='min', nodes=201, relaxation=0.5, tolerance=1e-06, max_iterations=1000, random_state=None, until=math.inf)
docs.text:
Bases: OptimalControlSolver

A solver of optimal control by the maximum principle of Pontryagin.

Its costates and the stationarity condition are derived symbolically. The solver builds the Hamiltonian H = L + λ · f from the running cost L and the rates f of the states, and derives the costate equations λ' = -∂H/∂x with λ(T) = ∂φ/∂x at the horizon T for the terminal cost φ. The controls solve ∂H/∂u = 0, projected onto their bounds, or take the bound that minimises H where H is linear in them. A forward-backward sweep integrates the states forward and the costates backward with fourth-order Runge-Kutta steps on a grid, and relaxes the controls towards their update until they converge. The weight of the update halves whenever the distance of the controls to their update stops falling, which breaks the cycles of the sweep. An objective to maximise is minimised with its sign changed. The solution holds the costates.

Choose it for smooth control problems with few states. It appears in many fields, such as optimal treatment in medicine, optimal harvest in ecology, and optimal growth in economics.

...         label,

docs.text:
Bases: Solver

A solver by strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta of order 2 or 3.

Its steps come from the CFL condition of conservation laws. The schemes of Shu and Osher are convex combinations of Euler steps, so they keep the total variation bound of a limited finite-volume scheme. With finite-volume fields the step is the smaller of cfl * h / s, for the cell size h and the largest wave speed s, and the stability limit of the Laplacian rates at the current parameters, and otherwise dt.

Choose it for conservation laws with shocks, where it keeps the scheme free of new oscillations. It appears in models of traffic, gas dynamics, and shallow water.
