docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A neutral community of constant size with speciation and drift.

Its species arise by speciation and vanish by drift.

Every species is transient, yet the number of species settles around S_N = sum_n theta / (theta + n) for n from 0 to N - 1, with theta = (N - 1) nu / (1 - nu), and the mean number of species of k individuals around phi_k = theta / k prod_j (N - j + 1) / (N - j + theta) for j from 1 to k. The system has the group community and the number richness of species.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Organisms that divide, die, and hop between patches on a periodic lattice.

They gather in clusters.

Births balance deaths, so the mean number of organisms per patch stays n while its variance grows. Without hops it grows as 2 alpha n t, so most patches empty while a few fill. Hops at the rate beta slow the growth to t^(1/2) in one dimension and ln t in two, so the clusters persist in low dimension although the mean density obeys a diffusion equation. The system has the numbers patches.x of organisms on the lattice patches, and their mean mean and variance variance over the patches.

def regrow(self, agent: PastureView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Grow the grass by one week of logistic growth.

    Args:
        agent:
            The patch.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    del system
    agent.grass += agent.growth * agent.grass * (1 - agent.grass)

docs.title: PenaeidShrimpSystem(gut=0.5, biomass=1.0, *, ration=2.5, respiration=0.05, L_inf=29.9, K=0.013, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

The growth of one penaeid shrimp from the juvenile stage.

The growth is forced by the food and the water temperature.

The individual ingests food up to a maximum ration set by its biomass and the water temperature, assimilates its gut content, respires, and spawns, while its gonads grow and its carapace length follows von Bertalanffy's curve L(t) = L_inf (1 - exp(-K t)) from zero, which nears its asymptote after six to eight months. The gut content settles near I / A_e, the ingestion over the assimilation efficiency.

The coefficients are those of the listing of Bala et al. (2017). With them the respiration of a juvenile at 28 C, respiration exp(0.07 T) (phi B)^0.185, is about half its biomass per day, more than its maximum ration, so the total biomass declines slowly while the gonads and the length grow. The weight gain the source describes needs a lower respiration coefficient, such as 0.02. The system has the states shrimp.gut, shrimp.biomass, shrimp.gonads, and shrimp.length.

docs.title: RickerSystem(n=0.5, *, r=2.0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Ricker's map of a population in discrete generations, n' = r n exp(-n).

It is chaotic for large r.

The positive fixed point n = ln r is stable while 1 < r < e^2. Beyond e^2, about 7.39, it loses stability to a two-cycle, and further period doublings lead to chaos near r = 14.8. The size stays positive for every r. The system has the population population.x.

Bases: Interaction

docs.title: RosenzweigMacarthurSystem(prey=None, predators=None, *, kappa=0.01, eta=0.8, phi=None, phi_end=None, rate=0.002, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Fast prey and slow predators whose carrying capacity shrinks at a rate.

A fast shrinking tips them.

By default the crowding rises from eta (1 - eta) / (1 + eta) to 1 - eta, the range where the coexistence point at x = 1 / (1 - eta) is stable, and the run starts there. A slow rise lets the populations track the point, and a rise faster than about 0.0004 makes the prey collapse for a while before they return.

In a collapse the prey fall to about 1e-30, far below any absolute tolerance, and an error of either sign there decides whether they return or, below zero, run into the pole of the feeding at x = -1 / eta. The registered solver therefore controls the relative error only, with ScipyODESolver(rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-300). The system has the populations prey and predators.

docs.title: SequentiallyLinearEcosystemSystem(n=60, k=4, *, rate=0.2, threshold=0.001, seed=1, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

An ecosystem with linear dynamics between extinctions that rewrite its network.

Every species reads k random species through influences of random sign and strength, and grows linearly with their abundances. Between extinctions the dynamics is linear, so the abundances approach the dominant eigenvector of the current network. A species whose abundance falls below threshold goes extinct with its influences, and a new species with k random influences takes its place, which changes the network and starts a new linear stretch. Extinctions come in bursts separated by quiet periods. The system has the abundances species.x and ages species.age of the variable group species and the strengths influences.w of the variable group influences on the edges.

Parameters:

The number of species.

The number of species every species reads.

The growth per step per unit of influence.

0.2 threshold float

The abundance below which a species goes extinct.

0.001 seed int | None

The seed of the network and of the initial strengths.

1 label str

The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

'system'

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import SequentiallyLinearEcosystemSystem

docs.title: SizeGrowthInteraction(label, *, target, state='u', drift=None, source=None, limiter='minmod', riemann='rusanov', sources=())
docs.text:
Bases: ConservationInteraction

Size growth du/dt + divergence(a u) = source(ns) of a size density u by a growth rate.

Ecology names it the growth of individuals along a size axis, the transport term of a size-structured population. The drift field is a(ns). The flux of the conservation law is the drift times the state, written in conservative form, so the total of the state on a periodic field stays constant and, on a spectral field, the dealiasing of products applies to it. The drift is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one per dimension, of the states and parameters of the field, and may read other states than the one it carries, such as the flow of a fluid derived from a streamfunction, or the drift of a probability density in a Fokker-Planck equation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target str

The path of the field whose state is carried.

required state str

The name of the carried state of the field.

'u' drift Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the drift, or one drift per dimension.

None source Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the source, or None for none.

None limiter str | None

The slope limiter of the reconstruction of a finite-volume field, 'minmod', 'van-leer', or None.

'minmod' riemann str | None

The numerical flux of a finite-volume field, 'rusanov' or 'godunov', or None for the divergence of the flux on a field of another discretization.

'rusanov' sources Sequence[str]

The paths of other elements the drift and the source read, as the namespaces sources. A field over the position lattice of a target on a phase space is read broadcast along the class axes.

()

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the numerical flux is unknown.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, FieldElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import SizeGrowthInteraction
>>> class CellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.u = u
>>> space = LatticeSpace((50,), spacing=0.1, boundary='periodic')
>>> values = {'u': np.exp(-((np.arange(50) - 25) / 5.0) ** 2)}
>>> volumes = 'finite-volume'
>>> field = FieldElement('tracer', element=CellElement, space=space, values=values, discretization=volumes)
>>> drift = SizeGrowthInteraction('drift', target='tracer', state='u', drift=lambda s: 1.0)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[field], interactions=[drift])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1.0, dt=0.01)
>>> total = trajectory.get_values('tracer.u')[-1].sum()
>>> round(float(total), 6) == round(float(values['u'].sum()), 6)

Bases: BaseSystem

Plants, prey, and predators on a grid.

The animals share emotions through decaying marks.

Every cell holds at most one organism. Prey eat plants and fear predators, and predators eat prey and grow angry with hunger. Happiness draws animals of the same kind towards the cells where it was marked and distress drives them away, a trail stigmergy of emotions that the cellular automaton of Olsen in Carmichael and Hadžikadić (2019) uses to study cooperation within each species. The system has the groups life/plants, life/prey, and life/predators, and the marks ground/marks.

Bases: BaseSystem

Prey and predators born and killed one at a time.

The prey crowd and the predation saturates.

The deterministic limit has the coexistence point x = m / (a (e - m h)). It is stable while K < 2 x + 1 / (a h), and enriching the prey beyond that turns it into large cycles, which demographic noise drives to extinction. The system has the populations prey and predators.

docs.title: TripletInteraction(label, *, target, a=0.0, state='x')
docs.text:
Bases: RateInteraction

Interactions of every species with the pairs of other species.

They add dx_i/dt += x_i sum_(j<k) a_ijk x_j x_k.

The coefficient a_ijk is the effect of the combination of the species j and k on the growth of the species i (Sidhom and Galla 2024, Eq. 2). The tensor holds it for both orders of the pair, a_ijk = a_ikj, so the sum over the sets j < k is half the contraction of the tensor with the abundances, and it holds 0 where indices coincide.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

required a Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(shape=(target, target, target))]

The coupling tensor of order 3, with one index per species, or a number for every entry.

0.0 state str

The name of the state that holds the abundance of a species.

'x'

Examples:

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Resident population x and invading population y.

They follow equations (13.3) and (13.4) of Jensen.

The maps of IntrinsicInstabilitySystem step both sizes. At every step x ← [x - eta (x - X)] exp(-alpha y) + √x sigma chi, an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck step damped by the invader. With probability p a mutation from x adds nu x to y, and otherwise y ← y (1 + beta) + √y sigma chi'. The noises chi and chi' are independent standard normal values, scaled by the square root of the population sizes as in birth and death processes, and both sizes are cut at 0.

docs.title: ActivityDrivenEpidemicsSystem(n=500, *, m=2, exponent=2.2, least=0.01, lam=0.9, mu=0.1, infected=0.05, seed=1, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

SIS spreading on an activity-driven temporal network, whose edges last one step.

At every step every node fires with probability its activity, drawn from a^-exponent above least, and joins m random nodes. The infection travels along the edges of a step, which disappear at the next step, so it spreads only when lam / mu exceeds a threshold set by the moments of the activity, 2 <a> / (m (<a> + sqrt(<a^2>))) in the limit of small probabilities, and not by the degrees of the network aggregated over time. The system has the states hosts.i and activities hosts.a of the group hosts on the nodes, and the variable group contacts on the edges of every step.

The probability of recovery at a step.

def visit(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Move every person to the location of the half day, then infect and recover.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    people = system.get_agents(self.people, CommuterView)
    at_work = round(system.time) % 2 == 1 and not self.closed
    places = np.array([int(person.work if at_work else person.home) for person in people])
    health = np.array([person.health for person in people])
    infected = np.bincount(places[health == INFECTED], minlength=places.max() + 1)[places]
    draws = system.rng.random(len(people))
    infection = (health == SUSCEPTIBLE) & (draws < 1 - (1 - self.p) ** infected)
    recovery = (health == INFECTED) & (draws < self.gamma)
    health = np.where(infection, INFECTED, np.where(recovery, RECOVERED, health))
    for person, place, state in zip(people, places, health, strict=True):
        person.move_to(int(place))
        person.health = float(state)

docs.title: CovidTransmissionInteraction(label, *, target, contacts, temperature=0.1, hard=False)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Infection and recovery of agents by relaxed Bernoulli draws, Eq. 6 of Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023).

A susceptible agent is infected with the probability 1 - exp(-psi sum_L beta_L I_L), where I_L is the share of infected agents among the other members of its place of kind L, household, school, or company, read through a weighted sum with the weights 1 / (n_L - 1) of co-members. An infected agent recovers with the probability gamma. Both are Bernoulli draws with a temperature, which every backend but JAX draws exactly, and JAX relaxes so runs have gradients in the transmissions. The interaction declares its draws reparameterized.

Bases: BaseSystem

Two cities with recurrent outbreaks of a disease.

The disease has fixed infection and immunity periods.

With one infected step and recovery immune steps, each city follows x' = a x (1 - x - x(t-1) - ... - x(t-recovery)), which reduces to the logistic map without immunity. docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Differentiable agents of a COVID-19 epidemic, after Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023).

The model of Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023, arXiv 2305.15340), a small version of GradABM-JUNE: a seeded synthetic population of households of two adults and two children, where children go to schools and adults to companies. Agents are susceptible, infected, or recovered, and are infected and recover by the relaxed Bernoulli draws of CovidTransmissionInteraction, Eq. 6, with a transmission beta_L per kind of place. NumPy runs draw exact agents and JAX runs relax the draws, so the system holds the tag differentiable and variational calibration fits the three transmissions through its JAX run. Time runs in days. The system has the group people, the element cases with the infections of children and adults of the day before, and the observable daily_infections.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A synthetic city in the spirit of EpiSims.

People infect those they meet at home and at work.

EpiSims models a city as a bipartite graph of people and locations whose edges are visits labelled with their times, and spreads disease between people at the same location. Here every person belongs to a household of mean size household and a workplace or school of mean size workplace, the people sleep at home and work by day, and the disease spreads by SIR contacts at every location. The locations form a network whose edges join a home to the workplaces of its members, the projection of the bipartite graph onto the locations. Households spread the disease within families and workplaces between them, so closing the workplaces, one of the interventions EpiSims was built to compare, confines outbreaks to households. The system has the homes, workplaces, and health states of the agent group people on the locations.

docs.title: HeterogeneousMeanFieldSIRSystem(exponent=2.5, k_min=3, k_max=100, *, beta=0.1, mu=1.0, infected=0.0001, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The SIR epidemic on an uncorrelated network of power-law degrees.

It is in heterogeneous mean field.

The degrees run from k_min to k_max with P(k) ~ k^-exponent. An outbreak grows when beta / mu > <k> / (<k^2> - <k>), a threshold close to <k> / <k^2> on heterogeneous networks, which vanishes on scale-free networks as k_max grows. Below it the epidemic dies out after infecting a share of the order of the initial one, and above it a finite share of the population ends recovered. The hubs are infected first. The system has the densities network.s, network.i, and network.r of the degree classes from k_min to k_max, members of the group network, and the shares infected and recovered of the whole population, the last one the final epidemic size at the end of the outbreak.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Susceptible, infected, and recovered densities of the nodes of one degree.

The densities are in heterogeneous mean field.

A susceptible node of degree k is infected at rate beta k theta and an infected node recovers at rate mu, so d i_k / dt = -mu i_k + beta k s_k theta and d r_k / dt = mu i_k. On an uncorrelated network, the probability that a contact of a susceptible node is infected is theta = sum_k (k - 1) P(k) i_k / <k>, a total over the degree classes, since an infected neighbour of degree k has at most k - 1 other contacts. The classes are the members of a group, and the infections and the recoveries are interactions of the group, which HeterogeneousMeanFieldSIRSystem adds.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The SIS epidemic on partnerships that dissolve and are replaced at once.

Every person keeps k partners at any time, on a random regular network. A partnership dissolves at the rate sigma, and the person who keeps it finds a new partner at once, at random. An infectious person infects a susceptible partner at the rate beta and recovers at the rate gamma. By default the infection pressure k beta and the rate k sigma of new partners per person are held fixed at pressure and turnover, so k = 1 is serial monogamy and a larger k is concurrency at the same contact rate. Concurrency lets the infection pass on before the partnership that brought it ends, so the epidemic grows faster and reaches more people. The system has the states people.i of the variable group people on the nodes and the variable group partnerships on the edges.

Bases: Element

Population of Watts and May whose infections pass along lasting partnerships.

The population has a fixed exposed period.

Susceptible people S acquire new partners at the rate c, each infecting with the probability beta over the partnership, and are infected at the rate pi = c beta (I / A + J) with the active population A = S + E + I. The first term is the infection by a new partner who is infectious, and the memory J is the infection by a current partner who turned infectious after the partnership formed, dJ/dt = pi(t - T) S(t - T) / A - J / tau, where partnerships last a mean time tau. The exposed E turn infectious after the fixed time T, and the infectious I develop the disease, which ends their sexual activity, at the rate nu, into R. The infection starts at time zero, so the infectious and the memory are zero before it.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Person of the agent-based SIR system.

The person has incubation, mortality, waning immunity, and lockdown.

A MovementInteraction walks a living person to a neighbouring cell with probability d, or lockdown_d during the lockdown, which lasts lockdown_length steps from lockdown_start. Transitions of the agent form, which AgentBasedSIRSystem adds, move the health of the person. An infectious person infects, with probability beta, every susceptible person in its cell, who becomes exposed. An infectious person recovers with probability gamma or dies with probability mu, and a recovered person loses immunity with probability alpha. Health is 0 susceptible, 1 exposed, 2 infected, 3 recovered, or 4 dead.

The incubation follows the convention of the residence time after of TransitionInteraction: the step of the exposure counts as the first step in the exposed state, so a person exposed in step n becomes infectious at the end of step n + incubation - 1. The clock that the person kept before counted the step of the exposure only when the person acted after its infector in that step, so the onset now comes half a step earlier on average.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Yearly strains that infect every resident less resistant than their strength.

The infected residents become immune.

Every resident keeps a resistance R drawn uniformly from [0, 1]. Once a year a strain of strength eta, drawn uniformly from [0, 1), infects the residents with R < eta, whose resistance becomes 1. In a large population an outbreak happens only in a year whose strain is stronger than every earlier one, a record, so outbreaks thin out as time goes on: the mean number of outbreaks in t years is close to the harmonic number H_t, about ln t + 0.577, a Poisson process in the logarithm of time. The system has the resistances residents.R, the infections of the last year residents.infected, and the strength pathogen.eta of the strain of the coming year.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The SEIR epidemic of Watts and May.

Partnerships that last longer spread the infection faster.

A susceptible person is infected at the rate pi(t) = c beta [I / (S + E + I) + int exp(-(t - t') / tau) pi(t' - T) S(t' - T) / (S + E + I)(t') dt'], by a new partner who is infectious or by a current partner who turned infectious during the partnership. The mean number of current partners is c tau, so a longer partnership raises the mean degree of the momentary network, and the infection rate grows with tau at fixed c and beta. The system has the fractions population.S, population.E, population.I, population.R, and the infection memory population.J.

Bases: ReactionNetworkSystem

The outbreak of zombies of Munz et al.

The dead rise again and humans are eventually overrun.

Humans S are born at the rate birth and die naturally at the rate delta. A zombie Z bites a human at the rate beta S Z, and humans destroy zombies at the rate alpha S Z. docs.text:
Bases: EvolutionInteraction

One generation of a population that climbs a random fitness landscape.

The population climbs as a whole, under strong selection.

All individuals share one genome. Each mutates one random locus with probability u, to a genome of random fitness in [0, 1], with probability mutation. If a mutant is fitter, the whole population takes the fittest mutant. If every individual mutated to a less fit genome, the population escapes to the fittest of them. Otherwise it stays. docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The numbers of objects at successive assembly indices.

Each level is discovered from the level below.

The objects of assembly index a + 1 grow as dN_{a+1}/dt = k (N_a)^alpha from a constant pool of building blocks. Without selection, alpha = 1, every object built before is reused and N_a(t) = (k t)^a / a!, the exponential expansion of the assembly possible. Selection, alpha < 1, reuses only a subset, so the discovery of new objects slows down and the deeper levels fill far later. The system has the numbers levels.N of the group levels, ordered by assembly index from 1.

def climb(self, agent: ClimberView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Flip a random bit, and keep the flip when it raises the fitness.

    Args:
        agent:
            The climber.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    n, k, seed = int(agent.n), int(agent.k), int(agent.seed)
    mutant = int(agent.genome) ^ (1 << int(system.rng.integers(n)))
    fitness = ClimberElement._get_nk_fitness(mutant, n, k, seed)
    if fitness > agent.fitness:
        agent.genome = float(mutant)
        agent.fitness = fitness

Each species takes one point mutation per step.

Every gene of a species contributes to its fitness through a random table of its own state, the states of the next k genes of the species, and the states of c random genes in each of s other species. The fitness of a species is the mean contribution of its n genes. At every step the species are picked in turn, and each flips one random bit and keeps the flip when it raises its fitness against the current genomes of the others. def climb(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Let every species in turn try one point mutation, and update the fitness of all.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    species = system.get_agents(self.species, CoevolvingSpeciesView)
    genomes = [int(item.genome) for item in species]
    for index, item in enumerate(species):
        mutant = genomes[index] ^ (1 << int(system.rng.integers(self.n)))
        trial = [*genomes[:index], mutant, *genomes[index + 1 :]]
        accepted = self._get_fitness(index, trial) > self._get_fitness(index, genomes)
        if accepted:
            genomes[index] = mutant
        item.moves = float(accepted)
    for index, item in enumerate(species):
        item.genome = float(genomes[index])
        item.fitness = self._get_fitness(index, genomes)

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Population dynamics of signed catalytic interactions.

The least populated species is replaced at every step.

Between replacements the relative populations follow Eq. (5.37) of Thurner et al. (2018), dx_i/dt = f_i with f_i = sum_j M_ij x_j - x_i phi, where phi = sum_jk M_jk x_k keeps the total at one, except that a species at zero stays there while f_i < 0. The rule integrates them for the time duration by Euler steps of step, then replaces the least populated species, ties broken at random, by a new one whose links to and from every other species are drawn from [-1, 1] with the probability p, whose degradation is drawn from [-1, 0], and whose population starts at 1 / N.

docs.title: select(system)
docs.text:
Run the population dynamics, then replace the least populated species.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system SystemView

The system.

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/biology/evolution/_networks.py 
def select(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Run the population dynamics, then replace the least populated species.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    species = system.get_agents(self.species, CompetingSpeciesView)
    matrix = np.array([np.asarray(item.links, dtype=float) for item in species])
    populations = self._relax(matrix, np.array([item.x for item in species]))
    size = len(species)
    weakest = np.flatnonzero(populations <= populations.min() + 1e-12)
    k = int(system.rng.choice(weakest))
    drawn = system.rng.uniform(-1, 1, (2, size)) * (system.rng.random((2, size)) < self.p)
    matrix[k, :], matrix[:, k] = drawn[0], drawn[1]
    matrix[k, k] = -system.rng.random()
    populations[k] = 1 / size
    populations /= populations.sum()
    for index, item in enumerate(species):
        item.x = float(populations[index])
        item.links = matrix[index]

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Replicate populations whose allele frequencies diffuse by drift.

The frequencies diffuse until the allele is lost or fixed.

Each replicate follows dx = N s x (1 - x) dt + sqrt(2 x (1 - x)) dW, whose density obeys Kimura's diffusion equation dp/dt = -N s d/dx [x (1 - x) p] + d^2/dx^2 [x (1 - x) p]. Every replicate ends at loss or fixation, and an allele that starts at the frequency x fixes with the probability (1 - exp(-N s x)) / (1 - exp(-N s)), or x for a neutral allele. The system has the frequencies alleles.x of the replicates.

Bases: BaseSystem

The NKCS model of Kauffman and Johnsen.

Species climb NK landscapes coupled to each other's genes.

Every gene of a species depends on k genes of its own species and on c genes in each of s partner species. A species keeps a point mutation when it raises its fitness, which changes the landscapes of the species that depend on it, so adaptations trigger coevolutionary avalanches. docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A monomorphic population that climbs a fitness landscape.

Mutants arise and fix one at a time.

Under strong selection and weak mutation the population carries one genome of loci alleles -1 or 1, and every substitution of a mutant moves it to a neighbouring genome. The walk climbs the landscape and settles on the stationary distribution Q ~ f^(N - 1), a Boltzmann distribution of the energy -ln f at the temperature 1 / (N - 1). Random fields alone, coupling = 0, give a landscape with one peak. Couplings J_ij of variance coupling^2 / loci give the rugged landscape of a spin glass, where a small population escapes local peaks. The system has the alleles genome.s on a one-dimensional lattice of loci, starting from the genome of all -1, and the fitness fitness of the genome.

Join two polymers and add the product to the pool.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system SystemView

The system.

def join(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Join two polymers and add the product to the pool.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    pool = system.get_agents(self.polymers, PolymerView)
    partner = pool[int(system.rng.integers(len(pool)))]
    if self.mode == 'directed':
        first = max(pool, key=lambda polymer: polymer.born)
    else:
        first = pool[int(system.rng.integers(len(pool)))]
    born = max(polymer.born for polymer in pool) + 1
    system.create(self.polymers, length=first.length + partner.length, born=born)

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The replicator dynamics of a game, by default hawks and doves.

Hawks and doves settle at a share V / C of hawks.

Every strategy is a member of the group population, and it grows with its payoff above the mean payoff. The hawks and doves game has the payoff matrix ((V - C) / 2, V), (0, V / 2) with hawks first. When the cost of a fight C exceeds the value V, hawks and doves coexist with V / C hawks, and otherwise hawks take over. A payoff matrix gives any other game, such as the prisoner's dilemma or rock, paper, scissors. The system has the shares population.x of the strategies, hawks first.

Bases: BaseSystem

The ecosystem of Solé and Manrubia.

Its species go extinct when their dependencies turn against them.

Every species depends on k species through couplings drawn from [-1, 1], and its field is the sum of these couplings. The couplings drift at random. docs.text:
Bases: TransitionInteraction

Origin and fixation of mutants that flip one locus of a genome.

The genome is the one of a monomorphic population.

Every locus of each of the N individuals mutates at the rate mu, so mutants of a given locus arise at the rate N mu. A mutant from the fitness f to f' fixes with the Moran probability (1 - f / f') / (1 - (f / f')^N), so the allele s of the locus moves between -1 and 1 by transitions at the product of the two. The fitness is F0 + sum_i h_i s_i + sum_ij J_ij s_i s_j / 2, and a flip of locus i changes it by -2 s_i (h_i + sum_j J_ij s_j).

def compute_birth(self, agent: IndividualView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the probability that an organism of type `S` reproduces.

    The probability is `1 / (1 + exp(-H(S)))`.

    Args:
        agent:
            The organism.

        system:
            The system view of the life cycle.

    Returns:
        probability:
            The probability of reproduction.
    """
    composition = system.get_composition('target', 'trait')
    size = sum(composition.values())
    row = self._get_couplings(self.seed, self.length)[int(agent.trait)]
    coupling = sum(row[int(np.asarray(genome))] * count for genome, count in composition.items())
    return float(expit(system.get_parameter('k') / size * coupling - system.get_parameter('mu') * size))

def mutate_genome(self, values: dict[str, object], system: SystemViewProtocol) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the values of an offspring with mutated genome bits.

    Every genome bit flips with probability `p_mut`.

    Args:
        values:
            The values of the offspring, with the genome of its parent as `trait`.

        system:
            The system view of the life cycle.

    Returns:
        values:
            The values with the mutated genome.
    """
    genome = int(np.asarray(values['trait'], dtype=float))
    flips = np.flatnonzero(system.rng.random(self.length) < system.get_parameter('p_mut'))
    return {**values, 'trait': float(genome ^ sum(1 << int(locus) for locus in flips))}

def mutate_point(row: np.ndarray, random: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a row of indices of bases with one random site mutated.

    The base at the site is replaced by one of the other three.

    Args:
        row:
            The indices of the bases, which the function changes.

        random:
            The random generator.

    Returns:
        row:
            The row after the mutation.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.evolution import mutate_point
        >>> row = mutate_point(np.zeros(4), np.random.default_rng(0))
        >>> int((row != 0).sum())
        1
    """
    site = random.integers(row.size)
    row[site] = (row[site] + random.integers(1, len(BASES))) % len(BASES)
    return row

docs.text:
Return the neutral networks of a map from sequences to phenotypes.

It returns their robustness and evolvability instead on request.

The neighbours of a genotype are the sequences one point mutation away. Its robustness is the number of its neighbours of the same phenotype, and its evolvability the number of different phenotypes among its neighbours. The robustness of a phenotype is the mean robustness of its genotypes, and its evolvability the number of different phenotypes among the neighbours of all its genotypes. The definitions follow Wagner (2008), as Raman (2021, §13.3) states them, so the phenotype of a genotype itself counts when a neighbour has it.

>>> genotypes = [''.join(letters) for letters in itertools.product('01', repeat=4)]
>>> result = neutral_network(
...     genotypes, phenotype_of=lambda sequence: sequence[0], kind='genotype-robustness', alphabet='01'
... )
>>> set(result.values.tolist())

def neutral_network(
    source: object,
    *,
    phenotype_of: Callable[[str], Hashable],
    kind: str = 'network',
    alphabet: Sequence[str] = 'ACGU',
    state: str | None = None,
) -> NeutralNetworkResult:
    """Return the neutral networks of a map from sequences to phenotypes.

    It returns their robustness and evolvability instead on request.

    The neighbours of a genotype are the sequences one point mutation away. Its robustness is the number of its
    neighbours of the same phenotype, and its evolvability the number of different phenotypes among its neighbours. The
    robustness of a phenotype is the mean robustness of its genotypes, and its evolvability the number of different
    phenotypes among the neighbours of all its genotypes. The definitions follow Wagner (2008), as Raman (2021, §13.3)
    states them, so the phenotype of a genotype itself counts when a neighbour has it.

    Args:
        source:
            A trajectory whose lattice state holds one sequence per row, an array of strings, or an array of letters
            on its last axis.

        phenotype_of:
            The function from a sequence to a phenotype key.

        kind:
            `'network'`, `'genotype-robustness'`, `'genotype-evolvability'`, `'phenotype-robustness'`, or
            `'phenotype-evolvability'`.

        alphabet:
            The letters of the sequences.

        state:
            The dotted name of the lattice state of a trajectory that holds one sequence per row, or `None` for the
            first state.

    Returns:
        result:
            The sequences, and the networks or the values of the kind.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The kind is unknown, the mapping is not callable, or a sequence holds a letter outside the alphabet.

    Examples:
        >>> import itertools
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.evolution import neutral_network
        >>> genotypes = [''.join(letters) for letters in itertools.product('01', repeat=4)]
        >>> result = neutral_network(
        ...     genotypes, phenotype_of=lambda sequence: sequence[0], kind='genotype-robustness', alphabet='01'
        ... )
        >>> set(result.values.tolist())
        {3.0}
    """
    if kind not in KINDS:
        error_msg = f'neutral_network has kind={kind!r}. Use one of {", ".join(KINDS)}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if not callable(phenotype_of):
        error_msg = f'neutral_network reads a function from sequences, not {phenotype_of!r}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    genotypes = _read_sequences(source, state)
    foreign = {letter for sequence in genotypes.flat for letter in sequence} - set(alphabet)
    if foreign:
        error_msg = f'The sequences hold the letters {sorted(foreign)}, which the alphabet {alphabet} lacks.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if kind == 'network':
        networks = {key: _network(items, alphabet) for key, items in _by_phenotype(genotypes, phenotype_of).items()}
        return NeutralNetworkResult(genotypes, networks=networks)
    values: np.ndarray | dict[Hashable, float]
    if kind == 'genotype-robustness':
        values = np.vectorize(lambda item: _robustness(item, phenotype_of, alphabet), otypes=[float])(genotypes)
    elif kind == 'genotype-evolvability':
        values = np.vectorize(
            lambda item: float(len(_neighbouring_phenotypes(item, phenotype_of, alphabet))),
            otypes=[float],
        )(genotypes)
    elif kind == 'phenotype-robustness':
        values = {
            key: float(np.mean([_robustness(item, phenotype_of, alphabet) for item in items]))
            for key, items in _by_phenotype(genotypes, phenotype_of).items()
        }
    else:
        values = {
            key: float(
                len(set().union(*(_neighbouring_phenotypes(item, phenotype_of, alphabet) for item in items))),
            )
            for key, items in _by_phenotype(genotypes, phenotype_of).items()
        }
    return NeutralNetworkResult(genotypes, values=values)

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Phase units coupled all to all through adaptive conduction delays.

The delays adapt to the activity of the units, as myelination.

Unit i follows dtheta_i/dt = omega_i + (kappa / N) sum_j sin(theta_j(t - tau_ij) - theta_i), and every delay dtau_ij/dt = epsilon H(tau_ij) (-(tau_ij - tau0) + rho sin(theta_j - theta_i)) relaxes to its baseline tau0 and is pushed by the phase difference of its units. With the defaults, fixed delays of 3 leave the units incoherent, and the adaptation of the delays restores a partial synchrony. The system has the phases unit_<i>.theta of the units and the delays axon_<i>_<j>.tau of the axons from unit i to unit j.

Bases: DynamicalSystem

An Adaptrode synapse driven by a train of input pulses that stops after a while.

While the pulses arrive the fast weight follows each pulse, the medium weight builds up, and the slow weight builds up further. After the input stops the fast weight falls back quickly to the medium one, which keeps a trace of the activity far longer, while the slow weight retains a long-term memory. docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The Amari neural field.

Its lateral inhibition holds a stationary bump of activity.

The potential follows tau u_t = -u + integral w(x - y) H(u(y)) dy + h on a periodic line, where H is the Heaviside firing rate, h < 0 the resting level, and w(x) = A (1 - |x| / sigma) exp(-|x| / sigma) the lateral-inhibition kernel. Amari showed that a bump of width a is stationary when W(a) + h = 0, with W(a) = A a exp(-a / sigma) the integral of w from 0 to a, and stable when w(a) < 0. A localized excitation then relaxes to the wide root, a = 2.54 for the defaults. The system has the potential field.u.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The dense homogeneous associative network of Gros.

Its memories become active one after the other.

Every memory is a clique of sites joined by excitatory links of strength w, and every other pair of sites inhibits each other with strength z. Without reservoirs the network is a winners-take-all network whose cliques are stable attractors. The reservoirs of an active clique deplete slowly, and once they are low the clique loses its excitation and its hold on the other sites, so the activity hops to an associated clique that shares sites with it. The memories become transient attractors, and the network runs through a sequence of them, an associative thought process. The default is the network of seven sites and six cliques of Gros (2015, figure 10.12). The system has the activities sites.x and the reservoirs sites.phi.

Bases: Interaction

Competition of the cliques of a winners-take-all network.

The reservoirs of the sites gate the competition.

Site i grows by dx_i/dt = (1 - x_i) r_i for a positive input r_i and decays by dx_i/dt = x_i r_i for a negative one, with r_i = sum_j [f_w(phi_i) w_ij + z_ij f_z(phi_j)] x_j. The excitatory links w_ij > 0 join the sites of every clique, and every other pair inhibits with z_ij = -|z|. The reservoir functions f(phi) = f_min + (1 - f_min) (atan((phi - phi_c) / width) - atan(-phi_c / width)) / (atan((1 - phi_c) / width) - atan(-phi_c / width)) switch off the excitation of a site whose own reservoir is low and the inhibition by a site whose reservoir is low.

docs.title: DelayAdaptationInteraction(label, *, source, target, axon, kappa=0.1, epsilon=0.01, rho=1.0, width=0.05, shortest=0.1)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Phase coupling through adaptive conduction delays.

The delays adapt to the phase differences of the units they join.

The target unit reads the phase of the source unit along the axon as it was one conduction delay ago, dtheta_i/dt += kappa sin(theta_j(t - tau_ij) - theta_i). The delay relaxes to its baseline and is pushed by the phase difference, dtau_ij/dt = epsilon H(tau_ij) (-(tau_ij - tau0_ij) + rho sin(theta_j - theta_i)), where the smooth step H(tau) = (1 + tanh(tau / width)) / 2 keeps the delay nonnegative. The coupling reads the delay no shorter than shortest, which bounds the steps of the solver.

docs.title: ExcitableElement(label, visual=None, *, phase=0, p=0.1, stimulus=0.0)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

Cyclic excitable element of the Kinouchi-Copelli network.

The element is quiescent at 0, excited at 1, and refractory up to m - 1.

Transitions move its phase every step. A quiescent element is excited by the external stimulus with probability 1 - exp(-r), where r is the stimulus rate per step, or by each excited neighbour with the transmission probability p, so it stays quiescent with probability exp(-r) (1 - p)^n when n neighbours are excited. An excited or refractory element moves to the next state, and the last refractory state returns to quiescence.

The membrane has sodium, potassium, and leak currents.

Upward crossings of 0 mV are recorded as spike events. Units are mV, ms, mS/cm², and µA/cm². The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the current, gating, and crossing interactions of HodgkinHuxleySystem read its parameters.

docs.title: KinouchiCopelliSystem(graph=None, *, sigma=1.0, stimulus=0.0, n_states=5, excited=None, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The Kinouchi-Copelli network of excitable elements.

Its dynamic range peaks at the critical point.

Every element excites each quiescent neighbour with the transmission probability p = sigma / K, where K is the mean degree of the graph, so sigma is the branching ratio, the mean number of elements one excitation excites. Below sigma = 1 activity dies out without a stimulus, and above it activity sustains itself. The response, the mean firing rate against the stimulus rate, spans the most decades of stimulus at sigma = 1. The system has the states neurons.phase, one value per node. Its standard observable activity is the fraction of excited elements, the firing rate per step.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default graph Graph | None

The NetworkX graph, or None for an Erdős-Rényi graph of 1000 nodes with mean degree 10.

None sigma float

The branching ratio.

1.0 stimulus float

The rate r of the external stimulus per step, which excites a quiescent element with probability 1 - exp(-r).

0.0 n_states int

The number of states of the cycle, one quiescent, one excited, and n_states - 2 refractory.

5 excited float | None

The initial fraction of excited elements, with the others quiescent, or None for states drawn uniformly over the cycle.

None random_state int | Generator | None

The seed or generator of the default graph and of the initial states.

0 label str

The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

'system'

Examples:

>>> import networkx as nx
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.neuroscience import KinouchiCopelliSystem
>>> system = KinouchiCopelliSystem(nx.random_regular_graph(4, 20, seed=0), sigma=1.0).prepare().system_
>>> system.elements[0].values['p']
0.25

docs.title: LeakyIntegrationInteraction(label, *, target, state='x', goal=0.0, time=1.0, noise=None)
docs.text:
Bases: RateInteraction

Leaky integration of a potential or an activity towards its input over a time constant.

Neuroscience names it the leak of a membrane or of a population, as in the Wilson-Cowan and leaky integrate-and-fire models. The rate is (goal(ns) - x) / time(ns) of a state x of a target, with optional noise. With a constant goal and time and an additive noise of amplitude sigma, the state follows the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx = (goal - x) / time dt + sigma dW, whose stationary variance is sigma**2 time / 2. A goal or a time function takes the namespace of the interaction, as for RateInteraction, and a number stands for a constant. A goal that is a number applies to every component of a vector state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target str

The path of the element or group whose state relaxes.

required state str

The name of the state of the target that relaxes.

'x' goal Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float

A function of the namespace that returns the goal, or a number.

0.0 time Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float

A function of the namespace that returns the relaxation time, or a positive number.

1.0 noise Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None

A function of the namespace that returns the amplitude of the noise, a number, or None for no noise.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The state is not a name, or a function is neither callable nor a number.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.elements import NonnegativeElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.neuroscience import LeakyIntegrationInteraction
>>> relaxation = LeakyIntegrationInteraction('relaxation', target='stock', goal=10.0, time=0.5)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[NonnegativeElement('stock')], interactions=[relaxation])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=5.0, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('stock.x')[-1]), 3)
10.0

docs.title: LegionSystem(stimulus=LEGION_OBJECTS, *, epsilon=0.1, W=6.0, W_z=1.5, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A LEGION network, a lattice of relaxation oscillators.

The network segments a stimulus into its objects.

Stimulated oscillators excite their stimulated neighbours, so each connected object synchronizes, and a global inhibitor lets only one object be active at a time, so different objects take turns. The inhibitor is driven by the largest activity of the oscillators, so one active oscillator drives it fully. Unstimulated sites have a negative input and stay silent.

The default epsilon = 0.1 gives a cycle of about 60 time units, so with the default stimulus the second object first fires near t = 51 and the first near t = 70. The value 0.02 of Terman and Wang makes the slow phases five times longer, and then no object starts an active phase before t = 220. The system has the fast variables oscillators.x, the slow variables oscillators.y, and the inhibitor inhibitor.z.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default stimulus Sequence[Sequence[float]]

The lattice of 1 for stimulated and 0 for unstimulated sites, by rows. The default holds two objects.

The time scale of the slow variables.

0.1 W float

The total excitatory weight into a stimulated site, shared among its stimulated neighbours.

6.0 W_z float

The strength of the global inhibition.

1.5 random_state int | Generator | None

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Population of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons in an exact mean field.

The mean field is the one of Montbrió, Pazó, and Roxin.

The excitabilities of the neurons follow a Lorentzian distribution of median H and half-width delta, so the firing rate r and the mean membrane potential v of the population follow dr/dt = delta / (tau^2 pi) + 2 r v / tau and dv/dt = (v^2 + H) / tau - tau (pi r)^2 exactly, with the membrane time constant tau. The synaptic field s filters the rate with exponential synapses, ds/dt = (r - s) / tau_d. Couplings and inputs add to the rate of v.

Bases: BaseSystem

The exact neural mass of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons.

Its gamma rhythm nests in a theta drive.

In the 'ping' setup an excitatory and an inhibitory population, with membrane time constants of 20 and 10 ms, couple through instantaneous synapses, and the theta current drives the excitatory one. In the 'ing' setup a single inhibitory population inhibits itself through exponential synapses of 10 ms, and the current drives it. Without forcing the populations rest or oscillate collectively in the gamma band, about 45 Hz for H_e = 10, as their excitabilities cross a Hopf bifurcation. A slow theta current sweeps them across it, so gamma bursts appear at every theta peak, theta-nested gamma oscillations. The defaults are those of Segneri et al. (2020, figure 3). The system has the rates excitatory.r and inhibitory.r, in spikes per millisecond, and the potentials excitatory.v and inhibitory.v, or the inhibitory population alone in 'ing'.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Rate neuron that adapts its gain and threshold.

The adaptation makes its firing rate exponentially distributed.

The membrane potential x integrates the input I0 + A sin(omega t) with rate Gamma, and the neuron fires at rate y = 1 / (1 + exp(a (b - x))). Stochastic gradient descent on the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the distribution of y and an exponential of mean mu gives a' = eps_a (1/a + (x - b) d) and b' = -eps_b a d with d = 1 - (2 + 1/mu) y + y²/mu. The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the relaxation and plasticity interactions of PolyhomeostaticNeuronSystem read its parameters.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Theta neurons on a random directed network with plastic synapses.

The synapses learn by spike-timing-dependent plasticity.

The neurons fire periodically with excitabilities spread around eta, and every synapse is potentiated when its presynaptic neuron fires shortly before its postsynaptic neuron and depressed when it fires shortly after. Spikes of neurons that fire at different rates fall at all delays, so the mean change of the efficacies follows the integral of the window, (A_plus - A_minus) tau: a window dominated by depression weakens the synapses and one dominated by potentiation strengthens them, while the spread of the efficacies grows. The system has the phases neurons.theta, the traces neurons.a and neurons.b, and the efficacies synapses.kappa on the edges.

docs.title: SpikeTimingPlasticityInteraction(label, *, neurons, synapses, k=1.0, epsilon=0.01, A_plus=1.0, A_minus=1.05, kappa_max=1.0)
docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Pulse coupling along plastic synapses.

The efficacy of a synapse follows the timing of the spikes at both ends.

The presynaptic neuron at the source of an edge drives the postsynaptic neuron at its target with the current (1 + cos theta_post) kappa P(theta_pre) / k, where k is the mean in-degree. The efficacy grows when the postsynaptic neuron fires after the presynaptic one and shrinks when it fires before, dkappa/dt = epsilon (A_plus a_pre P(theta_post) - A_minus b_post P(theta_pre)), the window W(dt) = A_plus exp(-dt / tau_plus) for dt > 0 and -A_minus exp(dt / tau_minus) for dt < 0 applied to every pair of spikes through the traces. Soft bounds scale potentiation by kappa_max - kappa and depression by kappa, so the efficacy stays between 0 and kappa_max.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Relaxation oscillator of Terman and Wang.

It is the dynamics of one site of a LEGION lattice.

The fast variable follows x' = 3x - x³ + 2 - y + I and the slow one y' = epsilon (gamma (1 + tanh(x / beta)) - y). A positive input I makes the oscillator oscillate and a negative one makes it excitable. The parameters m, W, theta_x, and kappa belong to the coupling of a lattice of oscillators, a CouplingInteraction that adds W m (sum_k m_k H(x_k - theta_x)) over the four nearest sites, where H is a smooth step of width kappa and m marks the stimulated sites, so only stimulated neighbours excite each other.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Theta neuron of Ermentrout and Kopell, a spiking phase.

The phase follows theta' = (1 - cos theta) + (1 + cos theta) eta.

The neuron fires when its phase passes π. With eta > 0 it fires periodically with period π / sqrt(eta), and with eta < 0 it is excitable. The change of variable V = tan(theta / 2) turns it into the quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron V' = V² + eta.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A network of theta neurons coupled all to all.

Theta neurons are equivalently quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons.

Neuron i follows theta_i' = (1 - cos theta_i) + (1 + cos theta_i)(eta_i + kappa I), where I is the mean pulse a_n (1 - cos theta_j)^n of all neurons at the current state. The excitabilities are evenly spaced quantiles of a Lorentzian distribution of center eta and half-width delta, the distribution for which Ott and Antonsen's ansatz reduces the network exactly to one complex equation. Strong excitatory coupling switches the network from a quiet state to collective firing. The system has the phases neurons.theta as its only state.

docs.text:
Bases: ThetaNeuronElement

Theta neuron that keeps traces of its own spikes.

Spike-timing-dependent plasticity reads the traces.

A spike is the smooth pulse P(theta) = (1 - cos theta)^2 * 2 / 3, of unit mean over the phase, which peaks as the phase passes π. The presynaptic trace a and the postsynaptic trace b rise with every pulse and decay with the times tau_plus and tau_minus, da/dt = P(theta) - a / tau_plus and db/dt = P(theta) - b / tau_minus, so they hold the recent spikes weighted by the exponential windows of the plasticity.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A winner-take-all network of units.

The units have self-limited growth and mutual inhibition.

Unit i follows tau x_i' = x_i (I_i - x_i - beta sum_{j != i} x_j), the competitive network of Fukai and Tanaka. One inhibition interaction binds every unit as an element set and reads the total activity of the set, so the network holds one interaction whatever the number of units. When the inhibition beta exceeds 1, only the unit with the largest input stays active, at activity I_max. When it is below 1, several winners share the activity. The winners-take-all network of Gros (2015, section 10.4), with reservoir variables and clique encoding, is a different model. The system has the activities unit_<i>.x.

docs.text:
Oncology systems.

They cover tumour growth, the vessels that feed it, and the therapies that treat it.

Bases: Element

Normal epithelium and prostate cancer cells with tissue and serum PSA.

The cells are driven by activated androgen receptors.

The normal cells follow dN/dt = r1 N (1 - (N + c1 (AD + AI)) / b1) - d1 N, the dependent cells dAD/dt = r2 AD (1 - m1)(1 - L) - d2 AD, and the independent cells dAI/dt = r3 AI (1 - (c1 N + AD + AI) / b3) - d3 AI + m1 r2 AD (1 - L), where L = (c1 N + AD + AI) / b2. The rates are r_i = psi1_i UD^2 / (psi2^2 + UD^2) + phi1_i UT^2 / (phi2^2 + UT^2) and d_i = psi3_i / (psi4 + UD + UT) for the receptors activated by DHT, UD, and by testosterone, UT. The tissue PSA follows dUIP/dt = -du1 UIP Nf - gamma_p UIP (AD + AI)^2 / (KP + AD + AI) - du2 UIP + r4, with the production r4 = sum_i beta_i (UT + UD + sigma) X_i over the cell types, and the serum PSA gains the leaks and is cleared at du3. The capacity of the normal cells b1 and their share Nf = N / b1 follow the prostate volume v1 a^phi / (v2^phi + a^phi) + v3 at the age a, divided by the volume Vc of a billion cells.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of ProstateAndrogenReceptorSystem read its parameters.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Androgen-dependent and androgen-independent prostate cancer cells.

The cells are under continuous androgen suppression.

The dependent cells follow dAD/dt = r1 U (1 - b (AD + c1 AI)) AD - (d1 + m1)(1 - U / U0) AD, the independent cells dAI/dt = r2 (1 - b (AI + c2 AD)) AI + m1 (1 - U / U0) AD, and the serum androgen du/dt = -du (U - U0) - U0 du a, which the drug efficacy a lowers to U0 (1 - a).

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of ContinuousAndrogenSuppressionSystem read its parameters.

docs.title: AngiogenesisImmunotherapySystem(A=5000.0, Vb=625.0, E=0.1, *, dose_an=15.0, dose_im=20.0, a2=1.35, a3=0.1, period=21.0, doses=6, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The Hahnfeldt tumour with effector cells under bevacizumab and atezolizumab.

The drugs are given every three weeks.

Each drug alone holds the tumour or slows it, and together they shrink it. The drug amounts follow the two-compartment system whose bolus solution is the book's closed form, with the elimination rate k10 = alpha beta / k21. The effector cells grow as r1 (A - c1 A^2) E, so 1 / c1 is the volume above which the tumour suppresses them. The drug effects in the vasculature and effector balances are the saturating effects of the book's pharmacodynamics. The resistance capacity delta_r = 0.01 and its threshold u_theta = 5 mg per kg are a choice, since the book gives none. The toxicity of each drug is exp(c / tox) - 1, linear for a low amount and exponential for a high one, and the observable toxicity is the mean of both. Volumes are in mm³, drug amounts in mg per kg, and time is in days. The system has the tumour tumour.A, the capacity tumour.Vb, the effector cells tumour.E, the drug amounts tumour.c_an and tumour.c_im, and the observable toxicity.

Bases: Element

Tumour, vasculature, and effector cells under bevacizumab and atezolizumab.

The tumour develops resistance.

The tumour A grows by the Hahnfeldt law toward its vascular capacity Vb and effector cells E kill it. The capacity is stimulated and inhibited by the tumour and destroyed by the antiangiogenic effect UAn, and the immunotherapy effect UIm boosts the effector cells. Each drug follows a two-compartment system with central amount c and peripheral amount q, in mg per kg, infused for width days every period days. Its effect is c^g / ((f U50)^g + c^g), where f = 1 + delta_r R and R integrates max(0, u_theta - c), so the drug loses potency while its concentration stays low. Volumes are in mm³, and time is in days.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of AngiogenesisImmunotherapySystem read its parameters.

Bases: Element

Tumour volume, its vascular volume, and an angiogenesis inhibitor.

The vascular volume sets the carrying capacity of the tumour.

The tumour follows dA/dt = -lambda1 A log(A / Vb), the vasculature dVb/dt = -lambda2 Vb + xi_s A - xi_i Vb A^(2/3) - a Vb U, and the inhibitor dU/dt = -du U + u(t), where the infusion u is dose for width time units every period, from start on. A width equal to the period is a continuous infusion.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Activated T cells, a tumour, and an anti-PD-1 drug.

The drug frees the T cells from checkpoint inhibition.

The PD-1-PD-L1 complex inhibits the activation and proliferation of T cells, and the drug lowers the free PD-1 on T cells. The cytokines are at their steady states, as in the book. The book gives neither the naive T cells ENC nor the association ratio sigma, which are set so that the T cells settle below the level that controls the tumour. The ranged parameters take the low ends of the book's ranges, and the drug is the book's continuous infusion of 10^-10 per day. A larger infusion frees more T cells and lowers the tumour. The book's free PD-1 (rho_r - du1 UAP) E turns negative once the drug exceeds rho_r / du1, and it is held at 0 there. With all PD-1 blocked nothing limits the T cells, which grow without bound and clear the tumour. Cells and the drug are in g/cm³ and time in days. The system has the T cells site.E, the tumour site.A, and the drug site.UAP.

Normal and malignant cells in the bone marrow and blood, and cancer stem cells.

The blood is the peripheral blood.

Normal marrow cells renew as r1 NBM log((b1 + b2) / (theta1 + NBM)), mutate into blasts at the rate m1 and into cancer stem cells at the rate m3, and move to the blood, where they arrive after the maturation time tau1 with the survival exp(-alpha1 tau1 - r2 APB(t - tau1)). docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The bone marrow and blood system of leukaemia.

In it, blasts crowd out the normal cells.

Normal marrow cells renew, mutate into blasts and cancer stem cells, and mature into blood cells after the delay tau1. Blasts grow in the marrow, move to the blood, and inhibit the normal cells, and cancer stem cells convert into blasts after the delay tau2. Cells are counts, time is in hours, and the history before the start is the initial state. The book's table gives ranges, and the defaults are values in them: the largest growth rate of normal marrow cells and carrying capacity of blasts, the smallest delays, and the release rate m2 that keeps the normal blood cells near their initial number. The book prints the arrival of marrow cells in the blood with a minus sign, and the system uses the plus sign of the release it balances. The blasts take over the marrow and the normal blood cells fall by orders of magnitude. The system has the normal marrow and blood cells patient.NBM and patient.NPB, the blasts patient.ABM and patient.APB, and the cancer stem cells patient.AS.

Parameters:

The mutation rate of normal marrow cells into blasts, per hour.

0.0013 m3 float

The mutation rate of normal marrow cells into cancer stem cells, per hour.

The maturation time of normal cells, in hours.

docs.title: CellCycleChemotherapySystem(*, dormant=False, u1=0.0, u2=0.0, v=0.0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Tumour cells in cell-cycle compartments under chemotherapy agents.

The agents kill, block, and recruit.

Without a dormant phase the cells cycle through G0 and G1, S, and G2 and M, a killing agent kills a fraction u1 of the dividing cells, and a blocking agent slows the transit through S by u2. With a dormant phase the cells rest in G0, cycle through G1 and S and through G2 and M, the killing agent kills u1 of the dividing cells, and a recruiting agent speeds the exit from G0 by the factor 1 + v. Each division gives 2 (1 - u1) cells, so the tumour grows for u1 < 1/2 and shrinks for u1 > 1/2, whatever the blocking and the recruitment. The parameters and initial cells are those of Tables 3.8 and 3.9 of Padmanabhan et al., in cell counts and per unit time. The book prints the agents as additive terms 2 l3 u1 and garbles the indices of the dormant system, so the system takes the form of Świerniak et al., where the agents act on the cells of the compartment they leave. Constant agents are given, untreated by default. The system has the cells tumour.A1 to tumour.A3, or tumour.A0 to tumour.A2 with a dormant phase.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dormant bool

Whether the cells have a dormant phase, the system of Table 3.9, or not, the system of Table 3.8.

The fraction of dividing cells the killing agent kills.

0.0 u2 float

0.0 v float

The relative increase of the exit from G0 the recruiting agent causes, with a dormant phase.

0.0 label str

The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

docs.title: CellCycleInvasionInteraction(label, *, target, offsets)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Cell cycle, divisions, and moves of the cells on the sites of a triangular lattice.

A cell in G1 enters early S at the rate Rr while a neighbouring site is vacant, a cell in early S enters S/G2/M at the rate Ry, and a cell in S/G2/M divides at the rate Rg into two cells in G1, the daughter on a neighbouring site chosen at random, which aborts when that site is occupied. A cell of each phase moves to a neighbouring site chosen at random at the rates Mr, My, and Mg, which aborts when it is occupied. Every site reads its six neighbours at member offsets along the group order, the steps of a triangular lattice in axial coordinates.

Bases: BaseSystem

Cell invasion with the fluorescent cell cycle, after Carr et al. (2021).

Melanoma cells on a triangular lattice pass through G1, early S, and S/G2/M, divide into two cells in G1 next to a vacancy, and move to vacant neighbouring sites, run by the Gillespie algorithm, as Wang et al. (2024, arXiv 2409.19675, section 2.1.2) use it. A cell leaves G1 only while a neighbouring site is vacant, so a full lattice keeps its cells in G1. The lattice is a rhombus of height rows of width sites in axial coordinates, filled at a density, with a vacant scratch of the columns between two fractions of the width. The system has the group cells of sites and the observables g1_cells, es_cells, and sg2m_cells, the number of cells in every phase, the summaries that ABC-SMC compares.

Bases: Element

Prostate cancer cells that follow their androgen cell quota.

The growth and the mutation of the cells follow the quota, and the cells release PSA.

The cells grow at the Droop rate rm (1 - q_i / Q_i), die at d_i, and switch from dependent to independent at mx1 m501^n / (Q1^n + m501^n) and back at mx2 Q2^n / (Q2^n + m502^n). The quotas follow dQ_i/dt = vm (qm - Q_i) / (qm - q_i) U / (U + v50) - rm (Q_i - q_i) - d3 Q_i, and the serum PSA dP/dt = r0 (AD + AI) + r1 AD Q1^theta / (Q1^theta + rho1^theta) + r2 AI Q2^theta / (Q2^theta + rho2^theta) - du P. The serum androgen relaxes at the rate du1 to Umin during the width days of therapy that open every period days and to U0 otherwise.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of ProstateCellQuotaSystem read its parameters.

Bases: Element

Activated T cells, tumour cells, and an anti-PD-1 drug.

The drug frees T cells from PD-1-PD-L1 inhibition.

The T cells follow dE/dt = (r1 ENC C1 / (C1_50 + C1) + r2 E C2 / (C2_50 + C2)) / (1 + UPP / psi_pp) - d1 E, with the cytokines at their steady states C1 = C1_ss and C2 = C2_ss, the tumour dA/dt = r3 A (1 - b A) - a_rho A E, and the drug dUAP/dt = u_ap - a_rl UFP1 UAP - du2 UAP. Free PD-1 is UFP1 = max(rho_r - du1 UAP, 0) E, free PD-L1 UFL1 = sigma_l (E + c_l A), and the complex UPP = sigma UFP1 UFL1.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of AntiPD1CheckpointSystem read its parameters.

Bases: BaseSystem

A tumour with NK cells, CD8 T cells, and lymphocytes under therapy.

The therapy is chemotherapy, IL-2, and TIL injection.

The tumour, implanted in a mouse, grows toward a high equilibrium that the immune cells cannot hold back. The doses of chemotherapy shrink it, and the injected tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes clear what the drug leaves. The parameters are the table of the book, except the decay rates of the drugs, which the book's table swaps. Cells are counted, and time is in days. The system has the states tumour.A, tumour.N, tumour.E, tumour.C, tumour.I, and tumour.M.

Tumour with NK cells, CD8 T cells, and circulating lymphocytes under therapy.

The therapy is chemotherapy, IL-2, and TIL injection.

The tumour A grows logistically and NK cells N and CD8 T cells E kill it. CD8 T cells kill at the rate D = a1 (E / A)^l / (g1 + (E / A)^l). The circulating lymphocytes C feed the NK cells. Bases: BaseSystem

Uninfected and infected tumour cells, an oncolytic virus, and a drug.

The drug is chemotherapeutic.

The virus infects the growing tumour, and the drug kills both uninfected and infected cells. Over the default run of 64 days, before the virus bursts through the tumour, the combination leaves the smallest tumour. Later the virus alone clears the tumour slightly faster, because the drug also kills the infected cells that make the virus. The infusion rate is a choice, since the book gives none. One unit of cells is a million cells, and one unit of time is two days. The system has the cells tumour.AU and tumour.AV, the virus tumour.V, and the drug tumour.U.

Bases: BaseSystem

Two competing tumour clones under a drug and a vaccine.

One clone is sensitive and the other resistant to chemotherapy.

The chemotherapy kills the sensitive first clone ten times faster than the resistant second clone. Alone, it removes the sensitive clone and frees the resistant clone from competition, so the tumour relapses resistant. With the dendritic-cell vaccine, the recruited immune cells clear both clones. The book does not system the drugs, so their effects are constant rates, and their values are a choice. The competition rates take a value in the book's range of 0.01 to 1. Cells are counted, and time is in days. The system has the clones tumour.A1 and tumour.A2 and the immune cells tumour.E.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Prostate cancer under continuous androgen suppression.

Androgen-independent cells survive the suppression.

The suppression lowers the serum androgen from U0 to U0 (1 - a) at the rate du. The androgen-dependent cells grow in proportion to the androgen and die and turn independent in proportion to the deprivation 1 - U / U0, so they decline once the suppression is deep enough, while the independent cells grow regardless and cause the relapse. Cells are counted, androgen is in ng/mL, and time is in days. The book's efficacy lies between 0.6 and 0.9, and only the upper end makes the dependent cells decline. The system has the cells tumour.AD and tumour.AI and the androgen tumour.U.

docs.title: DePillisRadunskayaSystem(E=0.15, A=0.25, N=1.0, *, u=0.0, s=0.33, r1=1.5, a2=0.3, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The de Pillis-Radunskaya system of immune, tumour, and normal cells.

The cells are under a constant drug infusion.

The cells are normalised so that the carrying capacity of normal cells is 1, and time is in days. Untreated, a tumour that starts at 0.25 escapes the immune cells and settles at the high equilibrium where it outnumbers the normal cells. A constant infusion u = 1 clears it, while the normal cells stay above 0.7. The parameters are those of Table 3.3 of Padmanabhan et al. The book's initial tumour of 1e-5 lies in the basin of the tumour-free equilibrium, which is stable since r1 < c2 s / d1 + c3, so the defaults are the initial conditions of de Pillis and Radunskaya 2003, E = 0.15, A = 0.25, N = 1. The book prints no infusion schedule, so the infusion is a constant rate u per day, untreated by default. The system has the cells patient.E, patient.A, patient.N and the drug patient.U.

docs.title: DelayedDCVaccineSystem(*, dose=1000000.0, period=7.0, width=1.0, start=0.0, doses=4, tau1=1.26, tau2=0.45, tau3=0.47, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A tumour and eight innate and adaptive immune populations under a vaccine.

The populations divide with delays.

Natural killer cells divide in tau1, CD8+ cells mature after seven divisions 7 tau2, and naive helper cells become type 1 helper cells after two divisions 2 tau3. Regulatory T cells, driven by the tumour and IL-2, inhibit natural killer, CD8+, and helper cells. The book's growth term m1 ED E of mature CD8+ cells has no saturation and makes them diverge within a day, so it saturates in the dendritic cells as m1 ED E / (g3 + ED), like every other term the dendritic cells drive. The book gives no schedule, and the vaccine is a one-day injection of dose dendritic cells per day every week, 4 times. The parameters and initial state are the book's, and with them the regulatory T cells hold the adaptive response down, so the tumour grows toward its capacity b. Cells are counts, IL-2 is in IU/L, and time in days. The system has the tumour site.A, the natural killer cells site.ENK, the naive and mature CD8+ cells site.ENC and site.E, the dendritic cells site.ED, the IL-2 site.C, the regulatory cells site.ER, and the naive and type 1 helper cells site.ENH and site.E1H.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Normal and tumour cells at a primary and a secondary site.

The migration of tumour cells is delayed.

Untreated, the faster tumour cells outcompete the normal cells at the primary site, and the cells that migrate seed a tumour that does the same at the secondary site. The parameters are those of Table 3.7 of Padmanabhan et al., with time in days, and the initial cells are at the upper ends of the book's ranges with the secondary site free of tumour. The book prints the kill at the secondary site with the infusion us in place of the concentration Us, so the system uses Us as at the primary site. The infusions are constant rates, untreated by default, within the book's range of 0 to 650. Bases: BaseSystem

Helper and cytotoxic T cells, a tumour, dendritic cells, and IL-2.

They are under a dendritic-cell vaccine.

Vaccinated dendritic cells drive the proliferation of helper cells, which secrete IL-2, and IL-2 with the antigen drives the proliferation of cytotoxic cells, which kill the tumour. The book gives no initial state or schedule. The T cells start at their resting level s / d = 0.02, the dendritic cells and IL-2 at 0, and the vaccine is a one-hour injection of dose per hour every week, 8 times. Without vaccine the tumour settles at 1 - c1 s2 / (d2 r3) = 0.9. The populations are in cells per mm³ scaled by the carrying capacity, IL-2 in pg/mm³, and time in hours. The system has the helper cells site.EH, the cytotoxic cells site.E, the tumour site.A, the dendritic cells site.ED, and the IL-2 site.C.

docs.title: DormantCellCycleElement(label, visual=None, *, A0=6.5, A1=0.2, A2=0.1, l0=0.05, l1=0.5, l2=1.0, b0=0.9, b1=0.1, u=0.0, v=0.0)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

Tumour cells in a dormant phase and two cycling phases.

The cells are under a killing and a recruiting agent.

The compartments hold the dormant cells in G0 A0, the cells in G1 and S A1, and the cells in G2 and M A2. A fraction b0 of the daughters enters G0 and b1 enters G1, so dA0/dt = -l0 (1 + v) A0 + 2 b0 (1 - u) l2 A2, dA1/dt = l0 (1 + v) A0 - l1 A1 + 2 b1 (1 - u) l2 A2, and dA2/dt = l1 A1 - l2 A2. The killing agent kills the fraction u of the cells that divide, and the recruiting agent speeds the exit from G0 by the factor 1 + v.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of CellCycleChemotherapySystem read its parameters.

docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

Sensitive cells and cells resistant by mutation or by a phenotype switch.

The switch is reversible, and the cells are under a dose.

The drug kills the sensitive cells, so the resistant cells, which grow slower, take the tumour over. Resistance is acquired spontaneously at the rates m1 and m2 and induced by the drug at the rates alpha_m and alpha_p per unit of dose, and switched cells return to sensitivity at the rate m5. Time and the cells are dimensionless, the carrying capacity being 1. The book gives values only for the two-population system of Greene, Sanchez-Tapia, and Sontag, its Table 3.5, which is this system without switched cells. The defaults are that system, with the induced rate alpha_m = 0.01 of the table and an effective dose of 1, so switching is off until m2, alpha_p, or m5 is set. The system has the cells tumour.S, tumour.Rm, and tumour.Rp.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Gompertz growth under a carrying capacity that keeps rising.

The vessels on the tumour surface keep raising the capacity.

The tumour follows dn/dt = r n log(K / n) and the capacity dK/dt = d n^(2/3), so the tumour first fills its initial capacity and then grows as fast as its vasculature, roughly as t^3. The defaults are the fit to breast cancer volumes in mm³ and days. The system has the volume tumour.x and the capacity vessels.K.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Quiescent, proliferating, and mature red cells and their mean volume.

The cells are under a constant 6-mercaptopurine level.

The drug sets the death rate of proliferating cells a1 = a0 U and the cell-cycle time tau = (g1 U + MCV0) tau_h / MCV_h. Quiescent cells enter the cycle at the rate m(Q) = m0 Q50^n / (Q50^n + Q^n), of which the fraction exp(-a1 tau) survives to give two daughters, and leave to mature at the rate r1, so dQ/dt = -r1 Q + (2 exp(-a1 tau) - 1) m(Q) Q. The proliferating cells follow dP/dt = -a1 P + (1 - exp(-a1 tau)) m(Q) Q, the mature cells, which live lifespan days, dL/dt = r1 Q - d1 L(t - lifespan), and their mean corpuscular volume dMCV/dt = ((g1 U + MCV0) r1 Q - 0.85 MCV(t - lifespan) d1 L(t - lifespan) - 0.15 MCV d1 L) / L. Before the start the mature cells and their volume keep their initial values.

The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of ErythropoiesisMercaptopurineSystem read its parameters.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The production of red cells under a constant level of 6-mercaptopurine.

The production starts from health.

The drug kills proliferating cells and lengthens their cycle, so fewer quiescent cells survive to mature, the mature red cells fall, and their mean volume rises to MCV0 + g1 U. The cells are in 10^12 per kg, the volume in fL, the drug in pMol per 8 x 10^8 red cells, and time in days. The parameters are those of Table 3.10 of Padmanabhan et al., with its half saturation of 2.7 x 10^10 cells per kg written as Q50 = 0.027. The patient starts at the healthy steady state, Q = Q50 (m0 / r1 - 1)^(1/n), L = r1 Q / d1, the book's ratio of proliferating to quiescent cells 0.71 / 6.43, and MCV = 85. The book garbles equation 3.36 as -r1 AQ (2 exp(a1 tau) - 1) m(AQ) AQ. The system takes the standard form of Mackey 1978 that Noble et al. use, dQ/dt = -r1 Q + (2 exp(-a1 tau) - 1) m(Q) Q, in which cells leave to mature at the rate r1 and the cells that enter the cycle return doubled once they survive the drug. docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

HER2+ breast cancer cells under trastuzumab and paclitaxel.

The model includes antibody binding and drug uptake.

The free antibody and the free paclitaxel are drivers held at their levels from their doses on. The antibody binds the receptors, which are in excess, so the bound antibody rises to the free antibody, and from the time t_a on it lowers the growth rate to r (1 - a1 Ab). The paclitaxel enters the cells and briefly lowers the carrying capacity. The cytotoxicity falls from one at the dose, so t_p is the dose time. The system has the cells tumour.A, the bound antibody tumour.Ab, and the internalized paclitaxel tumour.Pin.
