docs.title: act(system)
docs.text:
Decide the night, score the patrons, and let the coalitions split and merge.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system SystemView

The system view of the bar.

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/econophysics/_coalitions.py 
def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Decide the night, score the patrons, and let the coalitions split and merge.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the bar.
    """
    patrons = sorted(system.get_agents('patrons', CoalitionPatronView), key=lambda patron: patron.id)
    strategies = np.asarray(self.strategies, dtype=float)
    memory, size, capacity = strategies.shape[-1] - 1, len(patrons), system.get_parameter('capacity')
    stored = system.storage.get('history')
    history = np.asarray(stored) if isinstance(stored, np.ndarray) else system.rng.integers(0, size + 1, 2 * memory)
    records = system.storage.get('records')
    records = records if isinstance(records, dict) else {}
    labels = np.array([int(patron.coalition) for patron in patrons])
    if not self.coalitions:
        labels = np.arange(size)
    errors = self._get_errors(strategies, history.astype(float))
    best: dict[int, int] = {}
    attends = np.zeros(size, dtype=bool)
    for label in np.unique(labels):
        members = np.flatnonzero(labels == label)
        owner, strategy = np.unravel_index(np.argmin(errors[members]), errors[members].shape)
        best[int(label)] = int(members[owner])
        weights = strategies[members[owner], strategy]
        attends[members] = size * weights[0] + weights[1:] @ history[:memory] <= capacity
    attendance = float(attends.sum())
    crowded = attendance > capacity
    good = np.where(attends, not crowded, crowded)
    smoothing = system.get_parameter('smoothing')
    scores = np.array([patron.score for patron in patrons]) * (1 - smoothing) + smoothing * good
    for label in np.unique(labels[attends]):
        records.setdefault(int(label), []).append((attendance, float(np.sum(labels == label))))
    for label in list(records):
        records[label] = records[label][-memory:]
    splits = joins = 0
    if self.coalitions:
        splits = self._split(system, labels, best, records)
        joins = 0 if crowded else self._join(system, labels, attends, records)
    system.storage.update(history=np.concatenate(([attendance], history[:-1])), records=records)
    for patron, label, went, score in zip(patrons, labels, attends, scores, strict=True):
        patron.coalition, patron.attends, patron.score = float(label), float(went), float(score)
    system.report('attendance', attendance)
    system.report('coalitions', float(len(np.unique(labels))))
    system.report('mean_score', float(scores.mean()))
    system.report('splits', float(splits))
    system.report('joins', float(joins))

docs.text:
Bases: ChoiceInteraction

Stochastic crowd avoidance of diners, who leave crowded restaurants.

A diner returns to last evening's restaurant with probability 1 / n, with n the crowd it found there, and otherwise moves to one of the other restaurants at random, which raises the utilization to about 0.8. It is a Metropolis choice of intensity 1 where every other restaurant has utility 0 and staying has the utility -log(1 - 1 / n), so a proposed move is accepted with probability 1 - 1 / n.

The intensity of choice, 1 for the stay probability 1 / n.

1.0 activity float

The probability that a diner revises its choice in an evening.

1.0 phase str | None

The phase the choice runs in, or None for the default phase.

None

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import CrowdAvoidanceInteraction

Bases: TransferInteraction

Random pairwise trades of Dragulescu and Yakovenko of a fixed amount.

Debt is allowed down to a limit. In every trade an agent pays a fixed amount to another agent drawn at random, unless its wealth would fall below minus the debt limit. docs.title: ElFarolCoalitionsSystem(n_agents=100, *, capacity=60.0, memory=5, n_strategies=10, smoothing=0.1, coalitions=True, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Collins' El Farol bar with strategic group formation.

Its coalitions share their best strategy. Patrons of Rand and Wilensky's El Farol model predict the attendance with linear strategies of the last memory attendances and go when they predict room. In Collins' version (Carmichael et al. 2019, chapter 9) patrons form coalitions that use the best strategy of all their members, so a larger coalition has better predictions but adds more to the crowd. Coalitions split off the members with the best strategy after overcrowded nights, the core condition that no subgroup gains by leaving, and coalitions that attended together merge when it would not have crowded an earlier good night. Without coalitions the mean attendance stays near the capacity and patrons enjoy about half their nights, while coalitions make the attendance swing and lower the returns of all, because the patrons are boundedly rational. The return of a patron is exponentially smoothed with the weight smoothing, which the source leaves open.

The system has the group patrons and the bar bar, whose reporters are bar.attendance, the number of coalitions bar.coalitions, the mean return bar.mean_score, and the splits bar.splits and joins bar.joins of the night.

The attendance above which the bar is overcrowded.

The number of past attendances a strategy reads.

10 smoothing float

The weight of the last night in the return.

0.1 coalitions bool

Whether patrons form coalitions.

True random_state int | Generator | None

The seed or generator of the strategies.

>>> ElFarolCoalitionsSystem(10).prepare().system_.elements[0].prepare().size_

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Arthur's El Farol bar problem.

Its attendance self-organizes around the capacity. Every patron holds a random set of predictors of next week's attendance, drawn from a pool of 46, and acts on its currently most accurate one, going when it forecasts room in the bar. The attendance is random-looking, yet its mean settles near the capacity. The patrons read the past attendances from the observable attendance of the run, which the catalog lists, so a run passes it in observables.

The system has the group patrons, the one-member group pool of the forecasts and the errors of the predictors, the reinforcement scoring of the errors, and the choice choice to go when the forecast is below the capacity of the patrons.

docs.title: KineticWealthWelfareSystem(classes=9, *, cooperation=0.2, competition=0.3, eta=1.0, tax=0.0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The kinetic theory of wealth classes.

A positive tax adds a welfare policy. The population is a distribution over wealth classes, a site group on a lattice of the classes. Encounters between classes move particles one class up or down, with cooperation narrowing the gaps and competition widening them, so the total density stays constant. When competition wins, wealth polarises toward the poorest and the richest classes, and the Gini coefficient grows. A welfare policy is an encounter with a group of fixed density, which moves the richest third of the classes down and the poorest third up and lowers the stationary Gini coefficient.

The system has the distribution wealth, the encounters exchange, and with a tax the group state and the policy welfare. Its standard observables are the density, the mean wealth, and the Gini coefficient of wealth.

Parameters:

The number of wealth classes.

The probability of the move that narrows the gap between the classes of an encounter.

0.2 competition float

0.3 eta float

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Rounds of the minority game of Challet and Zhang.

The agents on the minority side win. Every round each agent plays the action, +1 or -1, that its chosen strategy assigns to the last m winning sides, the strategy of higher virtual score that a ChoiceInteraction of rule 'best' chooses before. The side with fewer agents wins, and every agent on it gains one point and every other loses one. The game reports the attendance A = sum_i a_i and the code of the history the strategies read, so a cumulative PayoffLearningInteraction gives every strategy one virtual point when it would have played the winning side, by the payoff payoff. The volatility sigma^2 / N of the attendance has a minimum below the value of random play near alpha = 2^m / N ~ 0.34.

def get_payoff(self, agent: MinorityPlayerView, system: SystemView, option: int) -> float:
    """Return the virtual payoff of a strategy of an agent in the last round.

    It is `+1` if it played the winning side.

    Args:
        agent:
            The agent.

        system:
            The system view of the rule that reads the payoff.

        option:
            The strategy, 0 for the first and 1 for the second.

    Returns:
        payoff:
            `+1` when the strategy would have played the winning side, or `-1`.
    """
    history = int(system.get_history(f'{self.label}.history')[-1])
    winner = -1 if system.get_history(f'{self.label}.attendance')[-1] > 0 else 1
    code = agent.second if option else agent.first
    return float((2 * int(strategy_table(code, self.memory)[history]) - 1) * winner)

def play(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Play one round, pay the agents, and update and report the history.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    agents = system.get_agents('players', MinorityPlayerView)
    history = self._get_state(system).history
    for agent in agents:
        code = agent.second if agent.strategy else agent.first
        agent.action = float(2 * int(self._get_table(code, system)[history]) - 1)
    attendance = sum(agent.action for agent in agents)
    winner = -1 if attendance > 0 else 1
    for agent in agents:
        agent.wealth += agent.action * winner
    state = self._get_state(system)
    system.storage['game'] = replace(state, history=(2 * history + (winner > 0)) % 2**self.memory)
    system.report('attendance', attendance)
    system.report('history', float(history))

def predict(self, agent: PatronView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Forecast the attendance with the most accurate predictor held.

    Args:
        agent:
            The patron.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    pool = system.get_agents(self.pool, PredictorPoolView)[0]
    errors, predicted = np.ravel(pool.errors), np.ravel(pool.forecasts)
    mask = int(agent.predictors)
    held = [index for index in range(len(PREDICTORS)) if mask >> index & 1]
    agent.forecast = float(predicted[held[int(np.argmin(errors[held]))]])

@staticmethod
def get_error(agent: PredictorPoolView, system: SystemView, index: int) -> float:
    """Return the absolute error of a predictor last week.

    Before the first attendance, it is its error so far.

    Args:
        agent:
            The pool.

        system:
            The system view of the rule that reads the error.

        index:
            The index of the predictor in the pool.

    Returns:
        error:
            The absolute error of the forecast of the predictor.
    """
    attendance = system.get_history(PredictorPoolElement.attendance)
    if not len(attendance):
        return float(np.ravel(agent.errors)[index])
    return float(abs(np.ravel(agent.forecasts)[index] - attendance[-1]))

docs.title: SavingExchangeInteraction(label, *, source, target, saving=0.0, phase=None)
docs.text:
Bases: TransferInteraction

Random pairwise trades of Chakraborti and Chakrabarti.

Every agent saves a fraction of its wealth. A trade between agents i and j keeps total wealth and gives w_i' = lambda w_i + eps (1 - lambda) (w_i + w_j) and w_j' = lambda w_j + (1 - eps) (1 - lambda) (w_i + w_j) with eps uniform on [0, 1], so i transfers (1 - lambda) (w_i - eps (w_i + w_j)) to j, an amount of either sign. Every step, every agent trades once with another agent drawn at random, in random order. Without saving the stationary wealth distribution is exponential, and with saving propensity lambda it is close to a Gamma distribution of shape n = 1 + 3 lambda / (1 - lambda).

docs.title: exchange_table(classes, cooperation, competition)
docs.text:
Return the transition table of encounters between wealth classes, A[h, k, i].

A candidate of class h that meets a richer field particle moves one class up with probability cooperation and one class down with probability competition. One that meets a poorer field particle moves one class up with probability competition and one class down with probability cooperation. So competition makes the rich richer and the poor poorer, and cooperation does the opposite. A move past the poorest or the richest class is not made.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default classes int

The number of wealth classes.

required cooperation object

The probability of the move that narrows the gap between the two classes, a number or a parameter.

required competition object

The probability of the move that widens it, a number or a parameter.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description table NDArray[object_]

The transition probabilities, which sum to one over the outcomes.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import exchange_table
>>> exchange_table(3, 0.2, 0.3)[0, 2].astype(float).tolist()
[0.8, 0.2, 0.0]
Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/econophysics/_welfare.py 
def exchange_table(classes: int, cooperation: object, competition: object) -> npt.NDArray[np.object_]:
    """Return the transition table of encounters between wealth classes, `A[h, k, i]`.

    A candidate of class `h` that meets a richer field particle moves one class up with probability `cooperation`
    and one class down with probability `competition`. One that meets a poorer field particle moves one class up with
    probability `competition` and one class down with probability `cooperation`. So competition makes the rich richer
    and the poor poorer, and cooperation does the opposite. A move past the poorest or the richest class is not made.

    Args:
        classes:
            The number of wealth classes.

        cooperation:
            The probability of the move that narrows the gap between the two classes, a number or a parameter.

        competition:
            The probability of the move that widens it, a number or a parameter.

    Returns:
        table:
            The transition probabilities, which sum to one over the outcomes.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import exchange_table
        >>> exchange_table(3, 0.2, 0.3)[0, 2].astype(float).tolist()
        [0.8, 0.2, 0.0]
    """
    table = np.zeros((classes, classes, classes), dtype=object)
    for candidate in range(classes):
        for field in range(classes):
            gap = int(np.sign(field - candidate))
            moves = {candidate + gap: cooperation, candidate - gap: competition} if gap else {}
            for outcome, probability in moves.items():
                if 0 <= outcome < classes:
                    table[candidate, field, outcome] += probability
            table[candidate, field, candidate] += 1.0 - table[candidate, field].sum()
    return table

def forecasts(history: npt.ArrayLike) -> Array:
    """Return the forecast of next week's attendance of every predictor of the pool.

    It lies between 0 and 100.

    Args:
        history:
            The past attendances, the last one last, at least ten of them.

    Returns:
        forecasts:
            One forecast per predictor of the pool.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import forecasts
        >>> forecasts([60.0] * 10)[:3].tolist()
        [60.0, 60.0, 60.0]
    """
    values = np.asarray(history, dtype=float)
    predicted = [function(values, **arguments) for function, arguments in PREDICTORS]
    return np.clip(predicted, 0.0, MAX_ATTENDANCE)

Return the Gini coefficient of a distribution over wealth classes.

Every member of its group reads it. The coefficient is sum_ij f_i f_j |w_i - w_j| / (2 F M), with the density F and the total wealth M.

Parameters:

def gini_coefficient(s: SimpleNamespace, wealth: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> Expression:
    """Return the Gini coefficient of a distribution over wealth classes.

    Every member of its group reads it. The coefficient is `sum_ij f_i f_j |w_i - w_j| / (2 F M)`, with the density `F`
    and the total wealth `M`.

    Args:
        s:
            The namespace of one member of the distribution.

        wealth:
            The wealth of every class.

    Returns:
        gini:
            The coefficient as an expression of reductions.
    """
    spread = total(s.x, weights=np.abs(wealth[:, None] - wealth[None, :]))
    return total(s.x * spread) / (2 * moment(s.x, 0, wealth) * moment(s.x, 1, wealth))

Return the rate pattern and the transition table of a welfare policy.

The policy taxes the rich and helps the poor. The policy moves a candidate of the richest third of the classes one class down, and a candidate of the poorest third one class up, and leaves the middle classes alone.

Parameters:

The number of wealth classes.

required

The transition table A[h, 0, i] of the policy.

>>> policy_table(3)[0].ravel().tolist()
[1.0, 0.0, 1.0]
Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/econophysics/_welfare.py 
def policy_table(classes: int) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """Return the rate pattern and the transition table of a welfare policy.

    The policy taxes the rich and helps the poor. The policy moves a candidate of the richest third of the classes one
    class down, and a candidate of the poorest third one class up, and leaves the middle classes alone.

    Args:
        classes:
            The number of wealth classes.

    Returns:
        pattern:
            The rate pattern `eta[h, 0]`, 1 for the classes the policy acts on and 0 for the others.

        table:
            The transition table `A[h, 0, i]` of the policy.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import policy_table
        >>> policy_table(3)[0].ravel().tolist()
        [1.0, 0.0, 1.0]
    """
    pattern = np.zeros((classes, 1))
    table = np.zeros((classes, 1, classes))
    third = max(1, classes // 3)
    for candidate in range(classes):
        outcome = candidate + 1 if candidate < third else candidate - 1 if candidate >= classes - third else candidate
        pattern[candidate, 0] = float(outcome != candidate)
        table[candidate, 0, outcome] = 1.0
    return pattern, table

Return the table of a minority game strategy.

It holds the bit the strategy plays after each of the 2^m histories. A table has 2^m bits, too many to store as one number beyond small memories, so a strategy is stored as the integer code that seeds a generator of its table.

Parameters:

required memory int

The memory m, the number of past outcomes the strategy reads.

required

Name Type Description table IntArray

The bit of the strategy for every history, from 0 to 2^m - 1.

>>> strategy_table(7, 2).shape
(4,)
Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/econophysics/_minority.py 
def strategy_table(code: float, memory: int) -> IntArray:
    """Return the table of a minority game strategy.

    It holds the bit the strategy plays after each of the `2^m` histories. A table has `2^m` bits, too many to store as
    one number beyond small memories, so a strategy is stored as the integer code that seeds a generator of its table.

    Args:
        code:
            The integer code of the strategy.

        memory:
            The memory `m`, the number of past outcomes the strategy reads.

    Returns:
        table:
            The bit of the strategy for every history, from 0 to `2^m - 1`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import strategy_table
        >>> strategy_table(7, 2).shape
        (4,)
    """
    return np.random.default_rng(int(code)).integers(0, 2, 2**memory)

def wealth_observables(classes: int) -> list[ObservableSpec]:
    """Return the density, the mean wealth, and the Gini coefficient of a distribution.

    The distribution is `wealth`, over wealth classes.

    Args:
        classes:
            The number of wealth classes.

    Returns:
        observables:
            The observables, each reading the moments of the distribution.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.econophysics import wealth_observables
        >>> [item.label for item in wealth_observables(9)]

    wealth = wealth_classes(classes)

        ObservableSpec('mean_wealth', partial(mean_wealth, wealth=wealth), group='wealth'),
        ObservableSpec('gini', partial(gini_coefficient, wealth=wealth), group='wealth'),
    ]

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Bouchaud and Mezard's wealth dynamics.

Returns are random and multiplicative, with exchange between neighbours. Agent i follows the Stratonovich equation dW_i = sigma W_i dB_i + (J / c) sum_j (W_j - W_i) dt over its neighbours j on a network of mean degree c. Without a graph, the agents are the members of a group and every agent exchanges with every other, c = N - 1, the complete graph at a cost linear in the number of agents. A given graph keeps the agents on a field over its edges. Exchange conserves the total wealth, and on the complete graph the relative wealth W_i / <W> approaches a stationary distribution with the Pareto tail P(W_i / <W> > w) ~ w^-mu of exponent mu = 1 + 2 J / sigma^2.

The system has the wealth agents.W and the mean wealth mean_wealth.

Advance the distress and the states of every bank by one step.

Parameters:

def spread(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Advance the distress and the states of every bank by one step.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    banks = sorted(system.get_agents('banks', InterbankView), key=lambda bank: bank.id)
    h = np.array([bank.h for bank in banks])
    status = np.array([bank.status for bank in banks])
    distressed = status == DISTRESSED
    new_h = np.minimum(1.0, h + np.asarray(self.impact, dtype=float).T @ (h * distressed))
    hit = (status == UNDISTRESSED) & (new_h > 0)
    new_status = np.where(distressed, INACTIVE, np.where(hit, DISTRESSED, status))
    for bank, level, code in zip(banks, new_h, new_status, strict=True):
        bank.h, bank.status = float(level), float(code)

docs.text:
Pass on the losses of the defaulting banks.

Then default the banks below the threshold.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system SystemView

The system view of the cascade.

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/finance/_solvency.py 
def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Pass on the losses of the defaulting banks.

    Then default the banks below the threshold.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the cascade.
    """
    banks = sorted(system.get_agents('banks', BalanceSheetView), key=lambda bank: bank.id)
    status = np.array([bank.status for bank in banks])
    equity = np.array([bank.equity for bank in banks])
    defaulting = status == DEFAULTING
    losses = (1 - system.get_parameter('recovery')) * np.asarray(self.liabilities, dtype=float).T @ defaulting
    equity = equity - losses
    hit = (status == SOLVENT) & (equity < system.get_parameter('threshold'))
    status = np.where(defaulting, DEFAULTED, np.where(hit, DEFAULTING, status))
    for bank, value, code in zip(banks, equity, status, strict=True):
        bank.equity, bank.status = float(value), float(code)
    system.report('defaults', float(np.sum(status != SOLVENT)))
    system.report('losses', float(losses.sum()))

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A cascade of defaults through interbank exposures.

It starts from a shock to the external assets of some banks. Banks are linked by contracts, liabilities[i][j] the amount bank i owes bank j. A bank whose equity falls below the threshold h defaults, and its creditors write off their claims on it, losing (1 - R) L_ij of their equity at the next step, which may default them in turn. This is the cascade of Thurner et al. (2018, Section 5.5.3.2), and with h = 0 and the recovery rate R = 0 it is the contagion on default of Gai and Kapadia (2010) as Bardoscia et al. (2021, Section 3.1) review it. The shocked banks lose the share shock of their external assets at the start. Without a given network, every bank has assets of 100, a fifth of them interbank claims split evenly over a random number of debtors of mean degree, and capital of 4 percent, the network of Gai and Kapadia, whose cascades are large in a window of intermediate degrees and rare for sparse or dense networks.

The system has the group banks and the cascade cascade, whose reporters are the number of defaulted banks cascade.defaults and the losses written off in the step cascade.losses.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The clearing of interbank payments of Eisenberg and Noe.

It is a fixed point of proportional payments. Bank i owes L_ij to bank j, p_bar_i in all, and holds external assets e_i. A clearing vector pays p_i = min(p_bar_i, e_i + sum_j Pi_ji p_j), every bank paying in full or all it has, its debtors paying in proportion Pi_ij = L_ij / p_bar_i, the liquidity contagion of Bardoscia et al. (2021, Section 3.1). Every step is one round of the iteration from full payments, which falls monotonically to the greatest clearing vector, the solution of the linear programme max sum_i p_i with p <= p_bar and p <= e + Pi^T p. Without a given network the liabilities are random and the external assets are small for a few banks.

The system has the group banks of the payments banks.payment, and the clearing clearing, whose reporters are the total unpaid liabilities clearing.shortfall and the number of defaulting banks clearing.defaults.

docs.text:
Bases: PolicyRuleInteraction[SystemView]

Banks that sell common assets on losses, and the market impact.

The market impact lowers the prices of what they sell. Every step the banks value their holdings at the current prices. Under the rule 'threshold' a bank whose losses exhaust its equity defaults and liquidates its whole portfolio, and otherwise stays passive. Under 'leverage' a bank sells the same share of every holding to bring its assets back to leverage times its equity, and liquidates everything when its equity is gone. The proceeds become cash, and the price of every asset falls to p0 exp(-alpha x), where x is the share of the asset liquidated so far and p0 its price after the shock.

docs.text:
Value the portfolios, sell, and move the prices by the market impact.

Name Type Description Default system SystemView

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/finance/_fire_sales.py 
def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Value the portfolios, sell, and move the prices by the market impact.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the fire sales.
    """
    banks = sorted(system.get_agents('banks', BalanceSheetView), key=lambda bank: bank.id)
    assets = sorted(system.get_agents('assets', MarketAssetView), key=lambda asset: asset.id)
    initial = np.asarray(self.holdings, dtype=float)
    holdings = np.asarray(system.storage.get('holdings', initial))
    prices = np.array([asset.price for asset in assets])
    base = np.asarray(system.storage.get('base', prices))
    liquidated = np.array([asset.liquidated for asset in assets])
    cash = np.array([bank.external for bank in banks])
    status = np.array([bank.status for bank in banks])
    values = holdings @ prices + cash
    equity = values - np.asarray(self.liabilities, dtype=float)
    failed = equity <= 0
    if self.selling == 'leverage':
        excess = values - system.get_parameter('leverage') * equity
        excess = np.where(excess > 1e-9 * values, excess, 0.0)
        risky = holdings @ prices
        share = np.divide(excess, risky, out=np.zeros_like(excess), where=risky > 0)
        share = np.where(failed, 1.0, np.minimum(share, 1.0))
    else:
        share = np.where(failed & (status == SOLVENT), 1.0, 0.0)
    sold = holdings * share[:, None]
    cash = cash + sold @ prices
    holdings = holdings - sold
    totals = initial.sum(axis=0)
    liquidated = np.minimum(
        1.0,
        liquidated + np.divide(sold.sum(axis=0), totals, out=np.zeros_like(totals), where=totals > 0),
    )
    prices = base * np.exp(-system.get_parameter('alpha') * liquidated)
    status = np.where(failed, DEFAULTED, status)
    equity = holdings @ prices + cash - np.asarray(self.liabilities, dtype=float)
    system.storage.update(holdings=holdings, base=base)
    for bank, value, money, code in zip(banks, equity, cash, status, strict=True):
        bank.equity, bank.external, bank.status = float(value), float(money), float(code)
    for asset, price, share_sold in zip(assets, prices, liquidated, strict=True):
        asset.price, asset.liquidated = float(price), float(share_sold)
    system.report('defaults', float(np.sum(status == DEFAULTED)))
    system.report('sold', float((sold @ prices).sum()))

docs.title: GaugeArbitrageMarketSystem(size=16, *, D=0.5, q=0.2, bump=1.0, seed=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Exchange-rate potentials on links as lattice Maxwell fields.

Traders who move a good on sites source them.

The potentials follow A_t = E and E_t = -codifferential(dA) - J, and the good follows rho_t = -codifferential(J) with the current J = -D (d rho - q A rho) along its covariant gradient, after Schwichtenberg (2020 §2.1 and §2.2.1). Here E is F_0i of the book, so codifferential(E) equals the excess of the good over its mean, as in its Gauss law, Eq. 2.37, with a uniform background of the mean density that keeps the periodic lattice neutral. The system departs from the book in two places. The book writes Eq. 2.39 with no metric, which gives A_tt = +codifferential(dA) - J, where every mode with a curl grows, so the system takes the sign of a wave. And Eq. 2.56 applies the covariant derivative twice, which does not conserve the good, so the system applies it once inside the divergence of the current. The book gives no values of D and q and sets mu_0 by no number, so D, q, and mu_0 = 1 are choices of this system.

docs.text:
Bases: PolicyRuleInteraction[SystemView]

Order-driven market of noise traders who imitate the expectation of a guru.

The network is rewired every day. Every step is a trading day. First every trader picks a random trader j and moves its link from the trader k it follows to j with probability 1 / (1 + exp(-beta (f_j - f_k))), where the fitness f is the wealth relative to the richest trader (Eqs. 3.4 and 3.5 of Caiani et al. 2016). The guru is the trader of the largest in-degree of the day before, and the intensity of choice beta grows by beta_step every day the guru survives and returns to 1 when it is replaced. Every trader draws its expected return sigma_i eps (Eq. 3.3) and adopts the one of the trader it follows, except the guru.

Then tau intraday operations run, each by a trader drawn at random. With the expected price p_ref exp(sqrt(tau) r) (Eq. 3.1), a trader expecting a rise bids U(p (1 - gamma1), p_hat) for a random share of its free cash, and a trader expecting a fall asks U(p_hat, p (1 + gamma2)) for a random share of its free stocks (Eq. 3.2 and Table 3.1). An order that crosses the book is a market order that trades with the best quotes by price and time priority, and what is left rests as a limit order, whose cash or stocks stay tied in the book until it trades or expires at the end of the day. The price is the last traded price, the mid quote when an operation trades nothing, and the previous price when the book is empty.

def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Rewire the network, form the expectations, and run the trading day.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the market.
    """
    traders = sorted(system.get_agents('traders', GuruTraderView), key=lambda trader: trader.id)
    rng, store = system.rng, system.storage
    price = self._get_stored(system, 'price', system.get_parameter('opening'))
    beta = self._get_stored(system, 'beta', 1.0)
    cash = np.array([trader.cash for trader in traders])
    stocks = np.array([trader.stocks for trader in traders])
    follows = np.array([int(trader.follows) for trader in traders])
    sigma = np.array([trader.sigma for trader in traders])
    guru = int(np.argmax(np.bincount(follows, minlength=len(traders))))
    beta = beta + system.get_parameter('beta_step') if guru == self._get_stored(system, 'guru', -1.0) else 1.0
    wealth = cash + price * stocks
    follows = self._rewire(follows, wealth / wealth.max(), beta, rng)
    own = sigma * rng.normal(size=len(traders))
    expectation = own[follows]
    expectation[guru] = own[guru]
    holdings = {
        'cash': cash,
        'stocks': stocks,
        'tied_cash': np.zeros_like(cash),
        'tied_stocks': np.zeros_like(cash),
    }
    closing, volume = self._trade_day(system, holdings, expectation, price)
    followers = np.bincount(follows.astype(int), minlength=len(traders))
    store.update(price=closing, beta=beta, guru=guru)
    for index, trader in enumerate(traders):
        trader.cash, trader.stocks = float(cash[index]), float(stocks[index])
        trader.wealth = float(cash[index] + closing * stocks[index])
        trader.expectation, trader.follows = float(expectation[index]), float(follows[index])
        trader.followers = float(followers[index])
    system.report('price', closing)
    system.report('log_return', math.log(closing / price))
    system.report('volume', volume)
    system.report('guru', float(guru))
    system.report('beta', beta)
    system.report('guru_followers', float(followers.max()))

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The order-driven market of Grilli and Tedeschi.

Its noise traders imitate gurus they choose by wealth. Noise traders expect random returns of their own volatility, but every day each adopts the expectation of the trader it follows on a directed communication network. Every day each trader moves its link to a random trader with a logit probability of the difference of their wealths, whose intensity grows every day the guru, the most followed trader, keeps its place, so followers concentrate on successful traders and their expectations synchronize. The traders then place market and limit orders around a geometric Brownian forecast in an order book with price and time priority, within the day. This is the model of Caiani et al. (2016, Chapter 3, Sections 3.2 and 3.4). Imitation produces coordination periods in which most traders follow one guru, and the returns get fat tails and volatility clusters. The source leaves two choices open: the volatilities are uniform on (0, sigma), and the intensity of choice grows by beta_step every day the guru survives. The cash and the stocks of the traders are conserved, which the default run checks as invariants.

The system has the group traders and the market market, whose reporters are market.price, market.log_return, market.volume, market.guru, market.beta, and market.guru_followers. The observables of the system are the totals total_cash and total_stocks.

@staticmethod
def get_growth(agent: KestenFirmView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the size multiplied by a random factor plus a random term.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

        system:
            The system view of the growth.

    Returns:
        size:
            The size after the step.
    """
    factor = float(system.rng.uniform(agent.lambda_low, agent.lambda_high))
    return factor * agent.x + float(system.rng.uniform(agent.b_low, agent.b_high))

docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

Kirman's foreign exchange market.

Its traders switch between fundamentalism and chartism like ants. Fundamentalists expect the exchange rate to revert to its fundamental value, s_t-1 + v (s* - s_t-1), and chartists expect the last change to go on, s_t-1 + g (s_t-1 - s_t-2). With the mean-variance demand of both and the share n_t of fundamentalists, the market clears at the deviation of Eq. 1.36 of Caiani et al. (2016, Section 1.3.2), (1 + r) x_t = [1 - v n_t + g (1 - n_t)] x_t-1 - g (1 - n_t) x_t-2, written there with s_t-2 for x_t-2, a shock of the supply of foreign exchange added. The share follows the recruitment chain of Kirman's ants, which the source refers to and Kirman (1993) gives: when spontaneous changes are rarer than recruitment, epsilon < (1 - delta) / (N - 1), the traders spend long periods mostly of one kind and switch suddenly. A market of fundamentalists is stable with the eigenvalue (1 - v) / (1 + r) (Eq. 1.37), and a market of chartists oscillates, stable only while g <= 1 + r (Eq. 1.38), so the volatility of the rate comes and goes with the chartists. One trader meets another every step, so the defaults take a small market of 30 traders, whose regimes switch within a few thousand steps.

The system has the deviation market.x and the number of fundamentalists market.k. The observable of the system is the share of fundamentalists market.fundamentalists.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A stock market of fundamentalists and chartists on a grid.

They trade in a limit order book and imitate. Every step every trader forecasts the price, as a fundamentalist who expects it to revert to the fundamental value or as a chartist who expects the last change to go on, and quotes a limit order for one share at its forecast. The order book matches the orders with price-time priority, and every trade moves money and a share between the two traders. Then traders copy the strategy of a neighbour whose wealth grew more. Fundamentalists hold the price near the fundamental value, chartists amplify its swings, and imitation lets the share of chartists wander, so the returns come in bursts with fat tails.

The two strategies are the fundamentalists and chartists of Lux and Marchesi (1999), and imitating a wealthier neighbour on the grid stands in for their switching between strategies. The order book is the order-driven market of Caiani et al. (2016, section 3.2.1). The traders of Caiani's chapter 3, noise traders who follow gurus of an evolving network, are a different model. The system has the group traders and the book book, whose reporters are book.price and book.volume, and the imitation imitation of the strategies of more successful neighbours.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Banks with overlapping portfolios whose fire sales spread their losses.

The fire sales of common assets spread the losses to one another. Every bank invests equal amounts in diversification assets drawn at random, a bipartite network of banks and assets, with assets leverage times its equity. A shock lowers the price of one asset, and banks react to their losses: under the linear threshold rule a bank stays passive until its losses exhaust its equity and then liquidates its whole portfolio, and under leverage targeting it sells a share of every holding to restore its leverage. Sales lower prices through the market impact p = p0 exp(-alpha x) of the share x of an asset liquidated, which hits every bank holding the asset, so losses travel between banks that share no contract, the indirect contagion of Bardoscia et al. (2021, Section 3.2) after Caccioli et al. (2014). Larger impact and leverage make the cascades larger, and leverage targeting sells more for small shocks.

The system has the groups banks, of the equity banks.equity and the cash banks.external, and assets, of the prices assets.price, and the fire sales sales, whose reporters are the number of defaulted banks sales.defaults and the value sold in the step sales.sold.

docs.text:
Bases: PolicyRuleInteraction[SystemView]

Clearing of interbank payments of Eisenberg and Noe.

It iterates p <- min(p_bar, e + Pi^T p). Every step every bank pays the smaller of what it owes, p_bar_i = sum_j L_ij, and what it has, its external assets plus the payments it receives, which its debtors make in proportion to their liabilities, Pi_ij = L_ij / p_bar_i. From full payments the iteration falls to the greatest clearing vector, and a bank that pays less than it owes defaults.

def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Make one round of payments and record the shortfall and the defaults.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the clearing.
    """
    banks = sorted(system.get_agents('banks', BalanceSheetView), key=lambda bank: bank.id)
    matrix = np.asarray(self.liabilities, dtype=float)
    owed = matrix.sum(axis=1)
    shares = np.divide(matrix, owed[:, None], out=np.zeros_like(matrix), where=owed[:, None] > 0)
    payments = np.array([bank.payment for bank in banks])
    external = np.array([bank.external for bank in banks])
    payments = np.minimum(owed, external + shares.T @ payments)
    equity = external + shares.T @ payments - payments
    defaulted = payments < owed * (1 - 1e-12)
    for bank, paid, value, flag in zip(banks, payments, equity, defaulted, strict=True):
        bank.payment, bank.equity, bank.status = float(paid), float(value), float(DEFAULTED * flag)
    system.report('shortfall', float(np.sum(owed - payments)))
    system.report('defaults', float(defaulted.sum()))

def quote(self, agent: StockTraderView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Forecast the price and quote a limit order for one share.

    Args:
        agent:
            The trader.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    price, previous = self._get_prices(agent, system)
    if agent.strategy:
        expected = heuristics.trend([previous, price], strength=system.get_parameter('extrapolation'))
    else:
        reversion = 1 - system.get_parameter('reversion')
        expected = heuristics.fundamental(
            [price],
            fundamental=system.get_parameter('fundamental'),
            reversion=reversion,
        )
    expected = max(LOWEST_PRICE, expected * (1 + system.get_parameter('noise') * system.rng.normal()))
    buying = expected > price
    new_bid, new_ask = (expected, 0.0) if buying else (0.0, expected)
    agent.bid = new_bid
    agent.ask = new_ask
    agent.demand = float(buying and agent.money >= expected)
    agent.supply = float(not buying and agent.shares >= 1)

docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Trader current along the links, down the covariant gradient.

The current is J = -D (rho_t - rho_s - q A (rho_s + rho_t) / 2). The covariant derivative is D_mu = d_mu - A_mu of Schwichtenberg (2020 Eq. 2.55), with the charge q of its Eq. 4.24, and the current is minus the diffusion constant times this derivative of the good, as in Eq. 2.56. The current moves the good from the source of a link to its target (footnote 18 of §2.1), and it is the source of the field of the link with the sign of the Ampere-Maxwell law of Eq. 2.39, E' = ... - J, so the Gauss law holds as the good moves. These signs give the potential a mass, A'' = ... - D q rho A, for a positive density and charge, so the fields stay bounded.

Bases: BaseSystem

Arthur and Polak's evolution of technology.

It builds logic functions from NAND gates. The pool starts with the NAND gate and the constants 0 and 1. Every step wires a random circuit from the pool and keeps it when it computes a wanted function, negation, two-input and, or, exclusive or, nor, equivalence, and implication, or three-input and, or, parity, and majority, so simple inventions become the building blocks of complex ones. The system has the pool technologies, whose size is the reporter technologies.count.

docs.text:
Bases: StockFlowSystem

The Bass diffusion system, people who adopt a new product.

They adopt through advertising and word of mouth. A market of N people splits into potential adopters P and adopters A. Potential adopters adopt at the rate (p + q A / N) P, where the coefficient of innovation p captures adoption from external influence, such as advertising, and the coefficient of imitation q adoption from contact with adopters. People are conserved, so the adoption is a flow from P to A. With q > p the adoption rate rises to a peak at the time log(q / p) / (p + q) and the adopters follow an S-shaped curve. Starting without adopters, the closed form is A(t) = N (1 - exp(-(p + q) t)) / (1 + (q / p) exp(-(p + q) t)). The defaults are the mean coefficients that Sultan, Farley and Lehmann (1990) estimated over many products, with time in years.

The system has the potential adopters market.P, the adopters market.A, and the adoption flow market.adoption in people per year, over years.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The co-evolving combinatorial critical model.

Its diversity shows punctuated equilibria. Every entity exists or not. Pairs of existing entities produce other entities through the production tensor M+ and destroy them through the destruction tensor M-, random tensors with on average r+ productive and r- destructive sets per entity, fixed during the run. Every step, in random sequential order, an entity exists when its active productive sets outnumber its active destructive ones, disappears in the opposite case, and keeps its state on a tie, and then switches spontaneously with a small probability p (Thurner et al. 2018, Section 5.6.4). The diversity stays nearly constant for long quasi-equilibria, whose lifetimes and the sizes of the changes between them have approximate power laws, and restructures in bursts. Mostly productive tensors fill the system, mostly destructive ones keep it nearly empty, and the punctuated regime lies in between without fine-tuning. The source leaves the initial state open, so every entity exists at the start with the probability initial. With the tensors of this implementation the setting r+ = 10 and r- = 15 of Fig. 5.14 restructures almost every step, so the defaults take r+ = 5 and r- = 10, which is punctuated.

The system has the group entities and the update update, whose reporters are the number of existing entities update.diversity and the entities that changed state in the step update.changes.

def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Update every entity once in random order.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the update.
    """
    entities = sorted(system.get_agents('entities', CombinatorialEntityView), key=lambda entity: entity.id)
    size, rng = len(entities), system.rng
    states = np.array([entity.exists for entity in entities])
    before = states.copy()
    plus, minus = self._get_sets(self.production, size), self._get_sets(self.destruction, size)
    fitness = np.array([entity.fitness for entity in entities])
    flips = rng.random(size) < system.get_parameter('p')
    for entity in rng.permutation(size):
        gain = states[plus[entity][:, 0]] @ states[plus[entity][:, 1]]
        loss = states[minus[entity][:, 0]] @ states[minus[entity][:, 1]]
        fitness[entity] = gain - loss
        if fitness[entity] != 0:
            states[entity] = float(fitness[entity] > 0)
        if flips[entity]:
            states[entity] = 1 - states[entity]
    for entity, state, value in zip(entities, states, fitness, strict=True):
        entity.exists, entity.fitness = float(state), float(value)
    system.report('diversity', float(states.sum()))
    system.report('changes', float(np.sum(states != before)))

def get_phone(agent: HouseholdView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return 1 for a household that has or gets a phone, else 0.

    if agent.phone or agent.income < agent.threshold:

docs.title: InteractingUrnsNetworkSystem(graph=None, *, rho=4, nu=1, m0=None, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

One urn with triggering per node of a network.

Every node draws from its own urn and those of its neighbours. The discovery process of Iacopini et al. (2020, Eqs. 1 and 2). Every node holds an urn of m0 balls of colours that no other urn holds. Every step every node draws one ball from its social urn, its own urn and one ball of every colour of the urns of its neighbours, all from the urns at the start of the step. It then adds rho balls of the drawn colour to its own urn, and when it draws a colour for the first time, a novelty, nu + 1 balls of colours that no urn held before. The number of novelties of a node grows as Heaps' law D_i(t) ~ t^beta_i, with beta = nu / rho for an isolated urn and higher exponents for nodes whose neighbours enlarge their social urns.

The urn of a node is the set of ball agents of the variable group balls on its node, one agent per colour with its multiplicity, which the node reads with agents_here and its neighbours with neighbors(group='balls'). The system has the urns urns and their novelties urns.novelties, and the balls balls.

def invent(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Wire a random circuit and add it to the pool if it is better.

    It is better when it computes a wanted function better.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    pool = system.get_agents('technologies', TechnologyView)
    arity, table, cost = self._wire(pool, system)
    if (arity, table) not in GOALS:
        return
    known = [technology for technology in pool if (technology.arity, technology.table) == (arity, table)]
    if not known:
        system.create('technologies', arity=arity, table=table, cost=cost)
    elif cost < known[0].cost:
        known[0].cost = cost

Hamill and Gilbert's adoption of fixed-line phones by British households.

The adoption starts from 1951. One household lives in every cell of a torus. The upper class lives in the top left quadrant, the lower class in the bottom left, and the middle class elsewhere, so neighbours tend to be alike. The first owners are a cluster of affording households grown from the richest upper-class household.

def redesign(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Propose new costs for a random component and its dependents.

    They are kept if the total cost falls.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    components = sorted(system.get_agents('components', PartView), key=lambda component: component.id)
    cost = np.array([component.cost for component in components])
    proposal, changed = RedesignInteraction._get_components(
        cost,
        np.asarray(self.dependencies, dtype=float),
        system.rng,
    )
    if proposal.sum() >= cost.sum():
        return
    for index in changed:
        components[index].cost = float(proposal[index])

docs.title: TapCatalysisSystem(m0=10, *, parents=4, alpha=0.01, goods=1250, pc=0.0044, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The TAP growth of goods from combinations of goods.

Their production functions are catalysed at random. The TAP model with catalysis of Hordijk and Kauffman (2022, Algorithm 1), in continuous time. From m0 goods, new goods made from i parents drawn uniformly among the M goods appear at the rate alpha^i C(M, i), for every i up to parents, until there are goods goods. The production function of a new good is a hyperedge of its parents and the good, its last member. A new good catalyses the production of every other good, and every other good catalyses its production, each with the probability pc, as directed edges from the catalyst to the good. Algorithm 1 draws a Poisson number of goods of every order per step from the rates at its start, and the process here draws them one at a time from the rates at that time. The initial goods are the food set, and autocatalytic_sets finds the largest autocatalytic set of the production functions, which exists in about half the runs at pc = 0.0044 and then tends to hold most of the network.

The system has the goods goods, the catalysis catalysis, and the production functions functions.

Bases: Element

Urn with triggering on a node of a network.

It draws from its own balls and those of its neighbours. The urn of the interacting discovery processes of Iacopini et al. (2020). The urn of a node is the set of ball agents on its node. Every step the node draws one ball from its social urn, its own balls with their multiplicities and one ball of every colour in the urns of its neighbours, in the phase 'draw'. In the phase 'grow' it adds rho balls of the drawn colour to its own urn, and when it draws the colour for the first time, a novelty, it adds one ball of each of nu + 1 colours that no urn held before, the adjacent possible.

@staticmethod
def draw(agent: UrnView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Draw a ball from the social urn of the node.

    It records its colour and whether it is a novelty.

    Args:
        agent:
            The view of the urn.

        system:
            The view of the system.
    """
    own = [ball for ball in agent.get_agents_here(BALLS) if isinstance(ball, BallView)]
    social = [ball for ball in agent.get_neighbors(group=BALLS) if isinstance(ball, BallView)]
    colors = [ball.color for ball in own] + [ball.color for ball in social]
    weights = np.asarray([ball.count for ball in own] + [1.0] * len(social), dtype=float)
    if not colors:
        return
    chosen = colors[int(system.rng.choice(len(colors), p=weights / weights.sum()))]
    agent.color = chosen
    agent.novel = float(not any(ball.color == chosen and ball.drawn for ball in own))

docs.text:
Reinforce the drawn colour in the own urn.

After a novelty, it adds the colours of the adjacent possible.

Parameters:

required system SystemView

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/economics/innovation/_discovery.py 
@staticmethod
def grow(agent: UrnView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Reinforce the drawn colour in the own urn.

    After a novelty, it adds the colours of the adjacent possible.

    Args:
        agent:
            The view of the urn.

        system:
            The view of the system.
    """
    if agent.color < 0:
        return
    rho, nu = system.get_parameter('rho'), system.get_parameter('nu')
    own = [ball for ball in agent.get_agents_here(BALLS) if isinstance(ball, BallView)]
    ball = next((ball for ball in own if ball.color == agent.color), None)
    if ball is None:
        agent.create(BALLS, color=agent.color, count=rho, drawn=1)
    else:
        ball.count += rho
        ball.drawn = 1
    if not agent.novel:
        return
    agent.novelties += 1
    stored = system.storage.get('colors')
    first = (
        stored
        if isinstance(stored, int)
        else int(max(item.color for item in system.get_agents(BALLS, BallView))) + 1
    )
    for color in range(first, first + int(nu) + 1):
        agent.create(BALLS, color=color, count=1, drawn=0)
    system.storage['colors'] = first + int(nu) + 1

docs.title: BrockMirmanGrowthSystem(K=0.2, *, alpha=1 / 3, beta=0.95, z_low=0.9, z_high=1.1, persistence=0.9, regime=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The Brock-Mirman economy.

It is the optimal growth of a representative agent whose productivity is Markov. A representative consumer maximises E_0 sum_t beta^t ln C_t subject to K_{t+1} = Y_t - C_t, with full depreciation and the output Y_t = z_t K_t^alpha of a representative firm, whose productivity z_t follows a Markov chain. The solution is the linear consumption rule C_t = (1 - alpha beta) Y_t, C = 0.68 Y for alpha = 1/3 and beta = 0.95, so the capital follows K_{t+1} = alpha beta z_t K_t^alpha and ln K is a stationary autoregression around (ln(alpha beta) + E ln z) / (1 - alpha). This is the standard model that Caiani et al. (2016, Section 1.1.4, Eqs. 1.3 to 1.9) compare with an agent-based economy. The source leaves the chain open, so the productivity takes two levels that stay with the probability persistence.

The system has the capital economy.K and the regime economy.regime. The observables of the system are economy.productivity, economy.output, and economy.consumption.

Bases: Element

Firm on a patch that harvests with its workers and sells food in its shop.

It pays wages with money it borrows. Every step the workers pool their labour on the firm's patch, the firm pays each the wage, borrowing what it lacks from the bank, and pays the interest and a share of the principal of its loans. A firm that sold out raises its price, and one with a stock above stock_limit lowers it and lays a worker off. Otherwise a firm posts vacancies up to the workforce that harvests the whole capacity of its patch, raises the wage while a vacancy went unfilled, and lowers it while its sales fall short of its wage bill. Profits above twice the wage bill go to the owner, and a firm without a living owner passes to one of its workers.

def produce(self, agent: BusinessView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Harvest with the workers, pay wages and the bank, and adjust.

    It then pays a dividend to the owner.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    people = BusinessElement._get_people_by_id(system)
    workers = [person for person in people.values() if person.employer == agent.id]
    bank = system.get_agents('bank', CentralBankView)[0]
    patch = SettlerElement._get_patch_here(agent)
    sold_out = agent.stock <= 0
    for worker in workers:
        worker.move_to(agent.location)
    labour = sum(worker.labour for worker in workers)
    harvest = min(patch.food, max(labour - patch.resistance, 0.0))
    patch.food -= harvest
    agent.stock += harvest
    bill = agent.wage * len(workers)
    self._borrow(agent, bank, bill - agent.money)
    for worker in workers:
        transfer(agent, worker, agent.wage, 'money')
        worker.harvested = worker.need
    self._pay_debt(agent, bank)
    self._adjust(agent, workers, patch, sold_out)
    agent.workers, agent.revenue = float(len(workers)), 0.0
    owner = agent.get_referenced('owner')
    if not isinstance(owner, SettlerView) and workers:
        owner = workers[0]
        agent.owner = float(owner.id)
    if isinstance(owner, SettlerView) and agent.money > 2 * bill:
        transfer(agent, owner, agent.money - 2 * bill, 'money')

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Forrest's categorized purchasing power of money.

Its three sectors can be steered one by one by feedback. The economy is split into the sectors of the basic, the desired, and the luxurious living conditions, with the gaps z_i = D_i - S_i between the demand and the supply of money of each, which the categorized monetary and fiscal policies x_i move through z' = A z + B x, and the indices of the sectors y = C z + D x, from the zero state (Forrest 2018, Eqs. 22.6 and 22.7). The policies of one sector act on all of them. By Theorem 11.3 and Example 11.2 the system can be decoupled by feedback into the systems w' = A w + B_i x_i and y_i = C_i w + D_i x_i of the sectors (Eqs. 22.9 to 22.12), whose market reactions keep each index on its own policy, so money poured into the luxury sector leaves the basic sector alone. The source gives no numbers, so the matrices are illustrative, with a stable A and a stable A - B D^-1 C, and the policies are steps.

The system has the gaps economy.z1 to economy.z3 and, with feedback, the decoupled states economy.w11 to economy.w33. The observables of the system are the indices economy.y1 to economy.y3 and the inputs of the economy economy.u1 to economy.u3.

        label,
        source=households,
        target=firms,
        state='households.deposits',
        into='firms.deposits',
        amount=lambda s: CircuitInteraction._get_consumption(s.households, s.firms),
        flow='consumption',
        legs=[
            ('firms.deposits', 'households.deposits', lambda s: s.firms.wage_share * s.firms.sales, 'wages'),
            ('firms.deposits', 'bank.deposits', lambda s: s.bank.interest * s.firms.loans, 'interest'),

def harvest(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Harvest every occupied patch and share the food among the people on it.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the interaction.
    """
    cells: dict[tuple[int, ...], list[SettlerView]] = {}
    for person in system.get_agents('people', SettlerView):
        cells.setdefault(SettlerElement._get_cell(person), []).append(person)
    for group in cells.values():
        patch = SettlerElement._get_patch_here(group[0])
        labour = sum(person.labour for person in group if person.age >= person.maturity)
        harvest = min(patch.food, max(labour - patch.resistance, 0.0))
        patch.food -= harvest
        for person in group:
            person.food += harvest / len(group)
            person.harvested = harvest / len(group)

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A credit market where firms sample banks and switch to cheaper lenders.

Defaults hit the lenders. Every step the banks quote rates that fall with their equity, every firm samples sample banks and switches from its lender to the cheapest of them with probability 1 - exp(intensity * (r_new - r_old) / r_new), borrows, and invests at a random return. Interest and write-offs of defaulted firms move net worth between firms and banks, so the total net worth changes only by the firms' returns and the entrants' net worth. A higher intensity of switching concentrates the loans in the cheapest banks and narrows the spread of the rates that firms pay.

The system has the groups firms and banks, the market credit with its reporter credit.spread, and the observables herfindahl, largest_share, bank_equity, firm_worth, returns, injected, defaults, and bad_debt.

def count(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Count the births and deaths of the step and remove the dead.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the interaction.
    """
    people = system.get_agents('people', SettlerView)
    living = [person for person in people if person.fate == ALIVE]
    dead = [person for person in people if person.fate != ALIVE]
    system.report('births', float(sum(person.age == 0 for person in living)))
    system.report('starvations', float(sum(person.fate == STARVED for person in dead)))
    system.report('old_age', float(sum(person.fate == AGED for person in dead)))
    for person in dead:
        self._settle(person, living, system)

Bases: BaseSystem

Hamill and Gilbert's staged adjustment of trade and the exchange rate.

The adjustment follows a rise in home prices. The economy starts in balance at the exchange rate E = M * PW / (X * PH), in units of World currency per unit of Home currency, with the export and import volumes and prices of the United Kingdom in 1999 by default. Home prices rise by inflation at the first stage. At every stage a floating rate takes the value that balances the currency market at the current volumes, a fixed rate stays, and the volumes respond to the prices of the stage before with constant price elasticities. The book follows two stages, the default.

The system has the economy home, the balance of trade at home prices balance, the real exchange rate real_rate, and the output output.

@staticmethod
def get_return(agent: FirmView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the return on the net worth and the loan invested.

    The rate of return is normal and at least -1.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

        system:
            The system view of the investment.

    Returns:
        gross_return:
            The return of the step.
    """
    draw = agent.mean_return + agent.volatility * system.rng.standard_normal()
    return (agent.net_worth + agent.loan) * max(draw, -1.0)

def get_worth(agent: FirmView) -> float:

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Customers and banks whose lending of excess reserves multiplies the base money.

The multiplier is 1 / ratio. The base money starts as equal deposits of the customers, held as reserves by their banks, picked at random. Every step the customers pay a share of their deposits to random customers and repay a share of their loans from their deposits, and every bank lends its reserves above the required share of its deposits. The loans are spent and redeposited at random banks. The reserves stay equal to the base money, so the broad money, the sum of deposits, settles near base_money / ratio. A regulator changes the reserve ratio to new_ratio at change_at, and the broad money moves to the new multiplier.

The system has the groups customers and banks, the institution regulator, and the observables broad_money, reserves, and loans.

Bases: Element

Firm of the toy business-cycle system.

It invests a share of its last profit and sells at a random price. Every period the firm invests I = gamma * Z, accumulates capital K = K + I, produces Y = phi * K, borrows B = max(K - A, 0), sells at the price P = pbar + 2 U(0, 1), earns Z = P * Y - r * K, and adds the profit to its net worth A. @staticmethod
def get_steps() -> tuple[tuple[str, str, Callable[[InvestingFirmView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the steps of a period in their order.

    Each is a label, a state, and the function of its next value. A firm invests, produces, borrows, sells, earns,
    adds the profit to its net worth, and, when the net worth turns negative, is replaced by an entrant, whose
    profit, capital, and net worth the last three steps reset.

    Returns:
        steps:
            The label of every step, the state it sets, and the function of its next value of the firm and the
            system view.
    """
    return (
        ('investment', 'K', lambda agent, system: agent.K + agent.gamma * agent.Z),
        ('production', 'Y', lambda agent, system: agent.phi * agent.K),
        ('borrowing', 'B', lambda agent, system: max(agent.K - agent.A, 0.0)),
        ('pricing', 'P', InvestingFirmElement.get_price),
        ('profit', 'Z', lambda agent, system: agent.P * agent.Y - agent.r * agent.K),
        ('accumulation', 'A', lambda agent, system: agent.A + agent.Z),
        ('entry_profit', 'Z', lambda agent, system: 0.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.Z),
        ('entry_capital', 'K', lambda agent, system: 1.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.K),
        ('entry_worth', 'A', lambda agent, system: 1.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.A),
    )

docs.title: LenderElement(label, visual=None, *, equity=100.0, ask=0.0, supply=0.0, lent=0.0, losses=0.0, alpha=0.1, capital_ratio=0.1)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

Bank that lends up to a multiple of its equity.

Its rate falls with its equity. The bank asks the rate alpha * equity ** -alpha of Delli Gatti et al. @staticmethod
def get_income(agent: LenderView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the interest a bank earns in the step.

    It is less what its defaulting borrowers cannot repay.

    Args:
        agent:
            The bank.

        system:
            The system view of the settlement.

    Returns:
        income:
            The change of the equity.
    """
    borrowers = LenderElement._get_borrowers(agent, system)
    return sum(firm.loan * firm.rate + min(FirmElement.get_worth(firm), 0.0) for firm in borrowers)

@staticmethod
def get_quote() -> tuple[tuple[str, Callable[[LenderView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the states a bank sets in the plan of a step.

    They are its rate and lending capacity from its equity.

    Returns:
        quote:
            The name of every state and the function of its value, of the bank and the system view.
    """
    return (
        ('ask', lambda agent, system: agent.alpha * max(agent.equity, 1e-6) ** -agent.alpha),
        ('supply', lambda agent, system: max(agent.equity, 0.0) / agent.capital_ratio),
        ('lent', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
        ('losses', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
    )

Bases: PolicyRuleInteraction[SystemView]

Representative household and bank of the Mark-0 economy.

They run the firms through one month every step. Every step the firms adjust their workforce, prices, and wages by the rules of thumb of Mark-0 (Eqs. 11 to 17 of Sharma et al. 2020) from the demand and the profit of the last month, pay their wages, and sell to the household, whose consumption budget c (S + W + rho_d S) (Eq. 5) splits among the firms by the logit demand of their prices relative to the mean price (Eq. 9). Firms pay interest and, when profitable with positive cash, a share delta of their cash as dividends (Eqs. 18 and 19). A firm whose debt to payroll Phi = -E / (W N) reaches the bankruptcy threshold Theta defaults, its debt falls on the bank, which moves the loan and deposit rates (Eqs. 21 and 22), and a bankrupt firm is revived with probability phi per month at the mean price and wage. Following the simplifications of the source, inflation expectations, the feedback of inflation on consumption, the effect of fragility on hiring, and the central bank are switched off, so the base rate is zero.

During the shock, from shock_time for shock_length months, the productivity falls by the share dzeta and the consumption propensity by the share dc. The credit policy 'naive' lifts the threshold during the shock and restores it at once after it, and 'adaptive' restores it to max(offset <Phi>, Theta) with the production-weighted mean fragility <Phi> (Eq. 24). At the end of the shock the household's savings are multiplied by kappa, the helicopter money.

def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Run one month of the economy.

    It adjusts, pays, sells, distributes, defaults, revives, and sets the rates.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the economy.
    """
    firms = sorted(system.get_agents('firms', Mark0FirmView), key=lambda firm: firm.id)
    names = ('workforce', 'demand', 'price', 'wage', 'cash', 'profit', 'active')
    keys = ('n', 'd', 'p', 'w', 'e', 'profit', 'active')
    state = {key: np.array([getattr(firm, name) for firm in firms]) for key, name in zip(keys, names, strict=True)}
    store = system.storage
    month = int(self._get_stored(system, 'month', 0.0))
    savings, inflation_ema = self._get_stored(system, 'savings', 0.0), self._get_stored(
        system,
        'inflation_ema',
        0.0,
    )
    rho_l, rho_d = self._get_stored(system, 'rho_l', 0.0), self._get_stored(system, 'rho_d', 0.0)
    start, length = system.get_parameter('shock_time'), system.get_parameter('shock_length')
    shocked = start <= month < start + length
    zeta = system.get_parameter('zeta') * (1 - system.get_parameter('dzeta') * shocked)
    c = system.get_parameter('c0') * (1 - system.get_parameter('dc') * shocked)
    if length > 0 and month == start + length:
        savings *= system.get_parameter('kappa')
    size = len(firms)
    if month > 0:
        state['sales'] = np.asarray(store['sales'])
        state['interest'] = np.asarray(store['interest'])
        self._adjust(system, state, zeta, 1 - state['n'].sum() / size)
    active = state['active'] > 0
    production = zeta * state['n']
    bill = state['w'] * state['n']
    wages = float(bill.sum())
    state['e'] = state['e'] - bill
    mean_price = self._get_weighted(state['p'][active], production[active])
    mean_wage = self._get_weighted(state['w'][active], production[active])
    budget = c * (savings + wages + rho_d * savings)
    weights = np.where(active, np.exp(-system.get_parameter('beta') * state['p'] / mean_price), 0.0)
    state['d'] = budget * weights / (state['p'] * weights.sum())
    sales = state['p'] * np.minimum(production, state['d'])
    interest = rho_d * np.maximum(state['e'], 0.0) + rho_l * np.minimum(state['e'], 0.0)
    state['e'] = state['e'] + sales + interest
    state['profit'] = sales - bill + interest
    savings += wages + rho_d * savings - float(sales.sum())
    dividends = np.where((state['profit'] > 0) & (state['e'] > 0), system.get_parameter('delta') * state['e'], 0.0)
    state['e'] -= dividends
    savings += float(dividends.sum())
    fragility_of = np.divide(-state['e'], bill, out=np.zeros(size), where=bill > 0)
    fragility = self._get_weighted(fragility_of[active], production[active])
    threshold = self._get_threshold(system, month, fragility)
    defaulted = active & (fragility_of >= threshold)
    losses = float(-state['e'][defaulted].sum())
    for key in ('n', 'd', 'e', 'profit', 'active'):
        state[key] = np.where(defaulted, 0.0, state[key])
    unemployment = 1 - state['n'].sum() / size
    revived = (state['active'] == 0) & ~defaulted & (system.rng.random(size) < system.get_parameter('phi'))
    start_size = unemployment * system.rng.random(size)
    state['n'] = np.where(revived, start_size, state['n'])
    state['p'] = np.where(revived, mean_price, state['p'])
    state['w'] = np.where(revived, mean_wage, state['w'])
    state['active'] = np.where(revived, 1.0, state['active'])
    previous = self._get_stored(system, 'price', mean_price)
    inflation = (mean_price - previous) / previous
    inflation_ema = system.get_parameter('omega') * inflation + (1 - system.get_parameter('omega')) * inflation_ema
    debts, deposits = float(-np.minimum(state['e'], 0.0).sum()), float(np.maximum(state['e'], 0.0).sum())
    f = system.get_parameter('f')
    rho_l = f * losses / debts if debts > 0 else 0.0
    rho_d = -(1 - f) * losses / (savings + deposits) if savings + deposits > 0 else 0.0
    store.update(
        month=month + 1,
        savings=savings,
        inflation_ema=inflation_ema,
        rho_l=rho_l,
        rho_d=rho_d,
        price=mean_price,
        sales=np.where(defaulted, 0.0, sales),
        interest=np.where(defaulted, 0.0, interest),
    )
    for index, firm in enumerate(firms):
        for key, name in zip(keys, names, strict=True):
            setattr(firm, name, float(state[key][index]))
    reported = {
        'unemployment': 1 - state['n'].sum() / size,
        'inflation': inflation,
        'output': float((zeta * state['n']).sum()),
        'savings': savings,
        'fragility': fragility,
        'bankruptcies': float(defaulted.sum()),
        'threshold': min(threshold, 1e9),
        'price': mean_price,
        'wage': mean_wage,
    }
    for name, value in reported.items():
        system.report(name, value)

Bases: BaseSystem

The Mark-0 economy of Sharma, Bouchaud, and co-authors.

It has a Covid shock to supply and demand. Firms produce perishable goods with a linear technology, sell them to a representative household at prices they adjust by rules of thumb, hire and fire by the gap between production and demand, and borrow from a representative bank, defaulting when their debt to payroll exceeds the threshold Theta (Sharma et al. 2020, Section 2). A month is a step, the money starts at zero, and the economy is stock-flow consistent apart from the written-off debts and the helicopter money. With the defaults of Table 1 the economy sits in the full employment phase. A lockdown lowers the productivity and the consumption propensity for shock_length months, after which a mild shock recovers in a V shape and a strong one tips the economy into an L-shaped recession of high unemployment, which easy credit and helicopter money can prevent. The source summarizes the model of earlier papers, so the initial firms (a workforce between 0.9 and 1, prices around 1, unit wages, no cash) and revived firms (the mean price and wage and a random share of the unemployed) follow Gualdi et al. (2015), and the demand reads prices relative to the mean price.

The system has the group firms and the economy economy, whose reporters are economy.unemployment, economy.inflation, economy.output, economy.savings, economy.fragility, economy.bankruptcies, economy.threshold, economy.price, and economy.wage.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Gooding's Metaphoria.

It is a mortal population of hunter-gatherers or of a monetary economy. Patches of a periodic lattice hold food that grows back to a random capacity and resist harvesting with a random resistance. People need food every step, age, die of starvation or old age, and have children who inherit their propensities to breed, explore, found firms, and quit jobs, with mutations, so the propensities evolve under the test of survival. Hunter-gatherers pool the labour of the adults on a patch and share the harvest. In the monetary economy firms harvest with paid workers, sell the food in shops, and borrow the wages from a bank that creates money as loans, so the money of all holders sums to zero at every step. Gooding found the hunter-gatherers stable, and the monetary population smaller and less healthy, with money concentrating to a Gini coefficient near 0.5. On land where the hunter-gatherers thrive the monetary population dwindles towards extinction, and with abundant food it lives on with persistent starvation.

The system has the group patches, one per cell, the variable group people, the reporters census.births, census.starvations, and census.old_age, and the observables population and money_gini. The monetary economy adds the variable group businesses, the group bank, and the reporter shops.gdp.

docs.title: NetworkHerdingSystem(theta=None, x=None, *, gamma=1.0, sigma=0.1, n_agents=50, density=0.1, herding=0.5, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Agents whose linear choices herd on the past choices of linked agents.

They herd on the agents they are linked to. The choice of agent i is c_it = sum_j theta_ij c_j,t-1 + gamma x_it, so the choices follow c_t = Theta c_t-1 + gamma x_t on the weighted network Theta, without self-links, Eqs. 1.10 and 1.11 of Caiani et al. (2016, Section 1.1.6). The individual characteristic is x_it = x_i + sigma eps_it, with a standard normal shock eps_it. The mean choice follows c_t = (1/N) sum_i d_i c_i,t-1 + gamma x_t (Eq. 1.12), where the out-degree d_i of agent i, the sum of column i of Theta, measures how much its choice moves the others, so the persistence of the aggregate depends on the out-degrees and on how they correlate with the choices. Without shocks the choices settle at (I - Theta)^-1 gamma x when the spectral radius of Theta is below 1.

The system has the group agents of the choices agents.c and the herding herding. The observable of the system is the mean choice mean_choice.

def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Set the reserve ratio of the banks from the schedule.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the regulator.
    """
    before = system.time < system.get_parameter('change_at')
    ratio = system.get_parameter('ratio') if before else system.get_parameter('new_ratio')
    name = f'{self.banks}.reserve_ratio'
    if system.parameters[name] != ratio:
        system.set_parameter(name, ratio)

docs.text:
Bases: DeclaredElement

National economy of three spending sectors, with sector policies.

It follows z' = A z + B u and y = C z + D u. The state z_i is the gap between the demand and the supply of money of sector i, the basic, the desired, and the luxurious living conditions, the output y_i is the index of the sector, and the policy x_i of a sector is a step of size policy_i at the time policy_time_i. Without feedback the economy takes the policies as its inputs, u = x. With feedback, the market reactions of Forrest's feedback component set u so that every sector responds to its own policy only, as the decoupled systems w_i' = A w_i + B_i x_i and y_i = C_i w_i + D_i x_i, whose states w_ik the element holds. The feedback component holds a copy of z that equals z from the common zero start, so u = D^-1 (y - C z) with the decoupled outputs y.
