docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A slow-fast circuit with a cubic flux-controlled memristor.

Its oscillations mix two amplitudes. The memristor has the charge q = a w + b w^3 of its flux w, and with the voltage x of the memristor, the current y of the inductor, and the voltage z of the second capacitor, the circuit follows epsilon x' = -y - (a + 3 b w^2) x, y' = alpha (x - R y - z + e), z' = -β y, and w' = x. Trzaska prints the memductance as a + 3 b w, but only the derivative a + 3 b w^2 of the characteristic gives the response he reports: for the defaults, from rest, the voltage settles on the mixed-mode oscillation 2^11, two large spikes and eleven small oscillations in a period of about 7.9, against the 7.816 he reports. The spikes last about a hundredth of the period, so the tuned solver runs at the relative tolerance 1e-8, below which looser runs drift to an irregular pattern of shorter periods.

The system has the states circuit.x, circuit.y, circuit.z, and circuit.w.

docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A tunnel-diode oscillator.

It is an inductor and a capacitor in parallel with a negative-resistance diode. The diode current is h(V) = gamma V^3 - alpha V, so Kirchhoff's laws give C V' = -h(V) - i and L i' = V, which is the van der Pol oscillator with ε = alpha sqrt(L / C). The voltage settles on a limit cycle of amplitude near 2 sqrt(alpha / (3 gamma)). The system has the voltage circuit.V and the inductor current circuit.i.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A dual-mass piezoelectric harvester in a car suspension.

The roughness of the road drives it. The unsprung and sprung masses follow m1 y1'' + b (y1' - y2') + k2 (y1 - y2) + k1 (y1 - z(t)) = 0 and m2 y2'' + b (y2' - y1') + k2 (y2 - y1) = 0, with the road profile z(t) = A sin(ω t). A lever with arm ratio n presses a piezoelectric bar of constant d and capacitance C, whose charge is n d k2 (y2 - y1) and whose voltage is the observable voltage. The damper b stands for the energy the bar absorbs. The system has the displacements harvester.y1 and harvester.y2, and the observable voltage.

docs.title: SpringDamperInteraction(label, *, target, states=('x1', 'x2'), stiffness='k', damping='b', divisor=None)
docs.text:
Bases: GradientInteraction

Linear spring and damper between two coordinates x1 and x2 of one element.

The coordinates have order 2. The spring is the gradient of the energy k (x1 - x2)^2 / 2, and the damper adds -b (x1' - x2') to the first coordinate and its opposite to the second, both divided by the divisor of every coordinate, such as its own mass. The stiffness and the damping are named parameters of the element.

docs.text:
Bases: CrossingInteraction

Pulses that set states of the target to new values at given or periodic times.

Engineering names them pulses or impulses, as the kicks of a sampled controller or of a pulsed circuit. The pulses fall at every time of times and, with a period, at start + j * period for j from 0, count times or without end. A pulse at the initial time of a run does not fire. The new values are functions of the namespace, which holds namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t. A pulse sets the states of every member of a group at once, and the trajectory records every pulse among its events, under the label of the interaction.

docs.text:
Bases: RateInteraction

Adaptation of a speed or a flow towards a desired one over an adaptation time.

Traffic engineering names it the speed adaptation of a driver, as in the optimal velocity and Payne-Whitham models. The rate is (goal(ns) - x) / time(ns) of a state x of a target, with optional noise. With a constant goal and time and an additive noise of amplitude sigma, the state follows the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx = (goal - x) / time dt + sigma dW, whose stationary variance is sigma**2 time / 2. A goal or a time function takes the namespace of the interaction, as for RateInteraction, and a number stands for a constant. A goal that is a number applies to every component of a vector state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target str

The path of the element or group whose state relaxes.

required state str

The name of the state of the target that relaxes.

'x' goal Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float

A function of the namespace that returns the goal, or a number.

0.0 time Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float

A function of the namespace that returns the relaxation time, or a positive number.

1.0 noise Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None

A function of the namespace that returns the amplitude of the noise, a number, or None for no noise.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The state is not a name, or a function is neither callable nor a number.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.elements import NonnegativeElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.systems.engineering.common.traffic import SpeedAdaptationInteraction
>>> relaxation = SpeedAdaptationInteraction('relaxation', target='stock', goal=10.0, time=0.5)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[NonnegativeElement('stock')], interactions=[relaxation])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=5.0, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('stock.x')[-1]), 3)
10.0

docs.title: BangBangPlantElement(label, visual=None, *, x=0.0, y=0.0, u=1.0, a=0.0)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

Second-order linear plant under a bang-bang control.

The control is held between samples, and it steers the plant to the origin. The plant follows x' = y and y' = a x + u with the control u of size 1, a = 0 for a free particle, a = -1 for a harmonic oscillator, and a = 1 for a saddle. The control stays constant between samples, and at every sample takes -1 above the switching curve y = g(x) of the plant and 1 below it. The curve is made of the two trajectories of the plant under u = 1 and u = -1 that reach the origin: g(x) = -sign(x) sqrt(2 |x|) for the free particle, the half circles g(x) = sqrt(1 - (x + 1)^2) on [-2, 0] and -sqrt(1 - (x - 1)^2) on [0, 2], and 0 outside, for the harmonic oscillator, and g(x) = sqrt(x^2 - 2 x) for x <= 0 and -sqrt(x^2 + 2 x) for x >= 0 for the saddle.

Parameters:

Bases: Element

Inverted pendulum on a cart that a bounded horizontal force pushes.

It follows Åström and Murray. The cart of mass M at position x carries a point mass m at the end of a rod of length l, at the angle theta from upright, positive towards negative x. The equations of motion are (M + m) x'' - m l theta'' cos(theta) + m l theta'^2 sin(theta) = force and l theta'' - x'' cos(theta) = g sin(theta), so upright is unstable and a positive force tilts the pendulum back from a positive angle.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A room assembled from thermal and electrical components.

It is heated under a thermostat with hysteresis. A voltage source drives a heating resistor whose heat enters the room, and the room loses heat through a wall of its own heat capacity to the outside air. The thermostat opens the switch of the resistor when the room rises through setting + band / 2 and closes it when the room falls through setting - band / 2. docs.title: KoopmanModelPredictiveControlSystem(plant='duffing', *, controlled=True, dictionary=None, x=0.5, y=0.0, n_runs=100, duration=1000, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A plant that a discrete-time controller steers with model predictive control.

The control runs on a fitted surrogate. The system runs the plant under a random binary input at the limits of its range, drawn every sample, and fits mode_decomposition with the input to the runs. The controller lifts the states with the dictionary, condenses the quadratic tracking cost over the horizon with the matrices of the surrogate, solves the bounded least squares problem with scipy.optimize.lsq_linear, and sets the input to the first value of the solution. The plant reads the input through a role, and CoSimulationSolver holds it between samples. The plants are those of figure 6.6 of the review of Brunton et al.: the forced Duffing oscillator x'' = a x + b x^3 + d x' + f cos(w t) + (3 + cos(x)) u, the Van der Pol oscillator x'' = -x - mu (x^2 - 1) x' + u, and the bilinear DC motor, whose second variable is the output that tracks the reference. The motor reads four times the input, as Korda and Mezić scale it. One time unit of the system is one sample of the controller.

The system has the variables plant/state.x and plant/state.y, the input controller/input.u, and the observable reference.

docs.title: MinimumTimeControlSystem(x=3.0, v=2.0, *, plant='free_particle', interval=0.1, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A linear plant steered to the origin of its phase space in minimum time.

A sampled bang-bang control steers it. The plant follows x'' = a x + u with |u| <= 1: a free particle, x'' = u, a harmonic oscillator, x'' + x = u, or an unstable saddle, x'' - x = u. Pontryagin's maximum principle makes the minimum-time control bang-bang, u = ±1, with the switch on the curve of the two trajectories under u = 1 and u = -1 that reach the origin: the control is -1 above the curve and 1 below it. As in Dilão's examples, the controller samples the position and the velocity every interval and holds the control until the next sample, so the plant reaches a neighbourhood of the origin, whose size shrinks with the interval, and stays there. A free particle from (x, v) above the curve reaches the origin at the time v + 2 sqrt(x + v^2 / 2), about 6.47 for the defaults. Only the states between the lines y = -(x + 1) and y = -(x - 1) of the saddle are controllable, and from the others the plant escapes to infinity.

The system has the position plant.x, the velocity plant.y, and the control plant.u, which the samples sample set.

docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A satellite moved between Kepler orbits by radial thrust.

The orbits have equal angular momentum. In normalised polar coordinates the satellite follows s'' = L_z^2 / s^3 - 1 / s^2 - ε sigma and θ' = L_z / s^2. From the periapsis of the orbit with H = -0.7, the transfer to H = -0.2 takes about 9.81.

The system has the distance satellite.s, the radial velocity satellite.s_d1, the angle satellite.theta, and the observable energy.

Bases: DynamicalSystem

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A conductive ball levitated in a vacuum by a field.

The field pushes and pulls it with alternating impulses. The velocity follows v' + b v = m Σ_k [δ(t + 1 - 4 k) - δ(t - 1 - 4 k)]: it relaxes freely, rises by m at the times 4 k - 1, and falls by m at the times 4 k + 1. Its periodic solution, with the triangular wave τ(t) = (2 / π) arcsin(sin(π t / 2)) and the rectangular wave e(t) = sign(cos(π t / 2)), is v = m / (2 cosh b) exp(-b τ(t) e(t)) e(t), which the ball follows from the start when it starts at m / (2 cosh b). The system has the velocity ball.v, raised by the impulses push and lowered by the impulses pull.

Bases: DynamicalSystem

An electromagnetic vibrating table, a shaker driven by a sinusoidal supply.

The supply drives it after its switch closes. The source u = U sin(omega t) feeds a resistor and a capacitor, whose voltage drives the current i2 of the coil of an electromagnet against the back electromotive force k1 v of the table. The electromagnet pulls the table, held by a spring and a damper, with the force g(i2) = k2 tan(alpha i2) / alpha, whose slope k2 at zero current is the one of Trzaska's linearized model. From rest, a transient of about 8 s dies out and the table vibrates steadily at the supply frequency, and the linearized model, g(i2) = k2 i2, gives nearly the same response since the current stays small.

The system has the current shaker.i2, the capacitor voltage shaker.uC, the displacement shaker.x, and the velocity shaker.v.

docs.title: FaradayDiskSystem(I=0.0, U=0.0, omega=0.0, *, B=1.5, M=4.8, N=250.0, R1=2.3, R2=109.0, L=0.2, C=0.75, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A battery charger driven by a Faraday disk generator.

The own current of the generator strengthens its field. A motor turns the conducting disk of radii r1 and r2 with a constant torque M in the field B of a magnet plus the field μ N I / l of a coil that the generated current flows through. With a = B (r2^2 - r1^2) / 2 and b = μ N (r2^2 - r1^2) / (2 l), the current, the polarization voltage of the battery, and the angular speed follow L I' = -R1 I - U + (a + b I) ω - E(I), C U' = I - U / R2, and J ω' = M - alpha sign(ω) - β r2 ω - (a + b I) I, where the battery voltage is E(I) = a0 + a1 I + a3 I^3 and the last term is the braking torque of the Lorentz force.

The generator charges the battery only when its voltage a ω exceeds the open-circuit voltage a0 = 8 of the battery, at ω above 35 for the default field. Below that speed the steady current is a small negative current, the battery discharges through the disk and helps the motor, and the steady speed grows linearly with the torque, as (M - alpha) / (β r2) up to the small Lorentz torque: with the defaults the current settles at -0.040 and the speed at 15.7. The coil acts as a negative resistance b ω against R1 + a1, so above ω = (R1 + a1) / b, about 32 or a torque near 9.5 for the defaults, the steady state loses its stability and the current oscillates around zero, swinging between charging and discharging, while the mean braking torque b <I²> bends the speed below the linear trend. A stronger magnet charges at the default torque: B = 4 gives a steady current of 0.013.

The system has the current charger.I, the polarization voltage charger.U, and the angular speed charger.omega.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A ring power grid in the swing-equation system.

More transmission capacity can break synchrony. The phase of node i relative to the grid frequency follows phi_i'' = P_i - gamma phi_i' + Σ_j K_ij sin(phi_j - phi_i). The first half of the ring are generators with P = power and the second half consumers with P = -power, joined by lines of capacity K. The default grid synchronises, but adding the line (0, 2) or doubling the capacity of the line (0, 1) makes the flows overload a line, and synchrony is lost, which is Braess's paradox. The system has the phases node_<i>.phi and frequency deviations node_<i>.phi_d1.

docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A car braked by a Faraday disk generator on its wheel.

The generator charges a supercapacitor.

The disk generates the voltage A v, with the structural constant A = |B| R^2 / (2 r_w) of the disk and the wheel, and drives the current through an inductor and a resistor into a supercapacitor, L I' = A v - R I - V_s and C V_s' = I. The current brakes the car with the force A I, together with dry and viscous friction, m v' = -A I - alpha sign(v) - β v, so the kinetic energy of the car ends up in the capacitor and in the losses. The system has the speed car.v, the current car.I, and the capacitor voltage car.Vs.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A cascade classifier, a column of stages that separates particles.

An air flow separates them. The particles separated are of a narrow size class. Material leaves every stage at unit rate, a fraction k upwards and 1 - k downwards. The top stage releases into the fine product and the bottom stage into the coarse product. Material of one size class is fed into one stage at a constant rate. At steady state the share of the feed that ends in the fine product is F_f = (1 - ((1 - k) / k)^(z + 1 - i)) / (1 - ((1 - k) / k)^(z + 1)) for z stages and feeding at stage i counted from the top, Barsky's fractional extraction.

The system has the material stage_<i>.m of each stage from the top, and the accumulated products fine.m and coarse.m.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A food relief system.

A pipeline ships food to a warehouse and distributes it to people in need. A disaster at onset leaves affected people who need a daily ration. The relief agency ships food at the need plus corrections that close the gaps between the warehouse stock and its desired cover of the need, and between the food in transit and the need over the shipping delay. Shipped food enters the pipeline and arrives at the warehouse through a third-order material delay. The warehouse distributes the need while its stock lasts. Food is conserved, so almost nothing reaches the people in the first days after the disaster, and the gap closes as the pipeline fills. The structure follows the relief food example of Bala, Arshad and Noh (2017, Section 4.11), with illustrative parameters in tonnes and days.

The system has the food stocks relief.in_transit and relief.warehouse in tonnes, and the flows relief.shipping, relief.arrivals, and relief.distribution in tonnes per day, over days. The observables of the system are relief.need and relief.shipments.

Its orders through a supply line make the stock oscillate. docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

An irrigation system.

A reservoir and an aquifer keep the root zone of the crops supplied. A river fills the reservoir with a yearly cycle, and the reservoir loses water to evaporation and spills above its capacity. The irrigation demand is the potential crop evapotranspiration plus the refill of the root zone towards a target fraction of its field capacity. The reservoir releases the demand grossed up for the canal losses, as far as its stock allows, and the losses seep into the aquifer. When the release falls short, the farmers pump the unmet demand from the aquifer up to the pump capacity. The crops draw water from the root zone at the potential rate scaled by a water-stress table, and the root zone percolates to the aquifer, which drains as baseflow. Water is conserved, so in the dry season the reservoir falls, the pumping rises, and the aquifer is drawn down. The structure follows the irrigation example of Bala, Arshad and Noh (2017, Section 4.11), with illustrative parameters in millions of cubic metres and days.

The system has the water stocks scheme.reservoir, scheme.soil, and scheme.groundwater, and the flows scheme.inflow, scheme.evaporation, scheme.spill, scheme.irrigation, scheme.seepage, scheme.groundwater_pumping, scheme.crop_water, scheme.percolation, and scheme.baseflow per day, over days. The observables of the system are scheme.demand, scheme.release, and scheme.pumping.

docs.title: RiceMillingSystem(*, harvest=2000.0, seasonality=0.8, procurement_delay=1.0, outturn=0.65, capacity=2000.0, expansion_time=12.0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

A rice milling system.

A mill buys paddy, mills it into rice and by-products, and sells them. Paddy arrives from the farms through a third-order procurement delay, at a rate that follows the harvest season around its mean. The mill processes its paddy stock in a month, as far as its milling capacity allows, and splits the milled paddy by mass into rice, the outturn, husk, bran, and milling losses. Rice, husk, and bran leave their inventories for the market at a fixed coverage. The capacity adjusts to the smoothed indicated milling rate, so in the harvest season the capacity lags and paddy accumulates, and in the lean season the capacity idles. Grain is conserved, every change of the paddy, rice, husk, and bran stocks is a flow, and over a year the milled paddy and the rice sales match the mean harvest and its outturn. The structure follows the rice milling case of Bala, Arshad and Noh (2017), with illustrative parameters in tonnes and months, since the case data are specific to their study.

The system has the grain stocks mill.paddy, mill.rice, mill.husk, and mill.bran in tonnes, the capacity mill.capacity, and the flows mill.paddy_purchases, mill.milled_rice, mill.husk_output, mill.bran_output, mill.milling_losses, mill.rice_sales, mill.husk_sales, and mill.bran_sales in tonnes per month, over months. The observables of the system are mill.procurement, mill.indicated_milling, and mill.milling.

A solid waste system.

The waste of a growing city is collected, recycled, composted, and landfilled. The population grows exponentially and generates waste in proportion to its size. The waste waits uncollected until the collection, limited by a collection capacity that the city expands towards the generation with a delay, removes it. Waste is conserved, so the landfill fills up to its capacity and dumping takes over. docs.title: LightEmittingRobotsSystem(n_robots=50, *, delay=10.0, side=10.0, I0=5.0, r0=1.0, V0=1.0, V_inf=0.1, tau=2.0, step=0.5, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Light-emitting robots that cluster or spread by their sensing of light.

They cluster when they sense the light of the others late and spread when early. Every robot emits a Gaussian light and measures the total light of the others, I_i = sum_j I0 exp(-d_ij^2 / r0^2) over the shortest distances on a periodic square arena. It moves at the speed V_inf + (V0 - V_inf) exp(-I_i(t - delay)) in a direction that diffuses with the time scale tau. A robot with a positive delay crosses a dark region at the fast speed it sensed earlier in the dark and slows down only once it is in the light, so the robots linger near each other and form clusters. A negative delay, a prediction of the light by its trend, makes a robot slow down before it reaches the light and speed up before it leaves it, so the robots avoid each other and spread over the arena. Every step lasts step, so the default run of 400 steps covers 200 s.

The system has the group robots of directions phi, measured lights light, and speeds speed, at positions in the arena.

Bases: BaseSystem

Light-sensitive robots in a circular well.

Their sensory delay decides whether they gather in the light. Each robot moves at V_inf + (V0 - V_inf) exp(-I(t - delay)) in a direction that diffuses with time scale tau, in the Gaussian light I = I0 exp(-(x^2 + y^2) / r0^2) at the centre of a well of radius R. The robots start at the centre, in directions spread around the circle, and do not interact. A positive delay drives them out of the light: a robot crosses the light at the fast speed it measured in the dark and lingers outside at the slow speed it measured in the light, so robots with a delay spend less time in the light than robots without one.

The system has the group robots of positions x, y and directions phi.

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Motion of light-emitting robots whose speed follows the light of the others.

The light is sensed with a delay. Every robot emits the Gaussian light I0 exp(-d^2 / r0^2) at the distance d, and measures the total light I_i of the other robots, at the shortest distances on the torus. It moves at the speed V_inf + (V0 - V_inf) exp(-I_i(t - delay)) in its direction, which diffuses with the time scale tau, phi <- phi + sqrt(2 step / tau) w with a standard normal w. A positive delay reads the light measured that long ago, and a negative delay predicts it by the linear extrapolation I(t) - delay I'(t), never below 0. Before the delay has passed, a robot uses the earliest light it measured. Every step of the rule lasts step.

docs.text:
Bases: Element

Robot of the swarmtaxis algorithm.

It keeps in radio contact with the swarm and avoids its neighbours. Every step the robot counts the robots within its radio range. When it loses a connection and has fewer than alpha connections, it turns around to stay with the swarm, and when it gains one it turns at random. A robot closer than its avoidance radius to another turns away from it. A robot is shadowed when another robot lies between it and the beacon, within the radio range and shadow_angle of the bearing to the beacon, and it is illuminated otherwise. Illuminated robots avoid at a larger radius than shadowed ones, so they move away from the swarm towards the beacon, and the swarm follows. The robot then moves forward at its speed.

def move(self, agent: SwarmRobotView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Update the connections, the shadow, and the heading, and move forward.

    Args:
        agent:
            The robot.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    neighbors = agent.get_neighbors(agent.radio_range)
    count = len(neighbors)
    agent.illuminated = 0.0 if self._is_shadowed(agent, neighbors) else 1.0
    heading = self._avoid(agent, neighbors, self._turn(agent, system, count))
    agent.connections = count
    agent.heading = heading % (2 * math.pi)
    x, y = SwarmRobotElement._get_position(agent)
    edge = agent.arena * (1 - EDGE_FRACTION)
    x = min(max(x + agent.speed * math.cos(heading), 0.0), edge)
    y = min(max(y + agent.speed * math.sin(heading), 0.0), edge)
    agent.move_to((x, y))

def drive(self, agent: CabView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Drive one block toward the target, and pick up or drop off the rider there.

    Args:
        agent:
            The cab.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    if agent.task == IDLE:
        return
    x, y = CabElement._get_cell(agent.location)
    target = (int(agent.target_x), int(agent.target_y))
    if (x, y) != target:
        step = (int(np.sign(target[0] - x)), 0) if x != target[0] else (0, int(np.sign(target[1] - y)))
        agent.move_to((x + step[0], y + step[1]))
    if CabElement._get_cell(agent.location) != target:
        return
    if agent.task == PICKING_UP:
        self._pick_up(agent, system)
    else:
        agent.task = IDLE
        agent.seats = 1.0

def drive(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Make a random driver brake, then move every car.

    The driver brakes with the interaction's probability.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    cars = sorted(system.get_agents('cars', MotoristView), key=lambda car: car.rank)
    if not cars:
        return
    if system.rng.random() < system.get_parameter('probability'):
        careless = cars[int(system.rng.integers(len(cars)))]
        careless.v = max(careless.v - careless.braking, 0.0)
    gap = system.get_parameter('gap')
    positions = [car.x for car in cars]
    for index, car in enumerate(cars):
        moved = car.x + car.v
        car.x = min(moved, positions[index + 1] - gap) if index + 1 < len(cars) else moved

def drive(self, agent: DriverView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Choose the speed from the distance to the car ahead and move along the ring.

    Args:
        agent:
            The driver.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    cars = system.get_agents(agent.group, DriverView)
    if system.dimensions is None:
        error_msg = 'Drivers move along a ring road, a continuous space with an extent.'
        raise SimulationError(error_msg)
    length = system.dimensions[0]
    ahead = DriverElement._get_car_ahead(agent, system, len(cars))
    x, y = DriverElement._get_position(agent)
    distance = (DriverElement._get_position(ahead)[0] - x) % length if ahead is not None else length
    acceleration = min(max(agent.acceleration, agent.min_acc), agent.max_acc)
    speed = (agent.speed + acceleration) * system.rng.uniform(1 - agent.eps, 1 + agent.eps)
    speed = min(max(speed, 0.0), agent.speed_limit)
    agent.speed = 0.0 if speed > distance else speed
    agent.move_to(((x + agent.speed) % length, y))

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The gas-kinetic-based traffic system.

Drivers brake on the traffic at an interaction point ahead. The density and the flow Q = rho V on a ring road follow rho_t + Q_x = 0 and Q_t + (Q**2 / rho + rho A(rho) V**2)_x = rho (Ve* - V) / tau, where the dynamic equilibrium speed

Ve* = V0 (1 - (theta + theta_a) / (2 A(rho_max)) (rho_a T / (1 - rho_a / rho_max))**2 B(dV))

reads the density rho_a and the speed V_a at the interaction point x + gamma (1 / rho_max + T V), with the variances theta = A(rho) V**2, the variance prefactor A(rho) = A0 + dA (tanh((rho - rho_c) / d_rho) + 1), the dimensionless speed difference dV = (V - V_a) / sqrt(theta + theta_a), and the Boltzmann factor B(d) = 2 (d phi(d) + (1 + d**2) Phi(d)) of the standard normal density phi and distribution Phi. Lengths are in kilometres and times in hours, and the defaults are the calibrated values of Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing. The flow starts in equilibrium with their dipole perturbation of the density, of height amplitude. Homogeneous traffic is unstable between about 24 and 51 vehicles per kilometre, where the perturbation grows into stop-and-go waves whose downstream fronts move against the traffic.

The system has the density road.rho and the flow road.Q.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Cars on a ring road whose speeds relax with noise towards a desired speed.

The local density sets the desired speed. Car i follows dv_i = -gamma (v_i - u(rho_i)) dt + sqrt(2 D(rho_i)) dW with the desired speed u(rho) = u0 (1 - rho / rho_max) and the noise intensity D(rho) = D1 rho, where the local density rho_i is the inverse of the headway to the car ahead. Cars start evenly spaced at the speed u(rho) of the mean density rho = n_cars / length. The mean speed stays at u(rho), so the mean flow follows the fundamental diagram rho u(rho), and the speeds fluctuate with the variance D1 rho / gamma. The uniform flow is linearly stable while u0 rho^2 / rho_max < gamma / 2, as for the optimal velocity system. Strong noise lets cars pass each other, and the headway of a car that has passed the car ahead wraps around the ring.

The system has the group cars of positions cars.x and speeds cars.v, car i + 1 ahead of car i.

docs.title: adjust(agent, system)
docs.text:
Brake when the car ahead is too close and accelerate otherwise.

The car brakes when the car ahead is closer than the safe distance. The lead car, which has no car ahead, keeps its distance to the car behind it instead.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default agent MotoristView

The car.

required system SystemView

The system.

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/engineering/traffic/_drivers.py 
def adjust(self, agent: MotoristView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Brake when the car ahead is too close and accelerate otherwise.

    The car brakes when the car ahead is closer than the safe distance. The lead car, which has no car ahead, keeps
    its distance to the car behind it instead.

    Args:
        agent:
            The car.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    cars = system.get_agents(agent.group, MotoristView)
    ahead = next((car for car in cars if int(car.rank) == int(agent.rank) + 1), None)
    if ahead is None:
        behind = next((car for car in cars if int(car.rank) == int(agent.rank) - 1), None)
        distance = agent.x - behind.x if behind is not None else np.inf
    else:
        distance = ahead.x - agent.x
    change = -agent.braking if distance < agent.safe_distance else agent.acceleration
    agent.v = float(np.clip(agent.v + change, 0.0, agent.speed_limit))

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The optimal velocity system of cars on a ring road.

Uniform flow breaks into stop-and-go waves. Car i relaxes its speed towards the optimal velocity of its headway h, v_i' = a (V(h) - v_i) with V(h) = V0 (tanh(h - hc) + tanh(hc)). Uniform flow with headway b = length / n_cars is unstable when V'(b) > a / 2, and then a jam forms that moves against the direction of travel. The cars are one group, and the headway of car i is the distance along the ring to member i + 1. The system has the group cars of positions cars.x and speeds cars.v, car i + 1 ahead of car i.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The Payne system, where the speed of traffic relaxes to the Greenshields speed.

The speed also anticipates density. The density and the flow q = rho v on a ring road of length 1 follow rho_t + q_x = 0 and q_t + (q^2 / rho + P(rho))_x = (rho V(rho) - q) / τ, with V(rho) = vmax (1 - rho / rho_max) and the anticipation pressure P(rho) = vmax rho / (2 τ rho_max). This is the speed equation v_t + v v_x = (V - v) / τ + V'(rho) rho_x / (2 τ rho) in conservation form. The flow starts in equilibrium with a bump of density. The system has the density road.rho and the flow road.q.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

Riders who request trips on a city grid and cabs sent to them.

A stable matching sends the cabs. Every step new riders appear at random cells with random destinations, and the dispatch matches the waiting riders with the idle cabs by a stable matching in which riders prefer nearer cabs and cabs prefer riders who waited longer. Every cab drives one block a step to its rider, collects the fare, and drives the rider to its destination. While the demand stays below the trips the fleet can serve, riders wait about as long as a cab takes to reach them. As the demand approaches that capacity, every cab is busy, the queue of waiting riders grows, and the waiting time rises steeply, as in a queue near saturation.

The system has the groups riders and cabs, the arrivals arrival, and the matching dispatch.

docs.title: TrafficDensityEquationSystem(n=100, *, length=50.0, density=0.5, gamma=1.0, u0=1.0, rho_max=1.0, D1=0.2, perturbation=0.01, random_state=0, label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem

The density and flux equations of Langevin traffic on a ring road.

Their uniform flow breaks into jams. The density rho and the flux w of cars that relax to the desired speed u(rho) = u0 (1 - rho / rho_max) at the rate gamma, with the diffusion coefficient D(rho) = D1 rho, follow the moment equations rho_t + w_x = (D rho_x)_x and w_t + (2 u w - rho u^2)_x = -gamma (w - rho u) + (D w_x)_x, closed by expanding the velocity distribution around u(rho). A long density wave of the uniform flow grows when the effective diffusion coefficient D(rho) + ((rho u^2)' - (rho u)'^2) / gamma = D(rho) - rho^2 u'(rho)^2 / gamma is negative, so the flow is unstable above the density D1 gamma rho_max^2 / u0^2, and the perturbation grows into dense jams. The uniform density starts with independent Gaussian perturbations of relative size perturbation in every cell, at the flux rho u(rho).

The system has the density road.rho and the flux road.w.

docs.title: BirthDeathInteraction(label, *, target, birth=None, death=None, rate=None, offspring=1, placement='here', inherit=(), split=(), mutate=None, schedule='random-sequential', phase=None, group=None, values=None, keep=None, reset=None, replace=False, renew=False, cull=None, kin=None, arrival=None, pick='first')
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction by which the agents of a group give birth to offspring and die.

At every step of discrete time each agent acts once, by schedule. An agent dies with the probability death. An agent that survives gives birth with the probability birth, or as many times as a Poisson number of mean rate, and every birth creates offspring new agents of group, or of the group of the parent. A probability is a number or a function of the agent and the system view, and a function that returns a condition gives probability one where it holds. The new agents stand where placement says: in the cell of the parent, in a free neighbouring cell, or where a function returns.

A new agent copies the states inherit of its parent, takes the values that values(parent, system) returns, and shares the states split with its parent, which keeps the share keep. Then mutate may change its values. Further options reset or replace the parent, renew a dying agent in place, cull a member of a kin group, and add arrivals without a parent, as their arguments describe. The process reports the births, deaths, and arrivals of every step.

Unlike JumpInteraction, which changes numeric states of a fixed set of members, it adds and removes agents, each with states of its own. Choose it when a population of individuals grows, shrinks, and passes traits to offspring.

It appears in many fields. Rabbits breed and wolves starve in a predator and prey model, cells divide and die in a tumour, firms enter and exit a market, and households form and dissolve in a model of demography.

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction by which members of a group choose among options by utility.

At every step each member revises its choice with the probability activity and keeps it otherwise. The rule draws the new option from the utilities u_k of the options:

  • 'logit': option k with probability exp(beta u_k) / sum_j exp(beta u_j), where beta is the intensity of choice.
  • 'metropolis' and 'fermi': a proposed option, accepted with probability min(1, exp(beta (u_new - u_old))) or 1 / (1 + exp(-beta (u_new - u_old))).
  • 'best': an option of largest utility, with ties broken by ties.

In the symbolic form utility(namespace, option) returns an expression, and every member draws at once. In the agent form utility(agent, system, option) returns a number, the members draw by schedule, and an option of utility -inf is never drawn.

Unlike TransitionInteraction, which moves a state between values by given rates, it draws the new value from the utilities of all options at once. Choose it when members pick the option that pays best, with noise.

It appears in many fields. Commuters choose a mode of transport, consumers choose a brand, farmers choose a crop, and voters choose a party by a logit model of discrete choice.

required rule str

The rule of the draw, 'logit', 'metropolis', 'fermi', or 'best'.

'logit' intensity Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

'symbolic' phase str | None

None proposal str

'others' ties str

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction that breeds the strategies of a group by selection and mutation.

Every period steps the interaction selects parents by their fitness and replaces strategies by offspring. The selection picks parents by tournaments, by roulette, in proportion to fitness, or by rank. The replacement says how offspring take their places:

  • 'generational': every member is replaced by an offspring of a pair of parents, which exchange the tails of their strategies with probability crossover, and the elite fittest pass unchanged.
  • 'moran': one birth and death at a time, a selected parent copying onto a random member.
  • 'death-birth': members die with probability death and the offspring of survivors fill their places.
  • 'truncation': the fraction least fit are replaced by the offspring of the others.
  • 'best-mutant': every member draws a mutant, and the fittest mutant spreads when it beats the fittest strategy.

Each gene of an offspring mutates with probability mutation by the rule change, or a function mutation(strategy, rng) returns the mutated copy. The fitness is a state of the members, or the function evaluate(strategies, system), which the replacement writes into the fitness state.

Unlike ImitationInteraction, by which members copy neighbours, it replaces strategies by the offspring of the fittest across the group. Choose it when strategies evolve by selection, crossover, and mutation.

It appears in many fields. Genetic algorithms search for designs, strategies of the iterated prisoner's dilemma evolve in tournaments, and genotypes evolve on a fitness landscape in population genetics.

Bases: NeighborInteraction

An interaction by which members copy a discrete state from their neighbours.

The rule says whom a member copies:

  • 'random': a random neighbour.
  • 'majority': the option that more of its neighbours hold than any other.
  • 'best': the neighbour with the largest payoff, when it beats its own.
  • 'better': a random neighbour, when its payoff beats its own, in the agent form only.
  • 'fermi': a random neighbour, with probability 1 / (1 + exp(-beta (P_j - P_i))), where P_j and P_i are the payoffs of the neighbour and the member.

The form says when: at the rate rate in continuous time, with the probability probability per step for every member at once, or by agents in the order of schedule. A member without such a neighbour keeps its state.

Unlike CouplingInteraction, which averages numeric states of neighbours, it copies one discrete value from them. Choose it when members adopt the choices of those around them.

It appears in many fields. Voters copy their friends in the voter model, players copy successful strategies in evolutionary games on networks, and farmers adopt the crops of their neighbours.

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction that moves the agents of a group by steps at every discrete step.

The step says where an agent goes:

  • 'neighbor': a random cell or node next to its own, on a lattice or a network.
  • 'gaussian': its position plus a normal vector of deviation scale, in a continuous space.
  • 'levy': a random direction and a Pareto length of least value scale and tail exponent, in a continuous space.
  • 'best': the next cell with the highest score(agent, cell, system), or with a vision the best cell along each direction up to that many cells, with ties broken by ties.
  • A function step(agent, system) that returns the destination, or None to stay.

An agent for which condition holds attempts one step, or a Poisson number of mean rate, takes it with the probability probability, and then with the probability accept(agent, destination, system). An exclusive movement never enters a cell held by another agent of the group. The agents move one after another by schedule, and every step charges its cost.

Unlike TopologyInteraction, which changes the space, it changes where agents stand in it. Choose it when agents walk, forage, or relocate.

It appears in many fields. Sheep wander a pasture, foragers follow Lévy flights, ants climb a pheromone gradient, and residents move house in the segregation model of Schelling.

docs.title: Dynamics
docs.text:
Define the dynamical systems that the systems of several fields share.

States evolve by their equations, in continuous or discrete time, on the nodes of a graph, as fields on a lattice, or as stocks that change through named flows.

docs.title: DynamicalSystem(states=None, equations=None, *, parameters=None, noises=None, time='continuous', convention='ito', element='state', label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem[CompositeSystem]

A system of states and the equations that evolve them, as rates or as maps.

The states and parameters are the variables of one DeclaredElement. In continuous time the equation of a state is its rate, a RateInteraction that may carry a noise amplitude in the Itô or Stratonovich convention. In discrete time it is the next value of the state, a MapInteraction, and every map reads the states at the start of the step. An equation is a function of a namespace whose target holds the states and parameters and whose t holds the time.

A subclass takes the parameters of its model under its own names and returns the states, equations, parameters, and noises from the hooks _get_states, _get_equations, _get_parameters, and _get_noises, the time from _get_time, the label of the element from _get_element_label, and the specs of the variables from _get_variables.

Unlike CompositeSystem, which takes any parts, it is written with one DeclaredElement and one RateInteraction or MapInteraction per state. Choose it when a model is a set of equations, one per state.

It appears in many fields. The Lorenz flow of mathematics, the populations of Wilson and Cowan in neuroscience, the Hénon map, and the multiplier and accelerator model of economics are dynamical systems.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The composite of the element and its equations built from the parameters at the last prepare.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

The excitatory and inhibitory populations of Wilson and Cowan, which settle at a rest point:

>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import exp
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.dynamics import DynamicalSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> def response(u):
...     return 1 / (1 + exp(-u))
>>> populations = DynamicalSystem(
...     states={'e': 0.1, 'i': 0.05},
...     equations={
...         'e': lambda s: -s.target.e + response(s.target.c_ee * s.target.e - s.target.c_ei * s.target.i),
...         'i': lambda s: -s.target.i + response(s.target.c_ie * s.target.e - s.target.c_ii * s.target.i),
...     },
...     parameters={'c_ee': 2.0, 'c_ei': 3.0, 'c_ie': 2.0, 'c_ii': 1.0},
...     element='populations',
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(populations, until=50.0, dt=1.0)
>>> e, i = (float(trajectory.get_values(f'populations.{name}')[-1]) for name in 'ei')
>>> abs(e - float(response(2.0 * e - 3.0 * i))) < 1e-6
True

The multiplier-accelerator of Samuelson, whose income y of a period depends on the two before it:

>>> economy = DynamicalSystem(
...     states={'y': 1.0, 'previous': 1.0},
...     equations={
...         'y': lambda s: s.target.g + s.target.c * (1 + s.target.v) * s.target.y - s.target.c * s.target.v
...         * s.target.previous,
...         'previous': lambda s: s.target.y,
...     },
...     parameters={'g': 1.0, 'c': 0.5, 'v': 0.5},
...     time='discrete',
...     element='economy',
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(economy, until=3)
>>> trajectory.get_values('economy.y').tolist()
[1.0, 1.5, 1.875, 2.03125]
>>> sorted(economy.get_tags().laws)
['update']

docs.title: NetworkDynamicalSystem(graph=None, states=None, equations=None, coupling=None, *, parameters=None, noises=None, convention='ito', element='nodes', label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A dynamical system with states on every node of a graph and coupled neighbours.

The states and parameters are those of a DeclaredElement, a member of a FieldElement on the NetworkSpace of the graph. The equations are the local rates of every node. For every state with a coupling g, the rate of node i gains sum_j A_ij g(x_i, x_j) over its neighbours j, a CouplingInteraction that reads node i as s.member and its neighbour as s.other. An initial value is one number for every node or an array with one value per node. The system runs in continuous time.

A subclass returns the graph from _get_graph and the couplings from _get_coupling, besides the hooks of DynamicalSystem.

Unlike DynamicalSystem, which holds one copy of its states, it puts one copy on every node, written with a FieldElement, a NetworkSpace, and a CouplingInteraction. Choose it when identical units interact along the edges of a graph.

It appears in many fields. Heat diffuses on a graph in mathematics, cells exchange ions through gap junctions in physiology, and oscillators synchronize on a network in physics.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The composite of the nodes, their equations, and their couplings built at the last prepare.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

Diffusion on a path of three nodes, which spreads the content of the first node evenly:

>>> import networkx as nx
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.dynamics import NetworkDynamicalSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> diffusion = NetworkDynamicalSystem(
...     nx.path_graph(3),
...     states={'u': [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]},
...     coupling={'u': lambda s: s.member.D * (s.other.u - s.member.u)},
...     parameters={'D': 1.0},
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(diffusion, until=20.0, dt=1.0)
>>> [round(float(value), 3) for value in trajectory.get_values('nodes.u')[-1]]
[0.333, 0.333, 0.333]

Cells coupled by gap junctions, each relaxing to its own rest value while it exchanges with its neighbours:

>>> cells = NetworkDynamicalSystem(
...     nx.cycle_graph(4),
...     states={'v': [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]},
...     equations={'v': lambda s: -s.target.v / s.target.tau},
...     coupling={'v': lambda s: s.member.g * (s.other.v - s.member.v)},
...     parameters={'tau': 10.0, 'g': 0.5},
...     element='cells',
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(cells, until=5.0, dt=1.0)
>>> bool(trajectory.get_values('cells.v')[-1][1] > 0)
True

docs.title: ReactionDiffusionSystem(states=None, equations=None, diffusivities=None, *, shape=64, spacing=1.0, boundary='periodic', discretization='finite-difference', parameters=None, noises=None, convention='ito', element='medium', label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: DynamicalSystem

A dynamical system of fields on a lattice, with local kinetics and diffusion.

The states and parameters are those of a DeclaredElement, a member of a FieldElement on a LatticeSpace. The equations are the local kinetics of every site, and every field u with a diffusivity D gains the rate D laplacian(u), a separate RateInteraction, so a split solver can treat it apart. A diffusivity is a number or a function of the namespace. An initial value is one number for every site or an array of the shape of the lattice. The system runs in continuous time.

A subclass returns the diffusivities from _get_diffusivities, the lattice from _get_space, and the boundary of every field from _get_boundaries, besides the hooks of DynamicalSystem. A system whose kinetics are reactions returns them from _get_equation_interactions.

Unlike NetworkDynamicalSystem, which couples nodes of a graph, it couples the sites of a lattice by a Laplacian, written with a FieldElement and a RateInteraction. Choose it when substances react locally and spread in space.

It appears in many fields. The Gray-Scott model makes spots and stripes in chemistry, the Fisher and Kolmogorov front spreads a species in ecology, and the FitzHugh-Nagumo model sends waves through heart tissue.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The composite of the field, its kinetics, and its diffusion built at the last prepare.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

The front of Fisher and Kolmogorov, which invades the empty right side of a line:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.dynamics import ReactionDiffusionSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> initial = np.zeros(50)
>>> initial[:5] = 1.0
>>> front = ReactionDiffusionSystem(
...     states={'u': initial},
...     equations={'u': lambda s: s.target.r * s.target.u * (1 - s.target.u)},
...     diffusivities={'u': 1.0},
...     shape=50,
...     boundary='reflecting',
...     parameters={'r': 1.0},
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(front, until=10.0, dt=1.0)
>>> bool(trajectory.get_values('medium.u')[-1][20] > trajectory.get_values('medium.u')[0][20])
True

The Gray-Scott model, whose substrate u feeds the autocatalysis of the activator v:

>>> u, v = np.ones(32), np.zeros(32)
>>> u[12:20], v[12:20] = 0.5, 0.25
>>> gray_scott = ReactionDiffusionSystem(
...     states={'u': u, 'v': v},
...     equations={
...         'u': lambda s: -s.target.u * s.target.v**2 + s.target.F * (1 - s.target.u),
...         'v': lambda s: s.target.u * s.target.v**2 - (s.target.F + s.target.k) * s.target.v,
...     },
...     diffusivities={'u': 0.2, 'v': 0.1},
...     shape=32,
...     parameters={'F': 0.04, 'k': 0.06},
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(gray_scott, until=20.0, dt=5.0)
>>> bool(trajectory.get_values('medium.v')[-1].max() > 0)
True

docs.title: StockFlowSystem(stocks=None, flows=None, *, parameters=None, element='stocks', label='system')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSystem[CompositeSystem]

A system of stocks that change only through named flows between them.

The stocks and parameters are the variables of one DeclaredElement. Every flow leaves a stock or a source outside the system and enters a stock or a sink outside the system, at a rate that is a function of a namespace whose source holds the stocks and parameters and whose t holds the time. A labelled Source or Sink in place of None names the environment. A flow is a TransferInteraction from the element to itself, so the trajectory reports it as <element>.<flow>, and a flow between two stocks keeps their total.

A subclass returns the stocks, flows, and parameters from the hooks _get_stocks, _get_flows, and _get_parameters, the label of the element from _get_element_label, and the specs of the variables from _get_variables.

Unlike DynamicalSystem, which writes a rate per state, it writes flows between stocks with a TransferInteraction, so what leaves one stock enters another. Choose it when a model is drawn as stocks and flows, as in system dynamics.

It appears in many fields. A bathtub fills and drains in engineering, nations build arms in the arms race of Richardson, and the models of system dynamics of Forrester follow stocks of people, capital, and goods.

Attributes:

Name Type Description system_ CompositeT

The composite of the element and its flows built from the parameters at the last prepare.

laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

A bathtub whose faucet fills it as fast as its drain empties it:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.dynamics import StockFlowSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> tub = StockFlowSystem(
...     stocks={'water': 50.0},
...     flows={
...         'faucet': (None, 'water', lambda s: s.source.inflow),
...         'drain': ('water', None, lambda s: s.source.outflow),
...     },
...     parameters={'inflow': 5.0, 'outflow': 5.0},
...     element='tub',
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(tub, until=10.0, dt=5.0)
>>> trajectory.get_values('tub.water').tolist(), trajectory.get_values('tub.faucet').tolist()
([50.0, 50.0, 50.0], [5.0, 5.0, 5.0])

The arms race of two nations, each arming faster the more the other holds:

>>> race = StockFlowSystem(
...     stocks={'a': 1.0, 'b': 1.0},
...     flows={
...         'arming_a': (None, 'a', lambda s: s.source.k * s.source.b),
...         'arming_b': (None, 'b', lambda s: s.source.k * s.source.a),
...     },
...     parameters={'k': 0.1},
...     element='nations',
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(race, until=10.0, dt=10.0)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('nations.a')[-1]), 3)
2.718

docs.text:
Define the elements that the systems of several fields share.

They hold one nonnegative amount, or the position of a point in a continuous space.

docs.title: NonnegativeElement(label, visual=None, *, x=0.0)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

An element that holds one nonnegative number x.

The number is an amount, a share, a concentration, or the density at one class of a distribution. The element has no laws of its own, and the reactions, flows, and encounters of its system change it. A group of these elements on the sites of a lattice of classes is a distribution over the classes.

Unlike DeclaredElement, which takes its states as data, it fixes one state x at zero or above. Choose it when a system tracks an amount that cannot be negative, such as a count, a mass, or a sum of money.

It appears in many fields. The number of people infected in an epidemic, the moles of a chemical species in a reactor, the money in a bank account, and the tokens in a place of a Petri net are each one nonnegative number.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the element, unique among the parts of its system.

required visual VisualSpec | None

How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

None x Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

The initial value, a nonnegative number.

0.0

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem

>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[NonnegativeElement('A', x=990), NonnegativeElement('B', x=10)])
>>> simulate(system, until=2, dt=1.0).get_values('A.x').tolist()

docs.text:
Bases: Element

An element of a point that moves in a continuous space by its acceleration.

The point has a vector state x of order 2, its position. The laws that act on it give the second derivative of x, and the companion state x_d1 holds its velocity. The boundary of the space acts on x.

Unlike Element, which declares its own states, it fixes one position of order 2 with its velocity. Choose it when members are bodies that move by forces in a continuous space.

It appears in many fields. Atoms of a gas, stars of a cluster, birds of a flock, and pedestrians of a crowd are points that move by the forces on them.

0.0 x_d1 ArrayLike

The initial value of the first derivative of the vector state. A number applies to every component.

docs.text:
Define the flows that the systems of several fields share.

The Lorenz flow is a model of convection in mathematics and the response system of chaotic synchronization in physics.

docs.title: LorenzElement(label, visual=None, *, x=1.0, y=1.0, z=1.0, sigma=10.0, rho=28.0, beta=8 / 3)
docs.text:
Bases: Element

An element that follows the Lorenz flow of three states.

The flow is x' = sigma (y - x), y' = x (rho - z) - y, z' = x y - beta z. For sigma = 10, rho = 28, and beta = 8/3 its runs never settle and never repeat, the strange attractor of Lorenz. A subclass that declares the states with a fractional StateSpec(order=q) gives the fractional Lorenz flow, with Caputo derivatives of order q.

Unlike Element, which leaves its laws to a subclass, it returns the three rates of the Lorenz flow. Choose it when a system needs a chaotic flow in three states, as a model or as a drive.

It appears in many fields. Lorenz derived it from convection in the atmosphere, it models a laser and a water wheel, and it drives a response system in studies of chaotic synchronization.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the element.

required visual VisualSpec | None

How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

None x Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

The initial convection intensity.

1.0 y Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

The initial temperature difference between rising and falling currents.

1.0 z Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

The initial deviation of the vertical temperature profile.

1.0 sigma Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

The Prandtl number.

10.0 rho Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

The Rayleigh number relative to its critical value.

28.0 beta Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

The geometric factor.

8 / 3

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.flows import LorenzElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[LorenzElement('lorenz', x=0.0, y=0.0, z=2.0, beta=0.5)])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1.0, dt=0.5)
>>> [round(float(value), 4) for value in trajectory.get_values('lorenz.z')]
[2.0, 1.5576, 1.2131]

docs.title: Kinetics
docs.text:
Define the kinetic encounters that the systems of several fields share.

Distributions over the values of a trait meet in pairs and change class.

docs.title: EncounterInteraction(label, *, candidate, field=None, rate=None, kernel=None, outcome='conservative', state='x', cross_section=None, factor=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction where members of two distributions meet and change class.

A distribution is a group of NonnegativeElement with one member per class of a trait. A candidate at class h meets the field at class k at the rate rate[h, k], and the outcome says what follows:

  • 'conservative': the candidate moves to class i with the probability kernel[h, k, i].
  • 'destructive': the candidate is removed.
  • 'proliferative': the candidate creates a new candidate at class i with the probability kernel[h, k, i], or at its own class without a kernel.

The rate and the kernel are functions of the namespace, which holds namespace.candidate, namespace.field, and the parameters. On a PhaseSpace encounters pair classes at the same position. Without a field the encounter is a linear redistribution between classes. With a cross_section the rate is the binary collision integral of kinetic theory, evaluated by a fast spectral method, which keeps the density exactly and the momentum and energy to spectral accuracy.

Unlike BilinearLaw, the law it lowers to, it names the outcomes of an encounter and builds the rates and kernels from them. Choose it when the change of a population comes from binary meetings of its members.

It appears in many fields. Traders exchange wealth when they meet, people shift their opinion after a conversation, immune cells destroy tumour cells they meet, and gas molecules change velocity when they collide.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required candidate Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(state,))]

The path of the group of the candidate density.

required field Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True, elements=(ANY,), states=(state,))]

The path of the group of the field density, or None for a linear redistribution.

None rate Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function rate(namespace) of the encounter rate, a number or an expression, or an array eta[h, k] of them, or eta[h] without a field, or None with a cross-section.

None kernel Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function kernel(namespace) of the array kernel[h, k, i] of the probabilities of the class of the moved or created candidate, or kernel[h, i] without a field, or None for a destructive encounter or the candidate's own class.

None outcome str

'conservative', 'destructive', or 'proliferative'.

'conservative' state str

The name of the state of the densities.

'x' cross_section Callable[..., object] | None

The function B(speed, cosine) of arrays of the relative speed and the cosine of the deflection angle, or None for encounters at a rate.

None factor Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns a factor of the collision frequency, such as a function of the density moment, or None for none.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The outcome is unknown, the state is no name, a function is not callable, a conservative encounter has no kernel, an encounter without a field is not conservative, an encounter has neither a rate nor a cross-section, or a cross-section comes with a rate, a kernel, a field, or an outcome.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.kinetics import EncounterInteraction
>>> kernel = np.full((3, 3, 3), 1 / 3)
>>> mixing = EncounterInteraction(
...     'mixing', candidate='population', field='population', rate=lambda s: 1.0, kernel=lambda s: kernel
... )
>>> mixing.outcome
'conservative'
>>> collide = EncounterInteraction('collide', candidate='gas', cross_section=lambda speed, cosine: 1.0)
>>> collide.rate is None
True

docs.title: Matching
docs.text:
Define the matching of requesters with providers that several fields share.

A matching pairs requesters with providers by a rule spec, through the match law of the core.

docs.title: BatchMatchingSpec() dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of a batch matching of the largest quantity at one clearing value.

It collects every offer, then matches. Requesters are sorted by decreasing and providers by increasing limit, and they pair while the limit of the requester covers that of the provider. The value is the midpoint of the last paired limits, and every pair matches at it.

Unlike ContinuousMatchingSpec, which matches offers as they arrive, it clears all offers at once at one value. Choose it when a market clears in rounds, as a call auction does.

It appears in many fields. Stock exchanges open with a call auction, electricity markets clear once per hour, and markets for emission permits clear in rounds.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import BatchMatchingSpec
>>> BatchMatchingSpec()
BatchMatchingSpec()

docs.title: ContinuousMatchingSpec(arrival='random') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of a continuous matching, where arriving offers take the best resting.

Every participant submits one offer, in random order or in order of creation. An arriving offer matches the best resting offers of the other side, the oldest first among equal limits, at their limits, as long as the limits cross, and its remainder rests. The resting offers are dropped at the end of every matching, as in Caiani et al. (2016, chapter 3).

Unlike BatchMatchingSpec, which clears at one value, it matches at many values in order of arrival. Choose it when offers meet as they come, as in a limit order book.

It appears in many fields. Stock exchanges trade continuously through a limit order book, and agent-based models of macroeconomics match firms and banks this way.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default arrival str

The order of arrival, 'random' or 'sequential'.

'random'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The order of arrival is unknown, raised when its owner checks it.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import ContinuousMatchingSpec
>>> ContinuousMatchingSpec().arrival
'random'

docs.title: IterativeMatchingSpec(adjustment=0.1, iterations=500, tolerance=0.001) dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of an iterative matching that moves a value until supply meets demand.

Starting from the last clearing value, or the median of the limits, the value moves by p <- p (1 + adjustment (D - S) / (D + S)) until the relative excess of requests falls below tolerance. Here D is the quantity requested at a limit of at least p and S the quantity offered at a limit of at most p. The members then match at that value, and the long side is rationed in random order, as in Hamill and Gilbert (2016, chapter 5).

Unlike BatchMatchingSpec, which reads the value off sorted offers, it searches for it by small steps. Choose it when a value adjusts to balance supply and demand, as in a tâtonnement of Walras.

It appears in many fields. Prices adjust in models of general equilibrium, wages adjust in labour markets, and interest rates adjust in models of credit.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default adjustment float

The speed of the value adjustment.

0.1 iterations int

The largest number of adjustments per clearing.

500 tolerance float

The relative excess of requests at which the adjustment stops.

0.001

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import IterativeMatchingSpec
>>> IterativeMatchingSpec(adjustment=0.05).iterations
500

docs.title: MatchSpec(requester, provider, quantity, value) dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of one match, a quantity at a value per unit between two members.

Unlike the rule specs, which say how members match, it records one match that a rule made. Choose it when an on_match function of a MatchingInteraction reads the match it receives.

It appears in many fields. A buyer pays a seller for goods, a worker takes a job at a wage, and a borrower takes a loan at a rate.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default requester object

The agent view of the requester.

required provider object

The agent view of the provider.

required quantity float

The matched quantity.

required value float

The clearing value per unit.

required

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import MatchSpec
>>> MatchSpec('a', 'b', 2.0, 5.0).quantity
2.0

docs.title: MatchingInteraction(label, *, requesters, providers, rule=RandomSearchSpec(), reserve='reserve', quantity='quantity', cap='cap', transfers=(), phase=None, on_match=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

An interaction that matches requesters with providers and settles every match.

Requesters state in their states the highest value they accept, reserve, the quantity they want, quantity, and the most value they can give, cap. Providers state the lowest value they accept and the quantity they offer. A name given as a pair names the state of the requesters first and of the providers second. The rule is a spec of the algorithm that pairs the offers, such as RandomSearchSpec, QueueSpec, BatchMatchingSpec, or StableMatchingSpec.

Every match lowers the quantities of both sides and moves every state of transfers: a negative sign moves value * quantity from the requester to the provider, and a positive sign moves quantity from the provider to the requester, so the totals stay the same. on_match(match, system) adds any other effect. The matching runs once per round of its phase and reports <label>.value, the clearing value weighted by quantity, <label>.volume, and <label>.unmatched.

Unlike TransferInteraction, which moves amounts between given pairs, it first forms the pairs by a rule, through the MatchLaw of the core, and then transfers. Choose it when who trades with whom and at what value are part of the model.

It appears in many fields. Buyers and sellers trade goods, workers and firms agree on wages, borrowers and banks agree on loans, and patients and hospitals are matched.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the matching.

required requesters Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(GROUP, VARIABLE_GROUP))]

The path of the group of requesters.

required providers Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(GROUP, VARIABLE_GROUP))]

The path of the group of providers.

required rule MatchingRule | Pairing

The spec of the algorithm that matches the members, such as ContinuousMatchingSpec(), or a function rule(requesters, providers, rng, capacity) of the agents with a positive quantity that returns their pairs, which match at the midpoint of both reserves. A PartnerSpec picks among the providers that still offer a quantity at a reserve the requester accepts, in random order of the requesters, and settles at the midpoint, or at the value of a PartnerMatchingSpec.

RandomSearchSpec() reserve str | tuple[str, str]

The state with the reserve of both sides, or a pair of the requesters' and the providers' states. An agent without the default state 'reserve' has no reserve as a requester and the reserve 0 as a provider.

'reserve' quantity str | tuple[str, str]

The state with the quantity of both sides, or a pair of the requesters' and the providers' states. An agent without the default state 'quantity' offers the quantity 1.

'quantity' cap str

The state of a requester with the most value it can give. A requester without the default state 'cap' has no reserve on what it gives.

'cap' transfers Sequence[tuple[str, int]]

The states every match moves, each with the sign -1 for a move from the requester to the provider or 1 for a move from the provider to the requester.

() phase str | None

The phase the matching runs in, or None for the default phase.

None on_match Callable[[MatchSpec, SystemT], None] | None

A function of every match and the system view, run after the transfers, or None.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

A transfer has a sign other than -1 or 1, or the rule is neither a matching spec nor a function, or it is invalid, raised by prepare, or an agent lacks a state other than a default one that names its reserve, quantity, or cap, raised by run.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import MatchingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import ContinuousMatchingSpec
>>> matching = MatchingInteraction(
...     'exchange',
...     requesters='traders',
...     providers='traders',
...     rule=ContinuousMatchingSpec(),
...     reserve=('bid', 'ask'),
... )
>>> matching.reports
('value', 'volume', 'unmatched')

docs.title: match(system)
docs.text:
Match the members, settle the matches, and report the results.

It reports the value, the volume, and the unmatched quantity.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system SystemT

The system view of the matching.

required Source code in src/skcomplex/systems/general/matching/_matching.py 
def match(self, system: SystemT) -> None:
    """Match the members, settle the matches, and report the results.

    It reports the value, the volume, and the unmatched quantity.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the matching.
    """
    requesters, providers = self._get_offers(system)
    matches = self._get_matches(requesters, providers, system)
    for match in matches:
        self._settle(match, system)
    unmatched = sum(offer.quantity for offer in requesters + providers)
    self._report_matches(matches, unmatched, system)

docs.title: PartnerMatchingSpec(candidates='all', choice='uniform', fallback=None, capacity=None, score=None, value='midpoint') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: PartnerSpec

A spec of a choice of partners that a matching settles at a value.

It is a PartnerSpec with the value of a pair, which only a matching reads.

Unlike PartnerSpec, which only pairs members, it also says the value at which each pair settles. Choose it when members pick partners by distance or score and then trade.

It appears in many fields. Buyers visit the nearest shops, workers apply to the best paying firms within reach, and traders deal with partners they trust.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidates str | float

The agents an agent considers, as in PartnerSpec.

'all' choice str

How an agent picks among its candidates, as in PartnerSpec.

'uniform' fallback str | None

The partner of an agent without candidates, as in PartnerSpec.

None capacity str | float | None

The largest number of pairs of an agent in one step, as in PartnerSpec.

None score Preference | None

The function score(agent, candidate) the choice 'score' reads, as in PartnerSpec.

None value str

The value of a pair that a matching settles, 'midpoint' of both reserves, 'provider', or 'requester'.

'midpoint'

docs.title: PartnerSwitchSpec(sample=3, intensity=1.0, partner='partner') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of a choice of partner that may switch to a cheaper provider.

Every requester, in random order, samples sample providers that still offer something. When the lowest limit among them is below that of its current partner, it switches with the probability 1 - exp(intensity * (p_new - p_old) / p_new), and stays otherwise. It matches with its partner at the limit of the partner, and its state partner holds the id of the partner across steps. The rule follows Caiani et al. (2016, chapter 2).

Unlike RandomSearchSpec, which meets new providers each time, it keeps a partner and switches with friction. Choose it when relations persist, such as customers loyal to a supplier.

It appears in many fields. Households keep their shops, firms keep their banks, and workers keep their employers unless a better offer comes, in agent-based models of macroeconomics.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sample int

The number of providers every requester samples.

3 intensity float

The intensity of switching.

1.0 partner str

The name of the requester state that holds the id of its partner.

'partner'

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import PartnerSwitchSpec
>>> PartnerSwitchSpec(sample=2, intensity=4.0).intensity
4.0

docs.title: QueueSpec(order='random') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of a queue of requesters served by the cheapest providers.

Requesters queue in random order, by decreasing reserve, or in order of creation, and each matches at the reserve of the cheapest providers whose reserve it accepts. The last requesters may get nothing.

Unlike IterativeMatchingSpec, which finds one value for all, it serves requesters one by one at the prices of the providers. Choose it when members are served in order, first come first served.

It appears in many fields. Customers queue at a shop, patients wait for organs, and households queue for housing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default order str

The order of the queue, 'random', 'reserve', or 'sequential'.

'random'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The order is unknown, raised when its owner checks it.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import QueueSpec
>>> QueueSpec(order='reserve').order
'reserve'

docs.title: RandomSearchSpec(tries=1, value='midpoint') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of a random search, where requesters meet random providers and match.

Every requester, in random order, makes up to tries meetings with providers that still offer something, and matches when the limits cross, at the midpoint of the two limits or at the limit of one side. It is the decentralised exchange of Hamill and Gilbert (2016, chapter 5).

Unlike BatchMatchingSpec, which sees every offer, it lets each requester see only a few. Choose it when information is local and search is costly.

It appears in many fields. Buyers search among sellers in a bazaar, job seekers meet a few firms, and animals search for mates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default tries int

The number of providers every requester meets.

1 value str

The value of a match, 'midpoint', 'requester', or 'provider'.

'midpoint'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The value rule is unknown, raised when its owner checks it.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import RandomSearchSpec
>>> RandomSearchSpec(tries=3).tries
3

docs.title: StableMatchingSpec(requester_preference=None, provider_preference=None, value='provider') dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSpec

A spec of the stable matching of Gale and Shapley, by mutual preferences.

Requesters propose to providers, which take as many as they offer units. Requesters rank the providers by requester_preference(requester, provider), by default the lower reserve, and providers rank the requesters by provider_preference(provider, requester), by default the higher reserve. The stable matching that favours the requesters, from the hospital and resident solver of the matching library, pairs every requester with at most one provider, and each pair matches one unit at the value of value. No requester and provider then prefer each other to their partners.

Unlike BatchMatchingSpec, which pairs by price alone, it pairs by preferences on both sides. Choose it when both sides rank each other and stability matters.

It appears in many fields. Medical residents match with hospitals, students match with schools, and donors match with patients in kidney exchange.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default requester_preference Preference | None

The score of a provider for a requester, a function of their agent views, higher for preferred providers, or None for the lower reserve.

None provider_preference Preference | None

The score of a requester for a provider, a function of their agent views, higher for preferred requesters, or None for the higher reserve.

None value str

The value of a match, 'provider', 'requester', or 'midpoint'.

'provider'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The value rule is unknown, raised when its owner checks it.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.systems.general.matching import StableMatchingSpec
>>> StableMatchingSpec(value='requester').value
'requester'
