stochastic.get_tags().randomness, simulate(stochastic, random_state=0).get_values('I.x').max()

('stochastic', 110.0)

With stochastic=True the system is 'stochastic', and the run with the seed 0 peaks at 110 infected people. The contributing guide shows how a system class of your own joins the catalog, with its field, topics, references, tests, and gallery example.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page lists every error of skcomplex.core.errors, with the shortest code that raises it, its message, what it means, and the fix. Search the page for the name of the error a run raised. Each class is a subclass of SkcomplexError, and most checks of a system raise a subclass of ValidationError.

simulate checks a whole system before it compiles and raises one error that lists every problem it found. Each line of that message names the path of the part, the problem, a fix, and a short code in brackets, such as [role]. The error takes the class of its problems when they share one, and is a ValidationError when they differ.

Each section runs on its own. Most use a population of hares that grows at the rate 0.55 a year, or the hare and lynx model of the build tutorial with the rates of Carpenter (2018).

docs.title: SkcomplexError
docs.text:
Every error of the library subclasses SkcomplexError, so one except clause catches them all. Here a solver for maps meets a system of rates.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import IterationSolver
from skcomplex.core.errors import SkcomplexError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    simulate(system, until=20, solver=IterationSolver())
except SkcomplexError as error:
    name, message = type(error).__name__, str(error)
name, message

('TagError',
 'The solver IterationSolver does not support the time continuous of the system. Pass a solver that supports them, '
 'or none for the default.')

The error is a TagError, one of the subclasses below. Catch the root class where a program treats every error of the library the same way, such as a sweep that logs failed runs and goes on. Catch a subclass where the fix depends on the error. A few checks keep the errors of Python and scikit-learn, such as the ValueError of set_params for an unknown name and the KeyError of get_values for a missing path.

docs.title: NotPreparedError
docs.text:
A part runs only after prepare has checked it. A law run on its own before it is prepared raises this error.

from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var

from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
from skcomplex.core.errors import NotPreparedError

x = var('x')
try:
    RateLaw(x, 0.5 * x).run({'x': 10.0})
except NotPreparedError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, RateLaw(x, 0.5 * x).prepare('growth').run({'x': 10.0}).value_

('RateLaw must be prepared before it runs. Call `prepare(...)` first.', 5.0)

The message reads "RateLaw must be prepared before it runs. Call prepare(...) first." The fix calls prepare first, and the rate at x = 10 is then 5.0. simulate prepares every part of a system itself, so a run never meets this error.

docs.title: ValidationError
docs.text:
A value that breaks a rule of its part or of the run raises a ValidationError, the parent of most errors below. Here the initial state names the hares by the label of the build tutorial, while the catalog class calls them prey.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import ValidationError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    simulate(system, until=20, initial_state={'hares.x': 10.0})
except ValidationError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, simulate(system, until=1, dt=1.0, initial_state={'prey.x': 10.0}).get_values('prey.x').round(1).tolist()

('The initial state names hares.x, which are not states of the system. Use the dotted names of states, such as '
 'prey.x, predators.x.',
 [10.0, 15.9])

The message says that hares.x is not a state of the system and suggests prey.x and predators.x. With prey.x the run starts from 10.0 thousand hares and reaches 15.9 thousand after a year.

docs.title: ContextError
docs.text:
Some objects prepare against an owner, such as a solver against the problem it advances. Prepared alone, without that context, they raise this error.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import RK4Solver
from skcomplex.core.errors import ContextError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    RK4Solver().prepare()
except ContextError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, simulate(system, until=2, dt=1.0, solver=RK4Solver()).get_values('prey.x').round(1).tolist()

('A solver prepares on a compiled problem. Pass the problem to `prepare`.', [30.0, 46.4, 68.5])

The message reads "A solver prepares on a compiled problem. Pass the problem to prepare." The fix passes the solver to simulate, which compiles the problem and prepares the solver on it. The run gives 30.0, 46.4, and 68.5 thousand hares.

docs.title: AlgebraicStateError
docs.text:
An algebraic state has no derivative of its own. The equations of its system fix its value at every time, so a rate law on it has no meaning.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import AlgebraicStateError
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class LevelElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec(algebraic=True)] = 0.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x

    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        return [RateLaw(namespace.x, 1.0)]


try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[LevelElement('level')]), until=1)
except AlgebraicStateError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- level: The RateLaw of level targets the algebraic state level.x, but the equations of the system determine this state. State the value of level.x with an `EquationLaw`, or declare it as a state of order 1. [algebraic-law]

The code is algebraic-law. The message says that the RateLaw of level targets the algebraic state level.x, and suggests an EquationLaw for its value or a state of order 1. The fix below states the value with an equation.

from skcomplex.core.components.laws import EquationLaw


class FixedLevelElement(LevelElement):
    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        return [EquationLaw(namespace.x, 2.0)]


simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[FixedLevelElement('level')]), until=1, dt=1.0).get_values('level.x').tolist()

[2.0, 2.0]

The level holds 2.0 at both frames.

docs.title: ConservationError
docs.text:
A run checks the invariants it is given at every frame, and a quantity that drifts further than its tolerance raises this error. The Lotka and Volterra model keeps V = b H - d ln H + a L - r ln L constant along every orbit, and forward Euler drifts off it.

import numpy as np

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import EulerSolver
from skcomplex.core.errors import ConservationError
from skcomplex.core.specs import ObservableSpec
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)


def get_constant(t, values):
    prey, predators = values['prey.x'], values['predators.x']
    return 0.024 * prey - 0.80 * np.log(prey) + 0.028 * predators - 0.55 * np.log(predators)


constant = ObservableSpec('constant', function=get_constant)
try:
    simulate(
        system, until=20, dt=1.0, solver=EulerSolver(dt=0.1), observables=[constant], invariants={'constant': 1e-3}
    )
except ConservationError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

The invariant constant changed from -2.65142 to -2.64349 at frame 1, time 1, beyond its tolerance 0.001.

The message says that the invariant changed from -2.65142 to -2.64349 at frame 1, beyond its tolerance 0.001. The fix is a smaller step, a solver of higher order such as RK4Solver, or the default solver, which keeps the constant.

docs.title: TensorShapeError
docs.text:
The operations on tensors read matrices and vectors of expressions. A value of another shape raises this error.

from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import SR, identity_matrix, var

from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import tensor_divergence
from skcomplex.core.errors import TensorShapeError

p = var('p')
try:
    tensor_divergence(p)
except TensorShapeError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, tensor_divergence(p * identity_matrix(SR, 2))

('tensor_divergence needs a square matrix, but got p, which has another shape.', (partial(p, 0), partial(p, 1)))

The message reads "tensor_divergence needs a square matrix, but got p, which has another shape." The fix passes the pressure as the isotropic tensor p I, whose divergence is (partial(p, 0), partial(p, 1)), the gradient of p.

docs.title: TensorSymmetryError
docs.text:
A tensor state declared symmetric stores only its independent entries, so its rate must have the same symmetry. Here a field of strain on a lattice takes an antisymmetric rate.

from typing import Annotated

from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import SR, matrix

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, FieldElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import TensorSymmetryError
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class StrainElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, S: Annotated[object, StateSpec(tensor='symmetric')] = 0.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.S = S

    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        S = namespace.S
        return [RateLaw(S, matrix(SR, [[0, S[0, 0]], [-S[0, 0], 0]]))]


sheet = FieldElement('sheet', element=StrainElement, space=LatticeSpace((4, 4)))
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[sheet]), until=0.1)
except TensorSymmetryError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.split(' on the tensor state ')[-1]

sheet.S breaks its symmetry 'symmetric' at the entry [1, 0], by the comparison at random component values, since Sage does not simplify the difference to 0. Give the state a rate of its declared symmetry. [tensor-symmetry]

The code is tensor-symmetry. The message says that the rate law on the tensor state sheet.S breaks its symmetry 'symmetric' at the entry [1, 0]. The fix writes the rate with the symmetry of the state, here with symmetric_part.

from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import symmetric_part


class SymmetricStrainElement(StrainElement):
    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        S = namespace.S
        return [RateLaw(S, symmetric_part(matrix(SR, [[0, S[0, 0]], [-S[0, 0], 0]])) - S)]


sheet = FieldElement('sheet', element=SymmetricStrainElement, space=LatticeSpace((4, 4)))
simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[sheet]), until=0.1).get_values('sheet.S').shape

(11, 16, 3)

The run records 11 frames of 16 sites with 3 independent entries each.

docs.title: RewritingError
docs.text:
A rewriting system grows a word at every generation, and max_size bounds its length. The algae of Lindenmayer replace A by AB and B by A.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import WordElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import ProductionLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import RewritingError


class AlgaeElement(WordElement):
    law_classes = (ProductionLaw,)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        return [ProductionLaw('A', 'AB'), ProductionLaw('B', 'A')]


try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[AlgaeElement('algae', axiom='A', max_size=4)]), until=5)
except RewritingError as error:
    message = str(error)
longer = CompositeSystem(elements=[AlgaeElement('algae', axiom='A', max_size=16)])
message, simulate(longer, until=5).get_values('algae.size').tolist()

("Word 'algae' would reach 5 symbols at generation 3, above its maximum size 4. Raise max_size or run fewer "
 'generations.',
 [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 8.0, 13.0])

The message says that the word would reach 5 symbols at generation 3, above its maximum size 4. With max_size=16 the sizes run through the Fibonacci numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, and 13.

docs.title: ParameterError
docs.text:
A parameter name that the problem does not hold, or a value outside its domain, raises this error. A schedule names the parameters of the built parts by their path.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import ParameterError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    simulate(system, until=20, schedule={'predation.alpha': lambda t: 0.0})
except ParameterError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

No parameter named 'predation.alpha' to schedule. Available names are: growth.r, predation.a, predation.b, death.d.

The message lists the valid names, growth.r, predation.a, predation.b, and death.d. The fix is schedule={'predation.a': lambda t: 0.0}. get_params of a system lists its model parameters, and names of a trajectory lists the paths of the built parts.

docs.title: LabelError
docs.text:
Every part of a system needs a label of its own, because roles, states, and parameters are named by it. Two elements called hares collide.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import LabelError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
births = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: 0.55 * s.target.x)
twins = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(4.0, StateSpec())})
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[hares, twins], interactions=[births]), until=1)
except LabelError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- system: Label 'hares' is used by more than one child of the root system. Give every child of a system a unique label of letters, digits, and underscores. [label]

The code is label, and the message asks for a unique label of letters, digits, and underscores. The fix renames the second element, such as to lynx.

docs.title: RoleError
docs.text:
A role names an element by its label. A typing error, or an element left out of the system, leaves the role bound to nothing.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import RoleError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
hunting = RateInteraction(
    'hunting', target='hares', state='x', sources=['lynx'], rate=lambda s: -0.028 * s.target.x * s.sources[0].x
)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[hares], interactions=[hunting]), until=1)
except RoleError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- hunting: Interaction hunting binds the role 'sources' to 'lynx', which is not an element or group path relative to the root system. Bind every role to the path of an element, group, or member of the system. [role]

The code is role. The message says that hunting binds the role sources to lynx, which is not an element of the system. The fix adds the element lynx, or binds the role to a label the system holds. A role reaches an element of a nested system by a path such as forest/foxes.

docs.title: RoleElementError
docs.text:
A role may be bound to an element that exists but does not fit it, because the element is of the wrong kind or lacks a state the role reads. Here births change the state n of hares that carry x.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import RoleElementError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
wrong_state = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='n', rate=lambda s: 0.55)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[hares], interactions=[wrong_state]), until=1)
except RoleElementError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- births: The role 'target' of births reads the state 'n', but the element hares bound to it carries x. Bind the role to an element that carries the state, declare the state on the element, or read another state. `get_requirements()` of an interaction and `get_states()` of an element show what they need and carry. [role-element]

The code is role-element. The message says that the role target of births reads the state n, but the element hares carries x. The fix is state='x', or a state n on the element. The page Check a system shows the same error for a role that accepts groups only.

docs.title: TagError
docs.text:
The tags of a part say what it needs, such as continuous or discrete time. Parts that disagree on a tag, or a solver that does not support the tags of a system, raise this error. Here a rate in continuous time meets a map in discrete time.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import MapInteraction, RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import TagError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
births = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: 0.55 * s.target.x)
lynx = DeclaredElement('lynx', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(4.0, StateSpec())})
deaths = MapInteraction('deaths', target='lynx', state='x', function=lambda s: 0.45 * s.target.x)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[hares, lynx], interactions=[births, deaths]), until=1)
except TagError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

The parts 'births' and 'deaths' disagree on the tag 'time': 'births' has continuous and 'deaths' has discrete. Give the system a time that joins them, or bind parts of one time.

The message says that births has the time continuous and deaths the time discrete. The fix writes both parts in one time, or splits the system into nested systems that run as partitions, as the tutorial Simulate shows. get_tags of each part shows where a tag comes from.

docs.title: SpaceError
docs.text:
A part that needs a space, a vector state without a space to give its dimension, or a location outside its space raises this error. Here a group sits on sites but has neither a size nor a space.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import SpaceError

try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[GroupElement('herds', element=Element, on='sites')]), until=1)
except SpaceError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, GroupElement('herds', element=Element, on='sites', space=LatticeSpace((5, 5))).prepare().size_

("Group 'herds' lives on sites but has neither a size nor a space.", 25)

The message reads "Group 'herds' lives on sites but has neither a size nor a space." The fix gives the group a space, here a lattice of five by five sites, or a size.

docs.title: SpaceTooLargeError
docs.text:
A space that would hold more sites than its limit raises this error before it allocates them. The Cayley graph of the free group on two generators is infinite.

from sage.all__sagemath_gap import libgap

from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CayleySpace
from skcomplex.core.errors import SpaceTooLargeError

try:
    CayleySpace(libgap.FreeGroup(['a', 'b'])).prepare()
except SpaceTooLargeError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, CayleySpace(libgap.FreeGroup(['a', 'b']), ball=2).prepare().size_

('The group space has more than 100000 sites. Ask for a smaller ball or a finite quotient, or raise max_sites.', 17)

The message reads "The group space has more than 100000 sites. Ask for a smaller ball or a finite quotient, or raise max_sites." The fix ball=2 keeps the 17 words of length at most two.

docs.title: PhaseSpaceTooLargeError
docs.text:
A phase space has one site per cell of its position lattice and of every class axis, such as a velocity, so its size is the product of all of them. limit guards the memory.

from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace, PhaseSpace
from skcomplex.core.errors import PhaseSpaceTooLargeError
from skcomplex.core.specs import AxisSpec

try:
    PhaseSpace(LatticeSpace((100, 100)), [AxisSpec('v', 64, -4.0, 4.0)], limit=100_000).prepare()
except PhaseSpaceTooLargeError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, PhaseSpace(LatticeSpace((10, 10)), [AxisSpec('v', 64, -4.0, 4.0)], limit=100_000).prepare().size_

('The phase space would take 640000 sites, above its limit of 100000.', 6400)

The message reads "The phase space would take 640000 sites, above its limit of 100000." The fix uses fewer cells, here a lattice of ten by ten with 6400 sites, or a higher limit when the memory allows.

docs.title: UnregisteredLawError
docs.text:
Each law class compiles to a mathematical form, such as an ordinary differential equation for RateLaw. A law of a class the engine has no form for raises this error, even a subclass of a core law. Here a growth law subclasses RateLaw.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import UnregisteredLawError
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class GrowthLaw(RateLaw):
    pass


class HaresElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 30.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x

    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        return [GrowthLaw(namespace.x, 0.55 * namespace.x)]


try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[HaresElement('hares')]), until=1)
except UnregisteredLawError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- hares: The law class GrowthLaw has no form the engine knows. Write the law with a class the core provides, such as `RateLaw` or `UpdateLaw`. [law-unregistered]

The code is law-unregistered. The message says that the law class GrowthLaw of hares has no form the engine knows. The fix writes the law with a class the core provides, here RateLaw(namespace.x, 0.55 * namespace.x).

docs.title: IncompatibleLawsError
docs.text:
The laws of one system must compile to one mathematical form, and a law that holds what its form cannot run raises this error. Here a rate draws a random number, which only update and renewal laws do.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import normal
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import IncompatibleLawsError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
noisy = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: normal('kick', 0.55, 0.1) * s.target.x)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[hares], interactions=[noisy]), until=1)
except IncompatibleLawsError as error:
    message = str(error)
message.splitlines()[-1]

- system: The RateLaw of births holds the random draw normal_kick(0.55, 0.1), but only update and renewal laws take random draws. Express randomness in continuous time with Noise laws for Wiener processes, Jump laws for random events, or Renewal laws for events after drawn waiting times. Correct the component as the message describes. [value]

The message says that the RateLaw of births holds the random draw normal_kick(0.55, 0.1). It suggests noise laws for Wiener processes, jump laws for random events, or renewal laws in continuous time. A nested system whose own parts mix law kinds raises the same error with the code laws-mixed, and the fix moves each kind into a nested system of its own.

docs.title: BackendError
docs.text:
A backend turns laws into numeric functions, and a law it cannot write raises this error. LAMMPS runs particles with positions and velocities, so it cannot run two populations.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import LammpsSolver
from skcomplex.core.errors import BackendError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    simulate(system, until=1, dt=1.0, solver=LammpsSolver())
except BackendError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

The LAMMPS backend cannot run this system. Unsupported: element prey, which declares no vector position state of order 2; element predators, which declares no vector position state of order 2; interaction growth; interaction predation; interaction death.

The message lists what the LAMMPS backend cannot run, such as the element prey, which declares no vector position state of order 2. The fix leaves out solver and backend, so the tags choose a pair that runs the laws, or picks one from the solvers page and the backends page.

docs.title: PipelineError
docs.text: A run does not raise this error. The compiler of the library lowers a system through passes, each of which reads some fields of the compilation and writes others. A pass that reads a field no pass writes, two passes that write one field, or passes that read each other in a cycle raise it while the compiler orders them. It concerns those who add a pass to the compiler, and the fix adds the pass that writes the field or splits the cycle.

docs.title: SolverError
docs.text:
A solver that does not fit its problem, or that fails to advance it, raises this error. A fixed step must be positive.

from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import RK4Solver
from skcomplex.core.errors import SolverError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    simulate(system, until=2, dt=1.0, solver=RK4Solver(dt=-0.1))
except SolverError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, simulate(system, until=2, dt=1.0, solver=RK4Solver(dt=0.1)).get_values('prey.x').round(1).tolist()

('dt = -0.1 must be positive.', [30.0, 46.4, 68.5])

The message reads "dt = -0.1 must be positive." With a step of 0.1 the run gives 30.0, 46.4, and 68.5 thousand hares. A solver that fails to advance, such as an implicit solve with no solution near the last values, raises the same class. A smaller step or a stiff solver fixes that case.

docs.title: InfeasibleError
docs.text:
A linear program with no feasible point raises this error when its law asks to raise. Two plants of 100 and 50 units cannot meet a demand of 300.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import LinearProgramLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import StaticTime
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import InfeasibleError
from skcomplex.core.specs import LinearObjectiveSpec, ParameterSpec, StateSpec

Output = Annotated[float, StateSpec(algebraic=True)]
Demand = Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]


class GridElement(Element):
    law_classes = (LinearProgramLaw,)

    def __init__(self, label, *, coal: Output = 0.0, gas: Output = 0.0, demand: Demand = 120.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.coal, self.gas, self.demand = coal, gas, demand

    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        coal, gas = namespace.coal, namespace.gas
        constraints = [coal + gas == namespace.demand, coal <= 100, gas <= 50, coal >= 0, gas >= 0]
        return [LinearProgramLaw([coal, gas], constraints, [LinearObjectiveSpec(20 * coal + 50 * gas, sense='min')])]


try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[GridElement('grid', demand=300.0)], time=StaticTime()), until=0.0)
except InfeasibleError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

The linear program of grid has no solution at time 0.0: the constraints coal_grid + gas_grid == demand_grid and the variables grid.coal, grid.gas cannot hold together. Relax one of them, or give the law the policy `infeasible='zero'` or `infeasible='hold'`.

The message says that the program of grid has no solution at time 0, names the demand constraint and the variables grid.coal and grid.gas, and suggests infeasible='zero' or infeasible='hold'. The fix is a demand the plants can meet, or one of those policies on LinearProgramLaw.

docs.title: SimulationError
docs.text:
A simulation used in a state that does not allow an operation raises this error. A recorder holds no trajectory before a run sends it frames.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import RecorderObserver, simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import SimulationError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hares = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
births = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: 0.55 * s.target.x)
growth = CompositeSystem(elements=[hares], interactions=[births])
recorder = RecorderObserver()
try:
    recorder.trajectory_
except SimulationError as error:
    message = str(error)
simulate(growth, until=2, dt=1.0, observers=[recorder])
message, recorder.trajectory_.get_values('hares.x').round(1).tolist()

<skcomplex.core.engine.runtime._trajectories.Trajectory object at 0x752fe182f5f0>
('The recorder has not received a problem. Run a simulation that observes it first.', [30.0, 52.0, 90.1])

The message reads "The recorder has not received a problem. Run a simulation that observes it first." After the run the recorder holds the frames 30.0, 52.0, and 90.1.

docs.title: CapacityError
docs.text:
A group whose members appear and disappear on a network holds a fixed number of rows, its capacity. A request to add a member beyond it raises this error. Here a network of three nodes gains one node at every step.

import networkx as nx

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import UpdateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import DiscreteTime, NetworkSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import CapacityError
from skcomplex.core.specs import TopologyRequestSpec


class GrowthElement(Element):
    def _get_laws(self, namespace):
        return [UpdateLaw(TopologyRequestSpec('add-node'), 1)]


def grow(capacity):
    nodes = GroupElement('nodes', element=Element, on='sites', variable=True, capacity=capacity)
    links = GroupElement('links', element=Element, on='edges', variable=True, capacity=3 * capacity)
    network = CompositeSystem(
        elements=[nodes, links, GrowthElement('growth')], space=NetworkSpace(nx.complete_graph(3)), time=DiscreteTime()
    )
    return simulate(network, until=3, random_state=0)


try:
    grow(capacity=4)
except CapacityError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, grow(capacity=6).get_network(-1).nodes.size

('The group nodes holds 4 members, its capacity, and a topology request adds another. Give the group a larger '
 'capacity, `GroupElement(..., variable=True, capacity=n)`.',
 6)

The message says that the group nodes holds 4 members, its capacity, and asks for a larger capacity. With room for 6 the network ends with 6 nodes after three steps.

docs.title: ExperimentError
docs.text:
An experiment that cannot run its tasks raises this error. A factory of systems must return a system, and one that forgets to return it gives None.

from skcomplex.core.errors import ExperimentError
from skcomplex.core.experiments import sweep
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem


def build(r):
    LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=r, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)


try:
    sweep(build, {'r': [0.45, 0.65]}, until=1)
except ExperimentError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

The factory of an experiment returns a system, not NoneType.

The message reads "The factory of an experiment returns a system, not NoneType." The fix adds return before the system. An experiment also raises this error when its worker processes die, for example for lack of memory, and the fix there is fewer workers or a smaller design.

docs.title: AnalysisError
docs.text:
An analysis that does not apply to its source raises this error. The equations of Lotka and Volterra have no closed form, so the exact solution fails.

from skcomplex.core.analysis import symbolic
from skcomplex.core.errors import AnalysisError
from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

system = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
try:
    symbolic(system, kind='solve')
except AnalysisError as error:
    message = str(error)
message

No closed form was found for prey.x, predators.x: the solution contains unevaluated transforms, integrals, or the unknown functions themselves. Simulate the system numerically instead.

The message says that no closed form was found for prey.x and predators.x, and suggests simulating the system instead. applicable_analyses lists the analyses that apply to a source, as the tutorial Analyse shows.

docs.title: EnumerationLimitError
docs.text:
An exact enumeration that does not finish within its time limit raises this error. The elementary modes of a reaction network, its smallest pathways at steady state, grow in number combinatorially. Here every pair of 14 species exchanges matter in both directions.

import networkx as nx
import numpy as np

from skcomplex.core.analysis import elementary_modes
from skcomplex.core.errors import EnumerationLimitError


def get_exchanges(size):
    arcs = list(nx.complete_graph(size, create_using=nx.DiGraph).edges)
    stoichiometry = np.zeros((size, len(arcs)))
    for column, (tail, head) in enumerate(arcs):
        stoichiometry[tail, column], stoichiometry[head, column] = -1, 1
    return stoichiometry


try:
    elementary_modes(get_exchanges(14), timeout=0.2)
except EnumerationLimitError as error:
    message = str(error)
message, elementary_modes(get_exchanges(3)).modes.shape

('The enumeration over 182 variables did not finish within 0.2 s. Close exchanges, or enumerate a subnetwork.',
 (5, 6))

The message says that the enumeration over 182 variables did not finish within 0.2 s, and suggests closing exchanges or enumerating a subnetwork. The fix is a smaller network, or a longer timeout. Three species give 5 modes over 6 exchanges: the three pairs that trade back and forth and the two cycles through all three.

docs.title: MissingExtraError
docs.text:
Some ready-made systems need an optional extra, a group of packages installed apart from the library. A system of metabolism built without its extra raises this error when it imports the missing package, with a message such as the one below.

The system flux_balance needs the extra 'metabolism'. Install it with `pip install 'scikit-complexity[metabolism]'`.

The message names the system and the extra and gives the command that installs it. The fix runs the command. The page Select a ready-made system lists the extras.

docs.title: RegistryError
docs.text: A run does not raise this error. The catalog of ready-made systems reads the class variables of every system module without importing it, and all_systems raises this error when a system class is not named with the suffix System, gives its field path as no string, or computes a listed class variable at run time. It concerns those who add a system to the catalog, and the fix writes those class variables as literals, as the page Share a system shows.

docs.title: Build a custom system
docs.text: This tutorial builds one model three ways: from the parts of the core, as a subclass of a shared recipe, and as a system class with model parameters. The model is the predator and prey cycle of the snowshoe hare and the Canada lynx, and every later tutorial of the guide starts from it.

docs.title: The data
docs.text:
The Hudson's Bay Company bought the pelts of hares and lynx from trappers for two centuries, and the counts rise and fall in cycles of about ten years. Hewitt (1921, The Conservation of the Wild Life of Canada) analysed these records. The counts below are the pelts of 1900 to 1920, in thousands, as distributed with the case study of Carpenter (2018, Predator-Prey Population Dynamics: the Lotka-Volterra model in Stan) in the file knitr/lotka-volterra/hudson-bay-lynx-hare.csv of the Stan example models. That file cites the lecture notes of Howard (2009) at Texas A&M University, which trace the numbers through the notes of Mahaffy (Math 636, San Diego State University) to Purves, Sadava, Orians, and Heller, Life: The Science of Biology.

import numpy as np

years = np.arange(1900, 1921)
hares = np.array(
    [30.0, 47.2, 70.2, 77.4, 36.3, 20.6, 18.1, 21.4, 22.0, 25.4, 27.1]
    + [40.3, 57.0, 76.6, 52.3, 19.5, 11.2, 7.6, 14.6, 16.2, 24.7]
)
lynx = np.array(
    [4.0, 6.1, 9.8, 35.2, 59.4, 41.7, 19.0, 13.0, 8.3, 9.1, 7.4]
    + [8.0, 12.3, 19.5, 45.7, 51.1, 29.7, 15.8, 9.7, 10.1, 8.6]
)
int(years[hares.argmax()]), int(years[lynx.argmax()])

(1903, 1904)

The hares peak in 1903 and the lynx a year later, in 1904. The predators follow their prey.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
Lotka and Volterra wrote the cycle as two equations. Hares H are born at the rate alpha H and are hunted at the rate beta H L. Lynx L gain at the rate delta H L from the hares they eat and die at the rate gamma L:

dH/dt = alpha H - beta H L
dL/dt = delta H L - gamma L

Carpenter estimated alpha = 0.55, beta = 0.028, gamma = 0.80, and delta = 0.024 per year, the means of the posterior of a Bayesian fit. The sections below use these rates and start from the records of 1900, 30.0 thousand hares and 4.0 thousand lynx.

docs.title: From the parts of the core
docs.text:
Each population is a DeclaredElement with one state x, and each term of the equations is a RateInteraction. An interaction that reads the other population names it in sources, and its rate reads it as s.sources[0]. How the parts fit explains each part in turn.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

hare_population = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(30.0, StateSpec())})
lynx_population = DeclaredElement('lynx', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(4.0, StateSpec())})
births = RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: 0.55 * s.target.x)
hunting = RateInteraction(
    'hunting', target='hares', state='x', sources=['lynx'], rate=lambda s: -0.028 * s.target.x * s.sources[0].x
)
feeding = RateInteraction(
    'feeding', target='lynx', state='x', sources=['hares'], rate=lambda s: 0.024 * s.target.x * s.sources[0].x
)
deaths = RateInteraction('deaths', target='lynx', state='x', rate=lambda s: -0.80 * s.target.x)
pelts = CompositeSystem(
    elements=[hare_population, lynx_population], interactions=[births, hunting, feeding, deaths]
)
trajectory = simulate(pelts, until=20, dt=1.0)
trajectory.get_values('hares.x').round(1)[:6].tolist()

[30.0, 46.4, 68.5, 81.2, 48.8, 18.6]

The simulated hares rise from 30.0 to 81.2 thousand in 1903, the year of the highest count of pelts, and fall to 18.6 thousand in 1905. The root mean square difference to the records, 7.8 thousand pelts, measures the fit.

fit = np.sqrt(np.mean((trajectory.get_values('hares.x') - hares) ** 2))
round(float(fit), 1)

7.8

docs.title: As a subclass of a shared recipe
docs.text:
The model is a set of reactions between two species. ReactionNetworkSystem of skcomplex.systems.general.reactions builds one element per species and one reaction per row of a table, with a propensity of mass action, the rate constant times the product of the reactant amounts. A subclass takes the parameters of the model under its own names and returns the species and the reactions. Each row holds the reactants, the products, and the rate constant.

from skcomplex.systems.general.reactions import ReactionNetworkSystem


class HareLynxSystem(ReactionNetworkSystem):
    until = 20.0
    dt = 1.0

    def __init__(
        self, hares=30.0, lynx=4.0, *, alpha=0.55, beta=0.028, gamma=0.80, delta=0.024, mode='rate', label='system'
    ):
        super().__init__(mode=mode, label=label)
        self.hares = hares
        self.lynx = lynx
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.delta = delta

    def _get_species(self):
        return {'hares': self.hares, 'lynx': self.lynx}

    def _get_reactions(self):
        return {
            'births': ({'hares': 1}, {'hares': 2}, self.alpha),
            'hunting': ({'hares': 1, 'lynx': 1}, {'lynx': 1}, self.beta),
            'feeding': ({'hares': 1, 'lynx': 1}, {'hares': 1, 'lynx': 2}, self.delta),
            'deaths': ({'lynx': 1}, {}, self.gamma),
        }


simulate(HareLynxSystem()).get_values('hares.x').round(1)[:6].tolist()

[30.0, 46.4, 68.5, 81.2, 48.8, 18.6]

The values match the composite system above. The class variables until and dt are tuned run settings, which simulate reads when a call leaves them out. The recipe also runs the same reactions as random events, which suits a small population.

jumps = HareLynxSystem(hares=30, lynx=4, mode='jump')
sorted(jumps.get_tags().laws), jumps.get_tags().randomness

(['jump'], 'stochastic')

docs.title: As a system class with model parameters
docs.text:
A BaseSystem subclass writes its parts in _build_system from its model parameters, so set_params, clone, and the experiments of the library change them by name.

from skcomplex.core.components.systems import BaseSystem


class PeltSystem(BaseSystem):
    until = 20.0
    dt = 1.0

    def __init__(self, hares=30.0, lynx=4.0, *, alpha=0.55, beta=0.028, gamma=0.80, delta=0.024, label='system'):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.hares = hares
        self.lynx = lynx
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.delta = delta

    def _build_system(self):
        prey = DeclaredElement('hares', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(self.hares, StateSpec())})
        predators = DeclaredElement('lynx', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(self.lynx, StateSpec())})
        alpha, beta, gamma, delta = self.alpha, self.beta, self.gamma, self.delta
        interactions = [
            RateInteraction('births', target='hares', state='x', rate=lambda s: alpha * s.target.x),
            RateInteraction(
                'hunting',
                target='hares',
                state='x',
                sources=['lynx'],
                rate=lambda s: -beta * s.target.x * s.sources[0].x,
            ),
            RateInteraction(
                'feeding',
                target='lynx',
                state='x',
                sources=['hares'],
                rate=lambda s: delta * s.target.x * s.sources[0].x,
            ),
            RateInteraction('deaths', target='lynx', state='x', rate=lambda s: -gamma * s.target.x),
        ]
        return CompositeSystem(elements=[prey, predators], interactions=interactions)


system = PeltSystem()
simulate(system).get_values('lynx.x').round(1)[:6].tolist()

[4.0, 4.4, 7.9, 22.5, 52.3, 49.5]

A faster birth rate of the hares raises their highest count over the twenty years from 81.2 to 85.8 thousand.

faster = simulate(system.set_params(alpha=0.65)).get_values('hares.x')
round(float(faster.max()), 1)

85.8

docs.title: The catalog class
docs.text:
LotkaVolterraSystem of skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology is the same model, ready made, with the rates r, a, b, and d. The later tutorials start from it in one line.

from skcomplex.systems.biology.ecology import LotkaVolterraSystem

catalog = LotkaVolterraSystem(prey=30.0, predators=4.0, r=0.55, a=0.028, b=0.024, d=0.80)
simulate(catalog, until=20, dt=1.0).get_values('prey.x').round(1)[:6].tolist()

[30.0, 46.4, 68.5, 81.2, 48.8, 18.6]

docs.title: Agent-based systems
docs.text: This page writes the behaviour of individual agents as plain Python and lets them move, eat, reproduce, and die on a grid, a network, or a continuous space. An agent is a member of a population that acts on its own rules, reads its surroundings, and changes them.

docs.title: Agents with rules
docs.text:
This section builds a population of foragers that wander a torus, find food, split when they are full, and starve when they are empty. Agents are ordinary elements whose laws are rules written as code. An Element subclass declares the states every agent holds and the parameters its group shares, as annotated arguments of its __init__. Its _get_laws returns a RuleLaw, whose function takes the agent and the system. A GroupElement built with variable=True holds the 50 foragers and lets them be created and removed during a run, and a periodic LatticeSpace of 30 by 30 cells holds the torus.

from typing import Annotated

from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import oo
from sage.sets.real_set import RealSet

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RuleLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, StateSpec, VisualSpec


class ForagerElement(Element):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label,
        visual=VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'food'}),
        *,
        food: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 5.0,
        hunger: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ):
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.food = food
        self.hunger = hunger

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.forage)]

    def forage(self, agent, system):
        cells = agent.get_neighbor_cells()
        agent.move_to(cells[int(system.rng.integers(len(cells)))])
        agent.food += system.rng.poisson(0.8) - agent.hunger
        if agent.food <= 0:
            agent.remove()
        elif agent.food > 10:
            agent.food /= 2
            agent.create(food=agent.food)


foragers = CompositeSystem(
    elements=[GroupElement('foragers', element=ForagerElement, size=50, variable=True)],
    space=LatticeSpace((30, 30), boundary='periodic'),
)
trajectory = simulate(foragers, until=20, random_state=0)
int(trajectory.get_values('foragers.count')[-1]), len(trajectory.get_agents('foragers', 20).ids)

(17, 17)

Of the 50 foragers, 17 are alive after 20 steps, and the frame of step 20 holds the ids of the same 17. Each forager gains a Poisson number of units of food with mean 0.8 per step and loses 1, so most of them starve.

An element or a group whose laws include rules is an agent, and so is every member of a variable group. In a system with rules, a group whose element type has no laws is a group of passive agents that rules read and change, unless an interaction whose laws are not rules binds it.

A system with rules is agent-based. It runs in discrete time on MesaSolver, one Mesa step per unit of time, with every agent activated in random order. MesaSolver declares what it runs like any solver, so simulate(system, solver=MesaSolver()) raises a TagError that names the laws, spaces, or times it does not support.

An agent acts on itself and on its surroundings through the view that its rule receives.

  • An agent reads and sets its states as attributes, and reads the parameters of its group, which change live like any parameter.
  • neighbors, neighbor_cells, agents_here, move_to, create, and remove act on its place and its population. Only the members of a group declared variable=True are created and removed during a run.
  • agent.get_neighbors(group=path) and agent.get_agents_here(path) read the agents of one group around the agent and at its place. So the agents of a variable group on the nodes of a network make a set of members per node that grows and that neighbours read, as the guide on networks shows.
  • agent.get_displacement_to(other) gives the vector to another agent or a location, the shortest one on a torus, and agent.get_distance_to(other) its length, or the number of hops on a network.
  • agent.group is the path of the group of the agent, and agent.group_label its label.

Agents live on a lattice, a network, or a continuous space.

  • GroupElement(label, element=..., size=..., location=...) places the agents at cell coordinates, network nodes, or positions, one per agent or one shared. Agents without a location take random places.
  • A LatticeSpace gives agents Moore or von Neumann neighbourhoods and an optional cell capacity, a NetworkSpace places agents on the nodes of a NetworkX graph, and a ContinuousSpace finds neighbours within a radius.
  • system.dimensions gives the extent of the space per axis, and system.torus whether it wraps.

The system view gives a rule access to the rest of the run.

  • system.rng is the random generator, system.get_agents(name) and system.count(name) read the other agents, and the view also lists the empty cells.
  • Every rule receives the system view scoped to the interaction or agent group that owns it. system.get_parameter('name') reads a parameter of the owner. system.get_agents('role') reads the group bound to a role of the owner, then a group by its path relative to the system of the owner, then by its path from the root. So a rule works unchanged in a subsystem.
  • Interactions with agent rules bind any number of agent groups, of any sizes, through their roles.

A run records every agent. Frames and trajectories hold the agents of every group with their ids, states, and locations, through trajectory.get_agents(group, frame), and the count of every group as the reporter <group>.count. The catalog has Schelling segregation as SchellingSystem, the voter system as VoterSystem, Boltzmann wealth exchange as BoltzmannWealthSystem, and the wolf and sheep system as WolfSheepSystem.

docs.title: Rules of interactions
docs.text:
This section gives a rule to an interaction, which reads the groups bound to its roles. A role is a named slot of an interaction that a group fills when the system binds it. Here five walkers drift along a periodic road of length 50 in a ContinuousSpace, inside a subsystem. An Interaction subclass counts the pairs closer than its reach of 10 at every step and appends the count to a list.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import Interaction
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RuleLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import ContinuousSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, RoleSpec


class WalkerElement(Element):
    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.step)]

    def step(self, agent, system):
        width, height = system.dimensions
        x, y = agent.location
        agent.move_to(((x + system.rng.uniform(0, 2)) % width, y))


class SpreadInteraction(Interaction):
    def __init__(self, label, *, walkers: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()], reach: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 10.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.walkers = walkers
        self.reach = reach

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.measure)]

    def measure(self, system):
        walkers = system.get_agents('walkers')
        close = [a for a in walkers for b in walkers if a != b and a.get_distance_to(b) < system.get_parameter('reach')]
        counts.append(len(close) // 2)


counts = []
places = [(10.0 * index, 0.5) for index in range(5)]
road = CompositeSystem(
    systems=[
        CompositeSystem(
            'road',
            elements=[GroupElement('walkers', element=WalkerElement, size=5, location=places)],
            interactions=[SpreadInteraction('spread', walkers='walkers')],
        ),
    ],
    space=ContinuousSpace(extent=(50.0, 1.0), boundary='periodic'),
)
trajectory = simulate(road, until=5, random_state=0)
counts

[3, 2, 3, 3, 2]

The counts of close pairs over the five steps are 3, 2, 3, 3, and 2. The rule reads its walkers by the role name 'walkers' and its reach by system.get_parameter('reach'), so it runs unchanged inside the subsystem road.

docs.title: Phases, institutions, and learning
docs.text:
This section orders each step into phases, lets an institution set policy, and lets agents learn from their past. A phase is a named part of a step whose rules run before those of the next phase. Traders quote bids in one phase, and in the next a clerk reads the best bid and sets a fee of one percent of it. A DiscreteTime with a PhasesScheduleSpec lists the two phases.

from typing import Annotated, ClassVar

import numpy as np

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import Interaction
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RuleLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import DiscreteTime
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, PhaseSpec, PhasesScheduleSpec, StateSpec


class TraderElement(Element):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label,
        *,
        value: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        bid: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
    ):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.value = value
        self.bid = bid

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.quote, phase='quote')]

    def quote(self, agent, system):
        agent.bid = system.rng.uniform(0, agent.value)


class ClerkInteraction(Interaction):
    law_classes: ClassVar[tuple[type, ...]] = (RuleLaw,)
    reports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ('best',)

    def __init__(self, label, *, fee: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.fee = fee

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.act, phase='settle')]

    def act(self, system):
        best = max(agent.bid for agent in system.get_agents('traders'))
        system.report('best', best)
        system.set_parameter('fee', 0.01 * best)


values = {'value': np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(0.5, 2, 20)}
market = CompositeSystem(
    elements=[GroupElement('traders', element=TraderElement, size=20, values=values)],
    interactions=[ClerkInteraction('clerk')],
    time=DiscreteTime(schedule=PhasesScheduleSpec([PhaseSpec('quote'), PhaseSpec('settle')])),
)
trajectory = simulate(market, until=3, random_state=0)
[round(float(best), 3) for best in trajectory.get_values('clerk.best')[1:]], round(float(trajectory.get_values('clerk.fee')[-1]), 4)

([1.668, 1.537, 1.577], 0.0158)

The best bids of the three steps are 1.668, 1.537, and 1.577, and the fee ends at 0.0158, one percent of the last best bid. The clerk publishes the best bid as the reporter clerk.best, and the trajectory records the fee as a parameter.

Phases. DiscreteTime(schedule=PhasesScheduleSpec([...])) lists the phases of a step.

  • A PhaseSpec(name, activation, repeat) runs its agents 'random'ly, 'sequential'ly in order of creation, 'simultaneous'ly, or 'by-type', for repeat rounds, such as intraday rounds.
  • In a simultaneous phase every rule reads the states of the start of the phase, and the writes apply at its end.
  • The activation 'visits' runs visits times as many visits as the agents of groups at the start of the phase. Each visit goes to an agent drawn with replacement, which runs its rules of the phase, the rules of its element and then its member rules, at the time k + i / n of visit i of n in step k.
  • RuleLaw(function, phase=name) puts a rule in a phase. Rules without a phase run in the phase 'default', which runs first unless the system lists it. So systems without phases keep one random activation per step.

Markets. A market that matches buyers with sellers is the recipe MatchingInteraction of the general realizations, which runs a batch auction with phases and a clerk.

Agent operations. These interactions of skcomplex.core.components.interactions run as agent rules.

  • TransferInteraction moves amounts of states between members, the agents of one cell, a Source, and a Sink. It runs as transfer laws with form='symbolic', or between paired agents with form='agent'.
  • system.get_composition(group, state) counts the agents of a group by the value of a state, kept up to date as agents change, so a birth probability can read the composition of the population.
  • GroupingInteraction draws pairs, partitions, neighbourhoods, or groups by a state every step, and acts on each.
  • TopologyInteraction adds and removes nodes and edges of a network, and rewires edges towards a weight.
  • The movement of agents and their birth and death are the recipes MovementInteraction and BirthDeathInteraction of the general realizations.

Institutions. An Interaction whose law is RuleLaw(self.act, phase=...) acts once per round of its phase, as the clerk above does. Economics names such an institution PolicyRuleInteraction.

  • It reads system.get_observable(name), the reporters and the observables of the run at the end of earlier steps through system.get_history(name, window), and the agents.
  • It sets parameters of any element or interaction with system.set_parameter(name, value). Rules see the change at once, and the trajectory records it.
  • It declares its own parameters as annotated arguments of its __init__, as the clerk declares fee.
  • Elements and interactions declare the values they publish in the class variable reports, and publish them with system.report(name, value). system.storage keeps private values of an element or an interaction across the steps of a run.

Learning. Agents learn from their own past and from each other.

  • agent.get_lags(state, window), a method of the agent view a rule receives, returns the past values of a state declared with lags, StateSpec(lags=m). A rule writes adaptive, trend-following, anchoring, and fundamentalist forecasts from these values.
  • A MapInteraction built with form='agent' and schedule='member' moves a score towards a realized payoff in the activation of every member, such as one visit. The economics PayoffLearningInteraction names this learning.
  • Choosing an option by its utility, copying the best neighbour, and evolving strategies are the recipes ChoiceInteraction, ImitationInteraction, and EvolutionInteraction of the general realizations.

docs.title: Porting Mesa systems
docs.text:
This section brings an existing Mesa model over, so its parameters become live, validated, and recorded. Mesa is the Python library of agent-based modelling that runs the steps of these systems. A Mesa model is ported piece by piece. Its agent class becomes an element whose step is a RuleLaw, and its agent attributes become states. The attributes of its Model become parameters, which then change live, are validated, and are recorded like those of any system. Here ten coins flip ten times each with the bias 0.5.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RuleLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import DiscreteTime
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, StateSpec


class CoinElement(Element):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label,
        *,
        heads: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        bias: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.5,
    ):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.heads = heads
        self.bias = bias

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RuleLaw(self.flip)]

    def flip(self, agent, system):
        agent.heads += float(system.rng.random() < agent.bias)


coins = CompositeSystem('coins', elements=[GroupElement('coins', element=CoinElement, size=10)], time=DiscreteTime())
int(simulate(coins, until=10, random_state=0).get_agents('coins', 10).values['heads'].sum())

54

The ten coins show 54 heads in 100 flips. Mesa still runs the steps, as the backend of agent-based systems.

docs.title: Anomalous processes
docs.text: This page writes processes that depart from ordinary diffusion and exponential decay. They have heavy-tailed jumps, events that fire after waiting times from any distribution, noise whose increments are correlated over the whole run, or derivatives of fractional order. A heavy tail means that very large values are far more likely than under a normal distribution.

docs.title: Draws from SciPy distributions
docs.text:
This section draws from any distribution of scipy.stats, such as a Lévy stable law for long flights. The function draw(name, distribution, **parameters) takes the name of the distribution, such as 'pareto', 'lomax', 'expon', 'beta', or 'levy_stable', with its shape parameters, loc, and scale as keywords.

Here 100 fliers each take a step drawn from a symmetric stable law of index 1.5 on every step, through an UpdateLaw of an Element subclass that a GroupElement repeats.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import UpdateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import draw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class FlierElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [UpdateLaw(s.x, s.x + draw('jump', 'levy_stable', alpha=1.5, beta=0.0))]


fliers = CompositeSystem(elements=[GroupElement('fliers', element=FlierElement, size=100)])
flight = simulate(fliers, until=20, dt=1.0, random_state=0)
flight.get_values('fliers.x').shape

(21, 100)

The positions hold 21 frames, the start and 20 steps, of 100 fliers each. The steps show the heavy tail. The largest step is about ninety times the median one.

import numpy as np

steps = np.abs(np.diff(flight.get_values('fliers.x'), axis=0))
int(steps.max()), round(float(np.median(steps)), 1)

(91, 1.0)

The largest of the 2000 steps has a length of 91, and the median length is 1.0. A SciPy draw follows these rules.

  • The keywords can be expressions of states and parameters.
  • A SciPy draw follows the rules of the other named draws, and it samples with the distribution's rvs and the random generator of the run.
  • Compiling rejects a name scipy.stats does not provide, listing the closest names, and keywords the distribution does not take.
  • In update laws, a SciPy draw is sampled for every member before each step, and the map then steps in Python with the compiled update of the backend.

docs.title: Jumps on clocks of waiting times
docs.text:
This section fires an event after a random waiting time, such as a trapped particle that escapes after a heavy-tailed wait. JumpLaw(waiting=..., reset=..., label=...) fires after a waiting time, applies its reset to the states all at once, and draws the next waiting time from the states after the reset. A renewal is one such firing.

Here 1000 walkers wait a Pareto time of index 0.5, which has no finite mean, and then jump by a normal step.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import JumpLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import draw, normal
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, StateSpec


class WalkerElement(Element):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.5,
    ):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x
        self.alpha = alpha

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        waiting = draw('wait', 'pareto', b=s.alpha)
        return [JumpLaw(waiting=waiting, reset={s.x: s.x + normal('jump', 0, 1)}, label='jumps')]


walkers = CompositeSystem(elements=[GroupElement('walkers', element=WalkerElement, size=1000)])
walk = simulate(walkers, until=1000, dt=100.0, random_state=0)
walk.problem.form.value, bool(walk.get_values('jumps.renewals')[-1] > 1000)

('renewal process', True)

The system compiles to the form 'renewal process', and the 1000 walkers renew more than 1000 times by time 1000. The clocks follow these rules.

  • Every member of a group renews on its own clock.
  • Draws in the waiting time and the reset take a fresh value at every renewal of every member, and every use of one name in a renewal reads the same value.
  • A waiting time that is a single draw must come from a distribution with nonnegative support. Compiling rejects one that can be negative, such as normal.

A system or partition whose only laws are such jumps compiles to the renewal form. RenewalSolver runs it exactly, from renewal to renewal with no time grid, and a frame holds the states the last renewal at or before its time set.

These jumps also combine with the rate and noise laws of the same element, which evolve the states between renewals. RK4Solver and EulerMaruyamaSolver stop every member at its own renewals when the members do not interact. When a law sums over the group, they split the step at every renewal time for all members. Other steppers reject these jumps.

The trajectory records every renewal pass as a RenewalRecord among its events, with the time and the member of every renewal and the member's states before and after it. The observable <label>.renewals counts the renewals up to every frame. The Rerun observer streams it as a time series, and the renewals as text entries under renewals/<label>. The compiler keeps the count of every member in a hidden state, <group>.<label>~renewals.

docs.title: Fractional noise
docs.text:
This section drives a state with noise that remembers its past, as in rough or persistent paths. NoiseLaw(targets, value, hurst=hurst) drives a state with fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index 0 < H < 1. The Hurst index sets how the increments correlate.

Here 500 walkers follow rough paths of index 0.3 with amplitude 1 up to time 1.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import NoiseLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import FractionalEulerMaruyamaSolver
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class RoughElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [NoiseLaw(s.x, 1, hurst=0.3)]


walkers = CompositeSystem(elements=[GroupElement('walkers', element=RoughElement, size=500)])
rough = simulate(walkers, until=1, dt=0.1, solver=FractionalEulerMaruyamaSolver(dt=0.01), random_state=0)
round(float(rough.get_values('walkers.x')[-1].var()), 1)

1.0

The variance of the positions at time 1 is 1.0, the variance t^(2H) of fractional Brownian motion at t = 1. The noise follows these rules.

  • The increments anticorrelate for H < 1/2 and correlate for H > 1/2.
  • A Hurst index of 1/2 compiles to a noise law without one. For other indices the amplitude must not depend on any state.
  • FractionalEulerMaruyamaSolver(dt, horizon) is the stepper of systems with fractional noise. When it first advances, it draws the increments of the whole run on its grid, with the circulant embedding of Davies and Harte over scipy.fft. So frames must fall on multiples of dt.
  • simulate passes the end of the run as the horizon, and advancing beyond it raises HorizonError.
  • Other SDE steppers reject fractional noise with an error that names FractionalEulerMaruyamaSolver.
  • fractional_gaussian_noise returns the noise paths themselves.

These ready-made systems have memory: ContinuousTimeRandomWalkSystem, LevyWalkSystem, AnnealedTransientTimeMotionSystem, FractionalBrownianMotionSystem, and LevyFlightSystem of skcomplex.systems.physics.soft_matter, and TrapSystem of skcomplex.systems.physics.statistical_mechanics.

docs.title: Fractional derivatives
docs.text:
This section gives a state a derivative of fractional order, for relaxation that is slower than any exponential. A state declared with a fractional order, StateSpec(order=0.6), has a Caputo derivative of that order. The Caputo derivative of order alpha weighs the whole past of the rate of change with a kernel that decays as a power of time.

Here a state relaxes under a RateLaw with D^0.6 x = -x from 1.0, and the run compares with the exact solution at time 20.

from typing import Annotated

from skcomplex.core.analysis import symbolic
from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import L1Solver
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class RelaxingElement(Element):
    def __init__(self, label, *, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=0.6)] = 1.0):
        super().__init__(label)
        self.x = x

    def _get_laws(self, s):
        return [RateLaw(s.x, -s.x)]


system = CompositeSystem(elements=[RelaxingElement('a')])
relaxing = simulate(system, until=20, dt=1.0, solver=L1Solver(dt=0.01, memory=10.0))
solution = symbolic(system, kind='solve', use_initial_state=True).solutions['a.x'].rhs()
exact = solution.subs({solution.variables()[0]: 20.0})
relaxing.problem.form.value, abs(float(relaxing.get_values('a.x')[-1]) - float(exact)) < 1e-3

('fractional differential equations', True)

The system compiles to the form 'fractional differential equations', and the simulated relaxation matches the exact Mittag-Leffler solution to within 1e-3 at time 20.

The rate laws on a fractional state give its derivative, D^alpha x = f(t, x), and superpose as for any state, so no other law kind is needed. Order 1 is the ordinary rate law. The derivative of order alpha at a time depends on the whole past of the state, so the solution relaxes like a Mittag-Leffler function, slower than any exponential.

A system with a state of a fractional order compiles to the fractional form, with the order of every state component in problem.orders. The states of order 1 of the same system keep their ordinary equations. Three steppers integrate the fractional form on a fixed grid from the start of the run, so frames must fall on multiples of their dt.

  • GrunwaldLetnikovSolver(dt, memory=None) weighs the past states with the binomial weights (-1)^j binomial(alpha, j).
  • L1Solver(dt, memory=None) interpolates the state linearly between grid points inside the Caputo integral.
  • FractionalABMSolver(dt) is the predictor-corrector of Diethelm, Ford, and Freed, of order 1 + alpha for smooth solutions, and the default.

The two explicit schemes are of order 1. All three keep the whole history, so a run of n steps costs n^2 operations. memory bounds that cost. The history of the last memory time units enters with its exact weights, and the older history enters through about 40 exponential modes fitted to the weights, so every step costs the same. For fractional relaxation of order 0.6, a window of 10 time units stays within 1e-8 of the whole history at time 20. A change of a fractional state between frames, such as one a schedule makes, starts a new history from the changed state.

simulate reports the misuses of fractional orders before compiling, each with the path of the state and a fix.

  • fractional-order: an order that is neither an integer nor in (0, 1).
  • fractional-time: a fractional state in a system whose declared time is not continuous.
  • order-unsupported: a chosen solver or backend that does not integrate fractional orders.
  • solver-unsupported: a law on a fractional state that no fractional solver runs, such as a noise law.

Solvers and backends declare the kinds of order they integrate in the orders field of their SupportSpec, 'integer' or 'fractional'. The NumPy and Numba backends run the fractional form.

symbolic(system, kind='solve') solves one linear fractional relaxation D^alpha x = c x as x(0) E_alpha(c t^alpha). It writes the solution with the symbolic function mittag_leffler, which evaluates numerically. It sums the power series in arbitrary precision with Sage for moderate arguments, and takes the asymptotic expansion for large ones. symbolic(system) writes a Caputo derivative as caputo(x(t), t, alpha).

The order belongs to the element type, so a sweep over orders builds one system per order. These ready-made systems of skcomplex.systems.mathematics.fractional_dynamics take the order as a model parameter: FractionalRelaxationSystem, FractionalOscillatorSystem, FractionalVanDerPolSystem, and FractionalLorenzSystem.

docs.title: Cell complexes and link fields
docs.text: This page puts states on the links and plaquettes of a lattice, or on the edges and faces of a network, as lattice gauge theories and discrete exterior calculus do. A cell complex is a set of cells of rising degree, sites of degree 0, links of degree 1, and plaquettes or faces of degree 2, where each cell is bounded by cells of the degree below. A CellComplexSpace holds these cells with the oriented incidence between them. It is a NetworkSpace, so groups on its 'edges' and 'hyperedges' hold states on links and plaquettes.

docs.title: Cells of lattices and networks
docs.text:
This section builds the complex of a torus and of a tetrahedron and reads how their cells connect. The matrix incidences_[k] has one row per cell of degree k + 1 and one column per cell of degree k. An entry is plus or minus one when the lower cell lies on the boundary of the higher one, with the sign of their orientations. The torus is a periodic LatticeSpace of 8 by 8 sites.

import networkx as nx

from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CellComplexSpace, LatticeSpace, NetworkSpace

torus = CellComplexSpace(LatticeSpace((8, 8))).prepare()
[matrix.shape for matrix in torus.incidences_], (torus.incidences_[1] @ torus.incidences_[0]).count_nonzero()

([(128, 64), (64, 128)], 0)

The torus has 64 sites, 128 links, and 64 plaquettes, so the matrices have the shapes (128, 64) and (64, 128). Their product has no nonzero entry, since the boundary of a boundary is empty. The complex of a network takes its faces from one of several sources, and the cliques of the complete graph on four nodes fill a tetrahedron.

tetrahedron = NetworkSpace(nx.complete_graph(4))
cliques = CellComplexSpace(tetrahedron, faces='cliques', dimension=3).prepare()
cliques.incidences_[2].shape

(1, 4)

The shape (1, 4) holds the one solid tetrahedron and its four triangles. The cells follow these rules.

  • The links of a lattice point along the positive direction of their axis. Fixed and reflecting edges drop the cells that leave the box.
  • A network takes faces=None for a minimum cycle basis, 'hyperedges' for its hyperedges, 'cliques' for its cliques up to dimension, or a sequence of node cycles.

docs.title: Exterior calculus
docs.text:
This section writes field equations on a complex with the operators of discrete exterior calculus. The exterior derivative d maps a state on cells of one degree to the next, as the gradient maps a potential to a field on links. The codifferential maps back down, as the divergence does. Here a potential A on the links of the torus follows the lattice Maxwell equations dA/dt = -E and dE/dt = codifferential(d A). Two RateInteractions write them on a GroupElement on the edges of the complex.

from typing import Annotated

import numpy as np

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import codifferential, exterior_derivative
from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CellComplexSpace, LatticeSpace
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec


class FieldLinkElement(Element):
    def __init__(
        self,
        label,
        visual=None,
        *,
        A: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        E: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
    ):
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.A = A
        self.E = E


space = CellComplexSpace(LatticeSpace((8, 8))).prepare()
potential = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=128)
links = GroupElement('links', element=FieldLinkElement, space=space, on='edges', values={'A': potential})
interactions = [
    RateInteraction('potential', target='links', state='A', rate=lambda n: -n.target.E),
