  • Backends: any
  • Arguments:
    • label: The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'infection'.
    • source: The path of the element or group the amounts leave.
    • target: The path of the element or group the amounts enter, the source again for a transfer within members.
    • state: The name of the state of the source the first leg takes from, or Source() for the environment.
    • into: The name of the state of the target the first leg adds to, Sink() for the environment, or None for state.
    • amount: The amount of the first leg, a number or a function.
    • flow: The name the symbolic form reports the first leg under, such as 'payment', or the empty string for flow_0.
    • pairing: How members are paired.
    • legs: Further legs, each a tuple of a state or Source(), a state, Sink(), or None, an amount, and optionally the name of its flow.
    • fallback: The path of the group whose members the agent form pairs with instead of the target members in a step in which no target member lives, or None for no fallback.
    • guard: A function that returns whether a pair transfers, a condition of the namespace or a boolean of the agents, or None for every pair.
    • rate: The rate of jumps of the symbolic form, a number or a function of the namespace, or None for a continuous flow.
    • reverse_rate: The rate of the jumps of the symbolic form that move the amounts back from the target to the source, a number or a function of the namespace, or None for no reverse jumps.
    • offset: The number of places along the group order from every source member to its target member, such as 1 for the next member, or 0 to pair the members of the roles.
    • boundary: Past the ends of the group order, 'periodic' closes a ring and 'fixed' holds no member.
    • form: The lowering, 'symbolic' to transfer laws or 'agent' to an agent rule.
    • schedule: The order of the agent form, 'random-sequential' over the pairs, or 'member' over the actors.
    • actor: The role whose members act under the schedule 'member', 'source' or 'target'.
    • partners: The number of partners an actor draws at random under the schedule 'member', or None for all of them.
    • remove: The member of a pair that transfers that is removed, 'source', 'target', or None.
    • phase: The phase the rule of the agent form runs in, or None for the default phase.
    • settlement: A function settlement(source, target, amounts, system) that settles a pair of agents from the amounts of the legs, read once, in place of moving them, or None to move them.

docs.title: A compatible interaction
docs.text:
A RateInteraction returns a rate law of continuous time, and its target accepts the real amount of a declared element.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

tank = DeclaredElement('tank', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(10.0, StateSpec())})
decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='tank', state='x', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.x)
sorted(decay.get_tags().laws), sorted(decay.get_tags().time)
trajectory = simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[tank], interactions=[decay]), until=2)
round(trajectory.get_values('tank.x')[-1], 2)

(['rate'], ['continuous'])
3.68

The decay has the law kind rate and the time continuous, and the tank falls from 10 to 3.68 after two time units.

docs.title: An incompatible interaction
docs.text:
A MapInteraction returns an update law of discrete time. It cannot join the rate in one system unless the system has a time that joins the two, so simulate raises a TagError that names the tag the parts disagree on.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import MapInteraction, RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.errors import TagError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

tank = DeclaredElement('tank', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(10.0, StateSpec())})
decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='tank', state='x', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.x)
halve = MapInteraction('halve', target='tank', state='x', function=lambda s: s.target.x / 2)
sorted(halve.get_tags().laws), sorted(halve.get_tags().time)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[tank], interactions=[decay, halve]), until=1)
except TagError as error:
    message = str(error)
message
assert "tag 'time'" in message

(['update'], ['discrete'])
The parts 'decay' and 'halve' disagree on the tag 'time': 'decay' has continuous and 'halve' has discrete. Give the system a time that joins them, or bind parts of one time.

The map has the law kind update and the time discrete. The message says that decay and halve disagree on the tag time, and asks for a time that joins them or for parts of one time.

docs.title: Laws
docs.text:
A law is the mathematical object an interaction returns, such as a rate, a noise, a jump, or an update. Its kind is a tag, and so are the times and spaces it runs in and its randomness, which says whether it draws random numbers. The law kinds of a system are those of its interactions, and a solver or a backend runs a system only when it supports every one of them. The table lists the kind, time, space, and randomness that each law class declares.

Law Kind Time Space Randomness ArrayUpdateLaw update discrete hypergraph, lattice, network deterministic BilinearLaw rate continuous lattice deterministic BoundaryLaw update any any deterministic CascadeLaw update discrete hypergraph, lattice, network deterministic CrossingLaw update continuous any deterministic DissipatorLaw rate continuous any deterministic EquationLaw equation continuous, static any deterministic ExtremalLaw update discrete hypergraph, lattice, network stochastic FluxLaw rate continuous continuous, lattice deterministic GeneratorLaw rate continuous any deterministic GradientStepLaw update discrete any deterministic JumpLaw jump continuous any stochastic LinearProgramLaw equation any any deterministic LocalRuleLaw update discrete hypergraph, lattice, network deterministic MatchLaw update discrete any deterministic NoiseLaw noise continuous any stochastic ProductionLaw update discrete any deterministic RateLaw rate continuous any deterministic RuleLaw update discrete any deterministic SampleLaw sampling discrete hypergraph, lattice, network stochastic SubstitutionLaw update discrete any deterministic TransferLaw update any any deterministic TransitionLaw jump discrete any stochastic UpdateLaw update discrete any deterministic

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Class What it adds Choose it when Uses ArrayUpdateLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which gives the next value of each member by an expression, it hands the whole array to a Python function. The change depends on the whole array at once, such as one random site. A sandpile adds a grain at a random site, a molecular model replays recorded configurations, and a genetic model mutates one random site of a genome. BaseLaw Unlike BasePart, it belongs to another part and is not added to a system on its own. A new kind of dynamics needs a lowering of its own, and choose an existing law, such as RateLaw or UpdateLaw, otherwise. It appears in every field through its subclasses, such as the rate of an epidemic, the next value of a cellular automaton, a chemical reaction as a random jump, and Kirchhoff's laws as equations. BilinearLaw Unlike RateLaw, which gives the rate of one state by an expression, it sums a product of two distributions over every pair of classes. The change of a population comes from binary meetings of its members. Traders exchange wealth when they meet, people shift their opinion after a conversation, immune cells destroy tumour cells they meet, and gas molecules change velocity when they collide. BoundaryLaw Unlike CrossingLaw, which finds the exact time a guard crosses zero, it corrects the state once per step. A state must stay inside a domain and the exact time of contact does not matter. Particles in a periodic box wrap around its edges, a random walker reflects off a wall, and an angle wraps into the interval from minus pi to pi. CascadeLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which runs once per step, it runs its relax laws until the lattice settles, so one step holds a whole avalanche. A slow drive and fast relaxation are separated in time, as in self-organized criticality. Grains topple in the sandpile model of Bak, Tang, and Wiesenfeld, slips spread along a fault in the earthquake model of Olami, Feder, and Christensen, and trees burn in a forest fire model. CrossingLaw Unlike BoundaryLaw, which corrects a state once per step, it finds the time of the event within the tolerance of the solver. The time of the event matters, such as an impact or a threshold. A ball bounces off the floor, a neuron fires when its potential reaches a threshold, and a thermostat switches a heater at a set temperature. DissipatorLaw Unlike GeneratorLaw, which adds a reversible part to the evolution, it adds an irreversible part that drives the state toward a mixture. The system exchanges energy or information with an environment. It appears in quantum optics, where an atom decays by spontaneous emission and a cavity leaks photons, and in quantum computing, where qubits lose their phase. EquationLaw Unlike RateLaw, which gives a derivative explicitly, it gives a relation that the compiler solves for the derivatives. The derivatives are coupled through a mass matrix, as in linked bodies. The equations of a double pendulum, the coupled currents of an electric circuit, and the joints of a robot arm are implicit in their accelerations. ExtremalLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which changes every member at once, it changes the one weakest or strongest site and its neighbours. Change happens at the extreme of a state, as in extremal dynamics. The least fit species mutates with its neighbours in the evolution model of Bak and Sneppen, the weakest point of a material breaks in models of fracture, and the most stressed site fails first in models of invasion percolation. FluxLaw Unlike RateLaw, which gives the rate of a state directly, it gives a flux whose divergence is the rate, so the scheme keeps the total and resolves shocks. An amount moves through space and forms sharp fronts. Traffic density forms jams on a road, a gas forms shock waves, and a flood wave travels along a river channel. GeneratorLaw Unlike DissipatorLaw, which adds an irreversible loss, it adds a reversible part that keeps the norm of the state. A state evolves by a unitary map, as a closed quantum system does. It appears in quantum mechanics, where it gives the Schrödinger equation of spins and atoms, and in quantum walks on networks, which search a graph. GradientStepLaw Unlike RateLaw, which changes states of the system in its own time, it changes parameters of another system by fitting it to data. A part of a model learns during the run. A recurrent neural network learns to predict a time series, a reservoir computer fits its readout, and an adaptive controller tunes its gains. JumpLaw Unlike RateLaw, which changes states continuously, it changes them at random instants by whole amounts. The units are few and their randomness matters. Molecules react one at a time in a cell, individuals are born and die in a small population, customers arrive at a queue, and a random walker jumps between sites. LinearProgramLaw Unlike EquationLaw, which fixes states by equations, it fixes them by an optimum under inequalities. A quantity at each time is the best choice under constraints. Flux balance analysis finds the fluxes of a metabolic network, an economy dispatches power plants at least cost, and a planner allocates production under capacity limits. LocalRuleLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which gives the next value by an expression of one member, it reads the ordered neighbourhood of each cell. The next value of a cell depends on the exact pattern around it. Conway's Game of Life, elementary cellular automata, models of excitable tissue, and models of traffic on a ring road follow local rules. MatchLaw Unlike RuleLaw, which acts on members, it forms the pairs that rules then act on. Who meets whom is itself part of the model. Workers match with firms in a labour market, students match with schools, buyers meet sellers in an order book, and partners pair in models of mating. NoiseLaw Unlike RateLaw, which adds a deterministic part, it adds a random part, and together they form a stochastic differential equation. Fluctuations drive the state, not only its mean. A stock price follows a geometric Brownian motion, a particle diffuses in a fluid, molecular noise shakes gene expression, and turbulence stirs a temperature field. ProductionLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which changes the value of a fixed number of states, it replaces symbols by strings, so the word grows. A structure develops by repeated rewriting. Lindenmayer systems model the branching of plants, rewriting rules build fractal curves, and grammars generate the structure of sentences. RateLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which gives the next value in discrete time, it gives a derivative in continuous time. A state flows, and add a NoiseLaw for a random part. Infected people recover at a rate, a balance grows by interest, a reactant is consumed by mass action, and a pendulum accelerates under gravity. RuleLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which gives the next value as an expression the compiler lowers, it runs arbitrary Python on each agent. Behaviour needs branches, memory, or search that an expression cannot hold. Sheep and wolves move and eat on a grid, traders follow strategies in a market, and households decide where to live in a model of segregation. SampleLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which sets the next value by a rule, it proposes values and accepts or rejects them. The states follow a Boltzmann distribution of an energy. Spins of a magnet in the Ising model, cells in the cellular Potts model, and residents in a model of segregation are sampled this way. SubstitutionLaw Unlike ProductionLaw, which rewrites symbols of a word, it rewrites tiles of the plane. A tiling grows by inflation and subdivision. It appears in mathematics and materials science. The Penrose tiling grows by substitution, and quasicrystals have the order of such tilings. TransferLaw Unlike RateLaw, which changes one state, it pairs a loss with a gain, so the amount is conserved. A quantity moves between holders and its flow is worth recording. People move from susceptible to infected, money moves between accounts, water flows between reservoirs, and stock moves along a supply chain. TransitionLaw Unlike UpdateLaw, which computes the next value, it draws it from a distribution over values. A state moves at random among a few values. Weather moves between dry and wet days, a text model draws the next word, a gene sequence moves between coding and non-coding regions, and a credit rating moves between grades. UpdateLaw Unlike RateLaw, which gives a derivative in continuous time, it gives the next value in discrete time. The model steps, such as a map, a generation, or a round. The logistic map follows a population from year to year, a cellular automaton steps its cells, and an account compounds interest monthly.

    • constraints: Sage relations, ==, <=, or >=, linear in the variables.

docs.title: LocalRuleLaw
docs.text:
A law that sets the next value of cells from their ordered neighbourhoods.

  • Law kind: update
  • Randomness: deterministic
  • Times: continuous, discrete
  • Solvers: CoSimulationSolver, GradientDescentSolver, IterationSolver, LatticeSolver, MesaSolver, RewritingSolver
  • Backends: any
  • Arguments:
    • targets: The symbol of a lattice state, or a tuple of them that the rule updates together.
    • over: The neighbourhood whose values the rule reads: a lattice neighbourhood of offsets, an adjacency on a network, a memory of group elements on a group space, or a memory translated by the group element that the first read state holds at every site, StateTranslationNeighborhood.
    • rule: A function, a TableSpec, a TotalisticSpec rule, an OuterTotalisticSpec rule, a LinearRuleSpec, or an object whose get_table() returns a TableSpec, such as a rule code.
    • reads: The lattice states whose neighbourhoods a function rule reads, or None for the targets.
    • schedule: 'synchronous' to update every site from the previous configuration, 'random-sequential' to update the sites one at a time in a random order, 'random-site' to update as many randomly chosen sites, 'checkerboard' to update the two sublattices of a square lattice in turn, or 'colored' to update the classes of a proper coloring of the neighbour graph in turn.
    • stochastic: Whether a function rule receives the uniform random array random.
    • label: The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.
  • Errors:
    • ValidationError: The schedule or the rule spec is invalid, or a run lacks the space or a read state.
  • Catalog systems: contact_process, diffusion_limited_aggregation, discrete_master_equation, earthquakes, fixed_energy_sandpile, forest_fire, hexagonal_forest_fire, landau_relaxation, manna_sandpile, q2r, and more in the catalog

  • Backends: any
  • Arguments:
    • target: The symbol of a scalar state, the column of symbols of a vector state, or a TopologyRequestSpec, whose value is the probability that the request fires.
    • value: A symbolic expression, a Call, or a callable f(t, values) that gives the next value.
    • label: The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.
    • increment: Whether the value is the state plus a change that adds to the changes of the other update laws of the state.
    • source: The value the law moves the state from, keeping every other value, or None.
    • order: A symbolic expression of the states, parameters, and draws of a member, whose values order the members that update one after the other, or None for members that update at once.
    • phase: The name of the phase of the step the law runs in, or None for the default phase.

docs.title: A compatible law
docs.text:
A JumpInteraction adds one unit to a queue at random times, at a rate of 2 per time unit. It returns a jump law, which GillespieSolver supports.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import JumpInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import GillespieSolver
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

queue = DeclaredElement('queue', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(0.0, StateSpec())})
arrive = JumpInteraction('arrive', target='queue', changes={'x': 1}, rate=lambda s: 2.0)
sorted(arrive.get_tags().laws)
system = CompositeSystem(elements=[queue], interactions=[arrive])
trajectory = simulate(system, until=5, solver=GillespieSolver(), random_state=0)
trajectory.get_values('queue.x')[-1]

['jump']
11.0

The law kind is jump, and with the seed 0 the queue holds 11 after five time units, near the mean of 10.

docs.title: An incompatible law
docs.text:
EulerSolver integrates rates and does not draw jumps, so simulate raises a TagError that names the law kind.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import JumpInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import EulerSolver
from skcomplex.core.errors import TagError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

queue = DeclaredElement('queue', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(0.0, StateSpec())})
arrive = JumpInteraction('arrive', target='queue', changes={'x': 1}, rate=lambda s: 2.0)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[queue], interactions=[arrive]), until=5, solver=EulerSolver())
except TagError as error:
    message = str(error)
message
assert 'laws jump' in message

The solver EulerSolver does not support the laws jump of the system. Pass a solver that supports them, or none for the default.

The message says that EulerSolver does not support the law kind jump, and asks for a solver that supports it or for none, which lets the tags choose the default.

docs.title: Solvers
docs.text:
A solver steps a system through time, or solves a static system at once. get_supported_tags() of a solver class returns the times, spaces, and law kinds it supports. simulate compares them with the tags of the system before it compiles the system, and raises a TagError when the solver lacks one. Leave the solver out and the tags choose the default solver. The table lists the supported tags of every solver, grouped by the mathematical form it solves.

docs.title: A compatible solver
docs.text:
A rate with a noise term returns a rate and a noise law, which together form a stochastic differential equation. EulerMaruyamaSolver supports both.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import EulerMaruyamaSolver
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

tank = DeclaredElement('tank', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(10.0, StateSpec())})
decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='tank', state='x', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.x, noise=0.1)
system = CompositeSystem(elements=[tank], interactions=[decay])
sorted(system.get_tags().laws), sorted(EulerMaruyamaSolver.get_supported_tags().laws)
trajectory = simulate(system, until=1, solver=EulerMaruyamaSolver(), random_state=0)
round(trajectory.get_values('tank.x')[-1], 2)

(['noise', 'rate'], ['equation', 'jump', 'noise', 'rate', 'update'])
6.15

The system has the law kinds noise and rate, and the solver supports equation, jump, noise, rate, and update. With the seed 0 the tank holds 6.15 after one time unit, near the 6.07 of the decay without noise.

docs.title: Spaces, neighbourhoods, and times
docs.text:
A space places the members of a group, such as the sites of a lattice or the nodes of a network, and its tag names the kind of structure. A neighbourhood says which members a law reads around one member. A time says how the system advances: in continuous time, in discrete steps, or not at all. A solver runs a system only when it supports the tags of its space and its time. The table lists the tags that each class declares.

Class Kind Tags AdjacencyNeighborhood neighbourhood none BallNeighborhood neighbourhood none BaseNeighborhood neighbourhood none BaseSpace space from a subclass BaseTime time from a subclass CayleySpace space lattice CellComplexSpace space cell complex CofaceNeighborhood neighbourhood none ContinuousSpace space continuous ContinuousTime time continuous DelaunayNeighborhood neighbourhood none DiscreteTime time discrete LatticeNeighborhood neighbourhood none LatticeSpace space lattice MemoryNeighborhood neighbourhood none MeshSpace space continuous NearestNeighborhood neighbourhood none NetworkSpace space hypergraph, network PhaseSpace space phase space RadiusNeighborhood neighbourhood none SimplexSpace space phase space StateTranslationNeighborhood neighbourhood none StaticTime time static

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Class What it adds Choose it when Uses AdjacencyNeighborhood Unlike BallNeighborhood, which reads offsets on a lattice, it reads the edges of a graph, so each node may have a different number of neighbours. Members sit on the nodes of a network. A person catches a disease from their contacts, a voter copies the opinion of a friend, and a bus of a power grid exchanges power with the buses it is wired to. BallNeighborhood Unlike LatticeNeighborhood, which takes its offsets one by one, it builds them from a radius and a metric. A law reads the usual neighbours on a grid. A sandpile topples grains to its four neighbours, a cell of the Game of Life counts its eight neighbours, and a voter model copies a random neighbour on a grid. BaseNeighborhood Unlike BaseSpace, which places members, it selects some of them around one member. A new rule for choosing neighbours is needed, and choose an existing neighbourhood, such as BallNeighborhood, otherwise. It appears in every field through its subclasses, such as the eight cells around a site of a lattice, the contacts of a person in a network, and the birds within sight of a bird in a flock. BaseSpace Unlike BaseElement, it holds no states, only the structure that members sit on. Members live on a new kind of structure, and choose LatticeSpace, NetworkSpace, or ContinuousSpace otherwise. It appears in every field through its subclasses, such as a grid of cells in an ecosystem, a contact network in an epidemic, and a box of particles in a gas. BaseTime Unlike BaseSpace, which says where members are, it says how the states advance. A system advances in a new way, and choose ContinuousTime, DiscreteTime, or StaticTime otherwise. It appears in every field through its subclasses, such as the flow of an epidemic in continuous time, the generations of a population in discrete time, and the static balance of an economy. CayleySpace Unlike LatticeSpace, which is the Cayley graph of the integers Z^d, it takes any finitely generated group, such as a free group whose graph is a tree. Cells live on the elements of a group. It appears in mathematics and computer science, in cellular automata on groups and in symbolic dynamics, as in the book of Ceccherini-Silberstein and Coornaert. CellComplexSpace Unlike NetworkSpace, which knows nodes and edges, it also knows faces and the orientation of each cell, so states on links can have a circulation. A state lives on links or faces, as in discrete exterior calculus. Lattice gauge theories hold angles on the links of a lattice, discrete exterior calculus models flows on meshes, and the Hodge decomposition splits the flows of a network into gradient and cyclic parts. CofaceNeighborhood Unlike AdjacencyNeighborhood, which reads nodes of the same kind, it reads cells of the next degree. A state on links depends on the faces around each link. It appears in physics and numerical analysis. Lattice gauge theories sum the plaquettes around each link, and discrete exterior calculus reads the faces around each edge of a mesh. ContinuousSpace Unlike LatticeSpace, whose sites are fixed, it lets members move to any real position. Members move freely, such as particles or animals. Atoms move in a box of a gas, birds fly in a flock, pedestrians walk through a station, and households live in the districts of a map. ContinuousTime Unlike DiscreteTime, which steps, it lets states change at every instant. The model is a differential equation or a stochastic process in continuous time. An epidemic flows by the SIR equations, a chemical reactor by its rate equations, a pendulum by Newton's law, and a stock price by a stochastic differential equation. DelaunayNeighborhood Unlike RadiusNeighborhood, which takes every member within a distance, it takes the members that touch, whatever the distance. Members interact with those beside them, with no gap between. Cells in a tissue push on the cells that touch them, bubbles share walls in a foam, and animals defend territories against their neighbours. DiscreteTime Unlike ContinuousTime, which flows, it advances by whole steps. The model is a map, a cellular automaton, or an agent-based model. A population grows by generations, a cellular automaton steps its cells, agents trade in rounds, and an account compounds interest monthly. LatticeNeighborhood Unlike BallNeighborhood, which builds its offsets from a radius, it takes any list of offsets. A neighbourhood has an irregular shape, or an order of its own, such as a cell and its two neighbours from left to right. It appears in elementary cellular automata, which read a cell and its two neighbours, and in rules that read cells in one direction only, such as the upwind cells of a model of advection. LatticeSpace Unlike NetworkSpace, whose links are arbitrary, it has regular neighbours, a shape, and a boundary. Members sit on a grid of cells, or a field discretizes a partial differential equation. Spins of a magnet sit on a square lattice, trees of a forest fire on a grid, and the cells of a reaction diffusion model on a mesh of points. MemoryNeighborhood Unlike LatticeNeighborhood, whose offsets are integer vectors, it takes words of a group. Cells live on a CayleySpace. It appears in mathematics and computer science, in cellular automata on free groups and on groups of automata. MeshSpace Unlike LatticeSpace, which is a regular grid, it fits domains of any shape. A partial differential equation on an irregular domain is solved by finite elements. Heat flows through a machine part, groundwater seeps through an aquifer, and a membrane deforms under a load. NearestNeighborhood Unlike RadiusNeighborhood, which takes every member within a distance, it takes a fixed number of members, whatever their distance. Each member attends to a fixed number of others. Starlings in a flock follow their seven nearest neighbours, fish school by their closest neighbours, and robots of a swarm align with the nearest robots. NetworkSpace Unlike LatticeSpace, whose neighbours are regular, it takes any pattern of links. The members are joined by contacts, roads, wires, or trades. A disease spreads on a contact network, generators synchronize on a power grid, banks lend to each other on an interbank network, and neurons fire along their synapses. PhaseSpace Unlike LatticeSpace, whose sites are positions alone, it adds axes of a trait, so a density can vary over position and trait together. A kinetic equation follows a distribution over position and a trait. Kinetic theory follows gas molecules over position and velocity, bacteria are counted over position and swimming direction, and cell populations over position and age. RadiusNeighborhood Unlike NearestNeighborhood, which takes a fixed number of members, it takes every member within a distance, so the number of neighbours varies. Members sense others up to a range, optionally within a field of view. Birds align with flockmates within sight in the Vicsek model, atoms interact within a cutoff, and pedestrians react to people ahead of them. SimplexSpace Unlike PhaseSpace, whose class axes are independent, it constrains the frequencies to a simplex. A density lives over the shares of several types. Populations evolve over the shares of strategies in evolutionary game theory, genotypes over allele frequencies in population genetics, and voters over the shares of parties. StateTranslationNeighborhood Unlike MemoryNeighborhood, whose memory set is fixed, it shifts the memory set by the value of the cell. Studying maps on groups that are not cellular automata. It appears in mathematics, in symbolic dynamics on groups, as the example of Ceccherini-Silberstein and Coornaert shows. StaticTime Unlike ContinuousTime and DiscreteTime, it has no dynamics. The answer is a balance or an optimum, not a path. Flux balance analysis finds the steady fluxes of a metabolic network, an economy finds the least cost dispatch of power plants, and a circuit finds its operating point.

docs.title: The tags of a space and a time
docs.text:
get_tags of a space returns its space tag, and that of a time returns its time tag. A solver compares them with the tags it supports before a run.

from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import ContinuousTime, LatticeSpace

grid = LatticeSpace((4, 4))
sorted(grid.get_tags().space), sorted(ContinuousTime().get_tags().time)

(['lattice'], ['continuous'])

A lattice of 4 by 4 sites has the space tag lattice, and ContinuousTime has the time tag continuous.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
A system is a part that holds elements, interactions, nested systems, a space, and a time. BaseSystem is the base of every system. A subclass takes the parameters of its model in __init__, builds its parts from them in _build_system, and derives its capability tags from its parts, which get_tags() returns. CompositeSystem takes its parts as data, so it needs no subclass. A general system that several fields share, such as ReactionNetworkSystem of skcomplex.systems.general.reactions, is a recipe built from core parts. The ready-made systems of skcomplex.systems subclass these, one class per model. The catalog lists them by field and by topic, with their import paths, model parameters, and capability tags, and all_systems of skcomplex.systems finds them by field, topic, or tag. The table lists the system classes of the core.

System Import Description CompositeSystem from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem A system that composes elements, interactions, and nested systems as data.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Class What it adds Choose it when Uses BaseSystem Unlike CompositeSystem, which takes its parts as data, it writes them in terms of named model parameters. A model has parameters that users set, sweep, or calibrate, as every system of the catalog does. The SIR model of an epidemic, the Lotka-Volterra model of predators and prey, the Ising model of a magnet, and the Kuramoto model of oscillators are system classes. CompositeSystem Unlike BaseSystem, which builds its parts from model parameters, it takes the parts themselves. Composing a model from parts once, or when nesting systems inside a larger one. A predator and its prey on a lattice, a savings account with interest and withdrawals, a circuit of resistors and capacitors, and an economy of nested regions are composite systems.

docs.title: A compatible system
docs.text:
A composite of random arrivals has jump laws, which GillespieSolver draws one event at a time.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import JumpInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import GillespieSolver
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

queue = DeclaredElement('queue', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(0.0, StateSpec())})
arrive = JumpInteraction('arrive', target='queue', changes={'x': 1}, rate=lambda s: 2.0)
system = CompositeSystem(elements=[queue], interactions=[arrive])
sorted(system.get_tags().laws), system.get_tags().randomness
trajectory = simulate(system, until=5, solver=GillespieSolver(), random_state=0)
trajectory.get_values('queue.x')[-1]

(['jump'], 'stochastic')
11.0

The system has the law kind jump and the randomness stochastic, and with the seed 0 the queue holds 11 after five time units.

docs.title: An incompatible system
docs.text:
A composite of a decay has rate equations, which GillespieSolver does not draw, so simulate raises a TagError that names the law kind.

from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement
from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
from skcomplex.core.engine.solvers import GillespieSolver
from skcomplex.core.errors import TagError
from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec

tank = DeclaredElement('tank', variables={'x': DeclaredVariableSpec(10.0, StateSpec())})
decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='tank', state='x', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.x)
try:
    simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[tank], interactions=[decay]), until=5, solver=GillespieSolver())
except TagError as error:
    message = str(error)
message
assert 'laws rate' in message

The solver GillespieSolver does not support the laws rate of the system. Pass a solver that supports them, or none for the default.

The message says that GillespieSolver does not support the law kind rate. Leave the solver out and the tags choose one that integrates rates.

docs.title: Find ready-made systems by tag
docs.text:
all_systems takes the values of capability tags, so it finds the ready-made systems that a solver or an analysis accepts.

from skcomplex.systems import all_systems

stochastic = all_systems(field='biology/epidemiology', tags={'randomness': 'stochastic'})
[name for name, _ in stochastic][:3]

['ActivityDrivenEpidemicsSystem', 'AdaptiveSISSystem', 'AgentBasedSIRSystem']

The list holds the first three stochastic systems of epidemiology, in alphabetical order.

• Agent-based Lotka-Volterra: Prey and predators that walk on a grid, whose numbers cycle.
  • COMETS: dynamic flux balance on a lattice with diffusion: An expanding colony of the E. coli core system on a lattice.
  • Carrying capacity of a meadow: Cows that graze a meadow for a summer of 25 weeks.
  • Competition: Two species that compete for the same resources.
  • Consumer-resource models of substitutable and essential resources: Consumer species that compete only through the resources they take up.
  • Droop cell-quota growth: The Droop system of a phytoplankton that grows on its stored nutrient.
  • Dynamic multi-species metabolic system: Two E. coli core strains that differ in maximal glucose uptake on one medium.
  • Exponential growth: A population that grows or declines at a constant per-capita rate.
  • Fibonacci rabbits: Fibonacci's rabbits, N_{t+1} = N_t + N_{t-1}.
  • Fisher-KPP: The Fisher-KPP equation, whose step invades the empty line as a front.
  • Food webs: A food web of logistic basal species and Lotka-Volterra consumers.
  • Generalized Lotka-Volterra microbial community: The generalized Lotka-Volterra system of a microbial community.
  • Generalized stochastic predator-prey: Prey and predators born and killed one at a time.
  • Hutchinson: Hutchinson's delayed logistic equation.
  • Intrinsic-instability populations: Jensen's coupled populations, whose steady state becomes unstable.
  • Joint, community, and SteadyCom flux balance: Two members of the E. coli core system that share a medium.
  • Logistic growth: A population that grows logistically towards its carrying capacity.
  • Logistic growth with a varying capacity: Logistic growth under a seasonal carrying capacity.
  • Lotka-Volterra: Prey and predators whose populations oscillate through predation.
  • Lotka-Volterra with harvesting: Lotka-Volterra predation where both species are harvested.
  • Mangrove succession: The regrowth of a mangrove forest of the Sundarbans after a clear cut.
  • Mutualism: Two species that grow logistically and feed each other.
  • Neutral Moran system with speciation: A neutral community of constant size with speciation and drift.
  • Neutral birth-death with hopping between boxes: Organisms that divide, die, and hop between patches on a periodic lattice.
  • Neutral macroecology: Many species under neutral birth, death, and immigration.
  • Nicholson-Bailey: Hosts and parasitoids in discrete generations.
  • Penaeid shrimp growth: The growth of one penaeid shrimp from the juvenile stage.
  • Random Lotka-Volterra with higher-order interactions: A random Lotka-Volterra community with third-order interactions.
  • Ricker map of overcompensating generations: Ricker's map of a population in discrete generations, n' = r n exp(-n).
  • Rosenzweig-MacArthur and rate tipping: Fast prey and slow predators whose carrying capacity shrinks at a rate.
  • Sequentially linear ecosystem: An ecosystem with linear dynamics between extinctions that rewrite its network.
  • Size-structured forest with shading and seed dispersal: The McKendrick-von Foerster density of trees over position and height.
  • Stigmergic predator-prey automaton: Plants, prey, and predators on a grid.
  • Wolf and sheep: The wolf and sheep predation system with one grass patch per cell.

docs.title: Class
docs.text:
The source of the class shows how it builds its parts from its model parameters.

class ActiveWalkersSystem(BaseSystem):
    """Active walkers who wear a system of trails into a green.

    They walk between the corners of the green.

    Walkers prefer existing trails to the direct way, and trails fade unless they are used, so a few shared trails
    emerge that bundle the ways between the corners, a compromise between short and comfortable routes. The system has
    the walkers `people/walkers`, the ground structure `land/ground.G`, and the trail potential `land/ground.V`.

    Args:
        size:
            The number of rows and columns of the green.

        n_walkers:
            The number of walkers.

        attraction:
            How strongly trails draw the walkers.

        T:
            The durability of trails.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the starting corners and goals.

        label:
            The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.collective_behaviour import ActiveWalkersSystem
        >>> [child.label for child in ActiveWalkersSystem().prepare().system_.systems]
        ['people', 'land']
    """

    field = 'biology/collective_behaviour'
    topics = ('agents', 'field', 'trail formation', 'co-simulation')
    references = ('Helbing, Keltsch, and Molnár 1997', 'arXiv:cond-mat/0012229')
    until = 300
    dt = 1

    def __init__(
        self,
        size: int = 30,
        *,
        n_walkers: int = 20,
        attraction: float = 1.0,
        T: float = 200.0,
        random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
        label: str = 'system',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.size = size
        self.n_walkers = n_walkers
        self.attraction = attraction
        self.T = T
        self.random_state = random_state

    @staticmethod
    def _get_corners(width: int, height: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        """Return the four corner cells of a grid, the entry points of the walkers."""
        return [(0, 0), (width - 1, 0), (0, height - 1), (width - 1, height - 1)]

    @staticmethod
    def _get_durability(namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the durability `T` of trails.

        It is the time over which the structure fades to bare ground.
        """
        durability: Expression = namespace.target.T
        return durability

    @staticmethod
    def _get_diffusion(namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the diffusion coefficient `D` of the trail potential."""
        coefficient: Expression = namespace.target.D
        return coefficient

    @staticmethod
    def _get_structure(namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the ground structure `G`, the goal of the trail potential."""
        structure: Expression = namespace.target.G
        return structure

    @staticmethod
    def _get_relaxation(namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the relaxation time `tau` of the trail potential."""
        time: Expression = namespace.target.tau
        return time

    def _get_goal(self, walker: AgentViewProtocol | None, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return a random entry point other than the cell of a walker as its goal."""
        if not isinstance(walker, WalkerView):
            return {}
        here = cast('tuple[int, int]', walker.location)
        goals = [corner for corner in self._get_corners(round(walker.width), round(walker.height)) if corner != here]
        goal_x, goal_y = goals[int(system.rng.integers(len(goals)))]
        return {'goal_x': float(goal_x), 'goal_y': float(goal_y)}

    @staticmethod
    def _has_arrived(walker: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> bool:
        """Return whether a walker stands at its goal."""
        del system
        return isinstance(walker, WalkerView) and walker.location == (round(walker.goal_x), round(walker.goal_y))

    def _waits(self, walker: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> bool:
        """Return whether a walker arrived at its goal in the previous step.

        Such a walker leaves the green now.
        """
        return self._has_arrived(walker, system) and isinstance(walker, WalkerView) and bool(walker.arrived)

    def _walks(self, walker: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> bool:
        """Return whether a walker is away from its goal.

        Such a walker steps.
        """
        return not self._has_arrived(walker, system)

    def _get_arrived(self, walker: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> float:
        """Return whether a walker stands at its goal at the end of its activation."""
        return float(self._has_arrived(walker, system))

    @staticmethod
    def _get_step(walker: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> object:
        """Return a neighbouring cell drawn with a weight growing with its alignment.

        The alignment is that of the step with the heading.

        The heading is the unit vector toward the goal plus `attraction` times the gradient of the trail potential, and
        the weight of a step is `exp(directedness * cos angle)`, where the angle is between the step and the heading.
        """
        if not isinstance(walker, WalkerView):
            return None
        x, y = cast('tuple[int, int]', walker.location)
        cells = cast('list[tuple[int, int]]', list(walker.get_neighbor_cells()))
        goal = np.array([walker.goal_x - x, walker.goal_y - y])
        steps = np.array([(cell[0] - x, cell[1] - y) for cell in cells], dtype=float)
        lengths = np.hypot(steps[:, 0], steps[:, 1])
        rises = np.array([system.get_field(TRAIL, cell) for cell in cells]) - system.get_field(TRAIL, (x, y))
        slope = 2 * (steps / lengths[:, None] ** 2).T @ rises / len(cells)
        heading = goal / max(float(np.hypot(*goal)), 1e-12) + walker.attraction * slope
        alignment = steps @ heading / (lengths * max(float(np.hypot(*heading)), 1e-12))
        weights = np.exp(walker.directedness * (alignment - alignment.max()))
        return cells[int(system.rng.choice(len(cells), p=weights / weights.sum()))]

    @staticmethod
    def _has_stepped(walker: AgentViewProtocol, cell: object, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> bool:
        """Return whether a walker stepped in its activation.

        It steps since it had not arrived at its goal before.
        """
        del cell, system
        return isinstance(walker, WalkerView) and not walker.arrived

    @staticmethod
    def _get_footprint(walker: AgentViewProtocol, cell: object, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> float:
        """Return the footprint a walker leaves on the ground of its cell.

        The footprint is `intensity (1 - G / G_max)`.
        """
        if not isinstance(walker, WalkerView):
            return 0.0
        return walker.intensity * (1 - system.get_field('target.G', cell) / walker.G_max)

    def _build_system(self) -> CompositeSystem:
        """Return the parts of the system."""
        rng = np.random.default_rng(self.random_state)
        corners = self._get_corners(self.size, self.size)
        starts = rng.integers(len(corners), size=self.n_walkers)
        goals = [corners[(start + 1 + int(rng.integers(len(corners) - 1))) % len(corners)] for start in starts]
        walkers = GroupElement(
            'walkers',
            element=WalkerElement,
            size=self.n_walkers,
            values={
                'goal_x': np.array([float(goal[0]) for goal in goals]),
                'goal_y': np.array([float(goal[1]) for goal in goals]),
                'attraction': self.attraction,
                'width': float(self.size),
                'height': float(self.size),
            },
            location=[corners[start] for start in starts],
        )
        ground = FieldElement(
            'ground',
            element=GroundElement,
            space=LatticeSpace((self.size, self.size), boundary='reflecting'),
            values={'T': self.T},
        )
        return CompositeSystem(
            self.label,
            systems=[
                CompositeSystem(
                    'people',
                    elements=[walkers],
                    space=LatticeSpace((self.size, self.size), boundary='fixed'),
                ),
                CompositeSystem(
                    'land',
                    elements=[ground],
                    interactions=[
                        RateInteraction(
                            'fading',
                            target='ground',
                            state='G',
                            rate=lambda s: -s.target.G / self._get_durability(s),
                        ),
                        RateInteraction(
                            'spreading',
                            target='ground',
                            state='V',
                            rate=lambda s: self._get_diffusion(s) * laplacian(s.target.V),
                        ),
                        RateInteraction(
                            'smoothing',
                            target='ground',
                            state='V',
                            rate=lambda s: (self._get_structure(s) - s.target.V) / self._get_relaxation(s),
                        ),
                    ],
                ),
            ],
            interactions=[
                MovementInteraction(
                    'walk',
                    target='people/walkers',
                    step=self._get_step,
                    condition=self._walks,
                    schedule='member',
                ),
                TransferInteraction(
                    'footprints',
                    source='people/walkers',
                    target='land/ground',
                    state=Source(),
                    into='G',
                    amount=self._get_footprint,
                    pairing='site',
                    guard=self._has_stepped,
                    form='agent',
                    schedule='member',
                ),
                BirthDeathInteraction(
                    'renewal',
                    target='people/walkers',
                    death=self._waits,
                    renew=True,
                    values=self._get_goal,
                    schedule='member',
                ),
                MapInteraction(
                    'arrival',
                    target='people/walkers',
                    state='arrived',
                    function=self._get_arrived,
                    form='agent',
                    schedule='member',
                ),
            ],
        )

docs.text:
The system uses these element and interaction classes, each with its nearest class of the core.

Elements:

  • WalkerElement, from Element
  • GroundElement, from Element

Interactions:

  • MovementInteraction, from Interaction, through the shared recipe MovementInteraction
  • TransferInteraction
  • BirthDeathInteraction, from Interaction, through the shared recipe BirthDeathInteraction
  • MapInteraction
  • RateInteraction
class MovementInteraction(Interaction):
    """An interaction that moves the agents of a group by steps at every discrete step.

    The `step` says where an agent goes:

    - `'neighbor'`: a random cell or node next to its own, on a lattice or a network.
    - `'gaussian'`: its position plus a normal vector of deviation `scale`, in a continuous space.
    - `'levy'`: a random direction and a Pareto length of least value `scale` and tail `exponent`, in a continuous
      space.
    - `'best'`: the next cell with the highest `score(agent, cell, system)`, or with a `vision` the best cell along each
      direction up to that many cells, with ties broken by `ties`.
    - A function `step(agent, system)` that returns the destination, or `None` to stay.

    An agent for which `condition` holds attempts one step, or a Poisson number of mean `rate`, takes it with the
    probability `probability`, and then with the probability `accept(agent, destination, system)`. An exclusive movement
    never enters a cell held by another agent of the group. The agents move one after another by `schedule`, and every
    step charges its `cost`.

    Unlike `TopologyInteraction`, which changes the space, it changes where agents stand in it. Choose it when agents
    walk, forage, or relocate.

    It appears in many fields. Sheep wander a pasture, foragers follow Lévy flights, ants climb a pheromone gradient,
    and residents move house in the segregation model of Schelling.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group whose agents move.

        step:
            The kind of step, `'neighbor'`, `'gaussian'`, `'levy'`, or `'best'`, or a function of the agent and the
            system view that returns the destination.

        probability:
            The probability that an agent takes an attempted step.

        rate:
            The mean number of attempted steps of an agent in one unit of time, or `None` for one attempt every step.

        condition:
            A function of the agent and the system view that returns whether the agent moves, or `None` for every agent.

        accept:
            A function of the agent, its destination, and the system view that returns the probability of taking the
            step, or `None` to take every step.

        exclusive:
            Whether an agent moves only to cells or nodes no other agent of the group holds.

        score:
            The function of the agent, a neighbouring cell, and the system view that the step `'best'` maximizes.

        scale:
            The standard deviation of every component of a Gaussian step, or the least length of a Lévy step.

        exponent:
            The tail exponent of the length of a Lévy step.

        cost:
            A `TransferInteraction` that the agent pays to itself or to the environment for every step taken, a function
            of the agent and the system view run for every step taken, or `None`.

        vision:
            The number of cells the step `'best'` looks along every direction of a lattice, a number or a function of
            the agent and the system view, or `None` for the cells next to the agent.

        schedule:
            The order of the agents, `'sequential'`, `'random-sequential'`, or `'member'`.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the movement runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        ties:
            The cell the step `'best'` takes among cells of equal highest score, `'random'`, `'first'`, or `'nearest'`,
            or `None` for `'random'` without a vision and `'nearest'` with one.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The step, the schedule, or the ties are unknown, the rate is not positive, a function is not callable, or
            the step `'best'` has no score, raised by `prepare`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.systems.general.agents import MovementInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> walkers = GroupElement('walkers', element=Element, size=2, location=[(2, 2), (2, 2)])
        >>> walk = MovementInteraction('walk', target='walkers', step='neighbor')
        >>> space = LatticeSpace((5, 5), metric='manhattan')
        >>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[walkers], interactions=[walk], space=space)
        >>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1, random_state=0)
        >>> [bool(abs(cell - 2).sum() == 1) for cell in trajectory.get_agents('walkers', 1).locations]
        [True, True]
    """

    law_classes: ClassVar[tuple[type[BaseLaw], ...]] = (RuleLaw,)

    def _get_draws(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the movement draws.

        It draws by its order, a random step, a probability or rate, or random ties.
        """
        ties = self.ties or ('random' if self.vision is None else 'nearest')
        drawn = self.step in ('neighbor', 'gaussian', 'levy') or (self.step == 'best' and ties == 'random')
        return (
            super()._get_draws() or drawn or self.probability != 1 or self.rate is not None or self.accept is not None
        )

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ElementKind.GROUP, ElementKind.VARIABLE_GROUP))],
        step: Step = 'neighbor',
        probability: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed(0, 1))] = 1.0,
        rate: float | None = None,
        condition: Callable[[AgentViewProtocol, SystemViewProtocol], bool] | None = None,
        accept: Callable[[AgentViewProtocol, object, SystemViewProtocol], float] | None = None,
        exclusive: bool = False,
        score: Callable[[AgentViewProtocol, object, SystemViewProtocol], float] | None = None,
        scale: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        exponent: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.5,
        cost: Cost | None = None,
        vision: Vision | None = None,
        schedule: str = 'random-sequential',
        phase: str | None = None,
        ties: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.step = step
        self.probability = probability
        self.rate = rate
        self.condition = condition
        self.accept = accept
        self.exclusive = exclusive
        self.score = score
        self.scale = scale
        self.exponent = exponent
        self.cost = cost
        self.vision = vision
        self.schedule = schedule
        self.phase = phase
        self.ties = ties

    def _check_functions(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a condition, acceptance, score, or cost that is not callable."""
        for name in ('condition', 'accept', 'score'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function, or None.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if isinstance(self.cost, TransferInteraction):
            self.cost.prepare()
        elif self.cost is not None and not callable(self.cost):
            error_msg = f'The cost of {self.label!r} is {self.cost!r}. Give a TransferInteraction, a function, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check_space(self, space: BaseSpace | None) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a step to a neighbouring cell or node in a continuous space."""
        if isinstance(self.step, str) and self.step in GRID_STEPS:
            self._check_grid('step', self.step, space, "step='gaussian' or step='levy', or a step function")

    def _prepare(self, context: BaseSpace | None = None) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown step, a rate not positive, or a bad function.

        Args:
            context:
                The space the interaction inherits from its system.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The step, the schedule, or the ties are unknown, the rate is not positive, a function is not callable,
                or the step `'best'` has no score.
        """
        super()._prepare(context)
        self._check_variant('step', self.step, STEPS, functions=True)
        if self.rate is not None and (isinstance(self.rate, bool) or not self.rate > 0):
            error_msg = f'The rate of {self.label!r} is {self.rate!r}. Give a positive number, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.schedule not in SCHEDULES:
            error_msg = f'Unknown schedule {self.schedule!r} of {self.label!r}. Use one of {", ".join(SCHEDULES)}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.ties is not None:
            self._check_variant('ties', self.ties, TIES)
        if self.vision is not None and not callable(self.vision) and not isinstance(self.vision, int | float):
            error_msg = f'The vision of {self.label!r} is {self.vision!r}. Give a number, a function, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.step == 'best' and self.score is None:
            error_msg = f'The step `best` of {self.label!r} maximizes a score. Pass `score(agent, cell, system)`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        self._check_functions()

    def _count_attempts(self, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> int:
        """Return the number of steps an agent attempts in one step of time."""
        return 1 if self.rate is None else int(system.rng.poisson(self.rate))

    def _get_cells(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, occupied: set[object]) -> list[object]:
        """Return the cells or nodes around an agent that it may move to."""
        cells = agent.get_neighbor_cells()
        if not self.exclusive:
            return cells
        return [cell for cell in cells if cell not in occupied]

    def _get_best(
        self,
        agent: AgentViewProtocol,
        cells: list[object],
        system: SystemViewProtocol,
        distances: list[int] | None = None,
    ) -> object:
        """Return the cell of the highest score, chosen among ties by the tie rule."""
        if self.score is None or not cells:
            return None
        scores = [self.score(agent, cell, system) for cell in cells]
        ties = self.ties or ('random' if distances is None else 'nearest')
        if ties != 'nearest':
            return cells[self._pick_best(scores, ties, system)]
        values = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
        best = np.flatnonzero(values == values.max())
        near = np.asarray([1 if distances is None else distances[int(index)] for index in best])
        return cells[int(best[near == near.min()][0])]

    @staticmethod
    def _shift(here: tuple[int, ...], cell: tuple[int, ...], system: SystemViewProtocol) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Return the unit step from a cell to a neighbouring cell.

        The step goes across the wrapped edge of a torus.
        """
        shift = [b - a for a, b in zip(here, cell, strict=True)]
        if system.torus:
            sizes = [int(item) for item in system.dimensions or ()]
            shift = [d - round(d / n) * n for d, n in zip(shift, sizes, strict=True)]
        return tuple(shift)

    def _get_sight(
        self,
        agent: AgentViewProtocol,
        occupied: set[object],
        system: SystemViewProtocol,
    ) -> tuple[list[object], list[int]]:
        """Return the cells in sight of an agent along every direction of a lattice.

        Its own cell comes first, with the distances.
        """
        vision = self.vision(agent, system) if callable(self.vision) else self.vision
        reach = int(vision or 0)
        here = tuple(int(item) for item in np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(agent.location_key)))
        sizes = [int(item) for item in system.dimensions or ()]
        cells: list[object] = [agent.location_key]
        distances = [0]
        shifts = [
            self._shift(here, tuple(int(item) for item in np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(neighbor))), system)
            for neighbor in agent.get_neighbor_cells()
        ]
        for shift in sorted(shifts, key=lambda step: tuple((item == 0, -item) for item in step)):
            for distance in range(1, reach + 1):
                point = [a + distance * d for a, d in zip(here, shift, strict=True)]
                if system.torus:
                    point = [item % size for item, size in zip(point, sizes, strict=True)]
                elif any(not 0 <= item < size for item, size in zip(point, sizes, strict=True)):
                    break
                cell = tuple(point)
                if not self.exclusive or cell not in occupied:
                    cells.append(cell)
                    distances.append(distance)
        return cells, distances

    def _get_destination(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol, occupied: set[object]) -> object:
        """Return the location a step of an agent leads to, or `None` to stay."""
        rng = system.rng
        if callable(self.step):
            return self.step(agent, system)
        if self.step == 'best' and self.vision is not None:
            cells, distances = self._get_sight(agent, occupied, system)
            return self._get_best(agent, cells, system, distances)
        if self.step in ('neighbor', 'best'):
            cells = self._get_cells(agent, occupied)
            if self.step == 'best':
                return self._get_best(agent, cells, system)
            return cells[int(rng.integers(len(cells)))] if cells else None
        position = np.asarray(agent.location, dtype=float)
        if self.step == 'gaussian':
            return position + rng.normal(0.0, self._get_parameter_value('scale', system), position.shape)
        direction = rng.normal(size=position.shape)
        length = self._get_parameter_value('scale', system) * (
            1.0 + rng.pareto(self._get_parameter_value('exponent', system))
        )
        return position + length * direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)

    def _charge(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Charge the cost of one step taken to an agent."""
        if isinstance(self.cost, TransferInteraction):
            self.cost.transfer(agent, agent, system)
        elif self.cost is not None:
            self.cost(agent, system)

    def _take(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, destination: object, occupied: set[object]) -> bool:
        """Move an agent to a destination unless an exclusive movement finds it held.

        It returns whether it moved.
        """
        if not self.exclusive:
            agent.move_to(destination)
            return True
        if destination == agent.location_key:
            return True
        if destination in occupied:
            return False
        occupied.discard(agent.location_key)
        agent.move_to(destination)
        occupied.add(agent.location_key)
        return True

    def _move(
        self,
        agent: AgentViewProtocol,
        system: SystemViewProtocol,
        probability: float,
        occupied: set[object],
    ) -> None:
        """Take the attempted steps of one agent.

        Each step has its probability and acceptance, and every step is charged.
        """
        for _ in range(self._count_attempts(system)):
            if probability < 1.0 and system.rng.random() >= probability:
                continue
            destination = self._get_destination(agent, system, occupied)
            if destination is None:
                continue
            if self.accept is not None and system.rng.random() >= self.accept(agent, destination, system):
                continue
            if self._take(agent, destination, occupied):
                self._charge(agent, system)

    def _move_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Move one agent whose condition holds, in its own activation."""
        if agent.alive and (self.condition is None or self.condition(agent, system)):
            occupied = (
                {other.location_key for other in system.get_agents(self._get_role('target'))}
                if self.exclusive
                else set()
            )
            self._move(agent, system, self._get_parameter_value('probability', system), occupied)

    def _move_all(self, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Move every agent of the group whose condition holds.

        They move in their order or in random order.
        """
        agents = system.get_agents(self._get_role('target'))
        occupied = {agent.location_key for agent in agents} if self.exclusive else set()
        probability = self._get_parameter_value('probability', system)
        order = system.rng.permutation(len(agents)) if self.schedule == 'random-sequential' else range(len(agents))
        for index in order:
            agent = agents[int(index)]
            if agent.alive and (self.condition is None or self.condition(agent, system)):
                self._move(agent, system, probability, occupied)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rule of the movement.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rule that moves the agents every step.
        """
        if self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._move_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        return [RuleLaw(self._move_all, phase=self.phase)]

class TransferInteraction(Interaction):
    """An interaction that moves amounts of states from one member to another.

    A leg moves an amount out of a state of the source member, or out of `Source()`, the environment, into a state of
    the target member, or into `Sink()`. The first leg moves `amount` from `state` into `into`, and `legs` add more. All
    amounts are read before any moves, so each leg sees the states as they were before the transfer. What a source state
    loses, the target state gains, unless a leg starts at `Source()` or ends at `Sink()`. A guard skips the transfer
    where it does not hold.

    The argument `form` chooses how the transfer runs:

    - `'symbolic'`: transfer laws between the source and the target of one element, or between member `i` of both
      groups. The amounts, the guard, and the rates are numbers or functions of the namespace, which reads the roles as
      `namespace.source` and `namespace.target`. With a `rate` the amount moves in jumps, and with `offset` each member
      transfers to the member `offset` places along the group. Every leg is reported as a flow.
    - `'agent'`: an agent rule, whose amounts and guard are functions of the source agent, the target agent, and the
      system view. The members are paired by `pairing`, and the pairs act in random order, or each member of `actor`
      acts in its own activation under the schedule `'member'`.

    A leg end `'<role>.<state>'` names a state of the element another role binds, so one transfer moves amounts between
    several holders, such as the payments of a circuit of sectors. A leg end of the agent form may also name
    `'<reference>.<state>'`, the state of the member that a reference state of the agent names, such as
    `'bank.deposits'` for the deposits of a customer's bank. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their
    names from `_get_role`.

    Unlike `RateInteraction`, which changes one state, it takes from one state what it adds to another, so the amount is
    conserved. Choose it when a quantity moves between holders, such as money, people, or mass.

    It appears in many fields. People move from susceptible to infected in an epidemic, money flows between accounts in
    an economy, water flows between reservoirs, and predators gain the biomass of the prey they eat.

    Args:
        label:
            The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as `'infection'`.

        source:
            The path of the element or group the amounts leave.

        target:
            The path of the element or group the amounts enter, the source again for a transfer within members.

        state:
            The name of the state of the source the first leg takes from, or `Source()` for the environment.

        into:
            The name of the state of the target the first leg adds to, `Sink()` for the environment, or `None` for
            `state`.

        amount:
            The amount of the first leg, a number or a function.

        flow:
            The name the symbolic form reports the first leg under, such as `'payment'`, or the empty string for
            `flow_0`. A named flow is reported as `<path>.<flow>` when the source and the target are one element or
            group, and as `<label>.<flow>` otherwise. A leg without a name is reported as `<label>.flow_<index>`.

        pairing:
            How members are paired. The symbolic form takes `'members'` alone.

            - `'members'`: member `i` of the source with member `i` of the target.
            - `'random'`: every source member with a random target member.
            - `'pairs'`: disjoint random pairs.
            - `'neighbors'`: every source member with the target members in the cells or nodes around it.
            - `'neighbor-pairs'`: disjoint random pairs of neighbours.
            - `'cell'`: the source and target members that stand in one cell or node.
            - `'site'`: every source member with the site of a target field at its cell, where a negative amount
              takes from the site and the functions take the cell in place of a target agent.

            The agent form also takes a `PartnerSpec`, which pairs members within a radius, by score, or with a
            fallback, or a function `pairing(sources, targets, rng, capacity)` that returns pairs, whose capacity is
            `partners`, or 1 without it. Under the schedule `'member'` it receives the actor alone as its first
            sequence, and the partners of the actor are the second items of its pairs.

        legs:
            Further legs, each a tuple of a state or `Source()`, a state, `Sink()`, or `None`, an amount, and
            optionally the name of its flow.

        fallback:
            The path of the group whose members the agent form pairs with instead of the target members in a step in
            which no target member lives, or `None` for no fallback.

        guard:
            A function that returns whether a pair transfers, a condition of the namespace or a boolean of the agents,
            or `None` for every pair.

        rate:
            The rate of jumps of the symbolic form, a number or a function of the namespace, or `None` for a
            continuous flow.

        reverse_rate:
            The rate of the jumps of the symbolic form that move the amounts back from the target to the source, a
            number or a function of the namespace, or `None` for no reverse jumps.

        offset:
            The number of places along the group order from every source member to its target member, such as `1`
            for the next member, or 0 to pair the members of the roles. A draw in an amount is then one draw per edge,
            which both ends read.

        boundary:
            Past the ends of the group order, `'periodic'` closes a ring and `'fixed'` holds no member.

        form:
            The lowering, `'symbolic'` to transfer laws or `'agent'` to an agent rule.

        schedule:
            The order of the agent form, `'random-sequential'` over the pairs, or `'member'` over the actors.

        actor:
            The role whose members act under the schedule `'member'`, `'source'` or `'target'`.

        partners:
            The number of partners an actor draws at random under the schedule `'member'`, or `None` for all of them.

        remove:
            The member of a pair that transfers that is removed, `'source'`, `'target'`, or `None`.

        phase:
            The phase the rule of the agent form runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        settlement:
            A function `settlement(source, target, amounts, system)` that settles a pair of agents from the amounts of
            the legs, read once, in place of moving them, or `None` to move them.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The form, the pairing, the schedule, the actor, the removal, or the boundary is unknown, a leg is
            malformed, two legs share a flow name, the symbolic form has an agent pairing, a fallback, or a settlement,
            the agent form a rate, an offset, or a flow name, a reverse rate has no rate, an offset is not a whole
            number or pairs two groups, a leg end of the symbolic form names no role, the settlement cannot be called
            or pairs with a site, or the schedule `'member'` has a pairing it cannot draw, raised by `prepare`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import TransferInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
        >>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
        >>> class TankElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, visual=None, *, level: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        ...         self.level = level
        >>> flow = TransferInteraction(
        ...     'flow', source='upper', target='lower', state='level', amount=lambda s: s.source.level / 2
        ... )
        >>> tanks = [TankElement('upper', level=4.0), TankElement('lower')]
        >>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=tanks, interactions=[flow])
        >>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1.0)
        >>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('upper.level')[-1] + trajectory.get_values('lower.level')[-1]), 6)
        4.0
    """

    law_classes: ClassVar[tuple[type[BaseLaw], ...]] = (MatchLaw, RuleLaw, TransferLaw)

    def _get_tags(self) -> Tags:
        """Return the tags of the rules of the agent form or of the transfers.

        The transfers jump when they have a rate.
        """
        if self._get_argument('form') == 'agent':
            return self._get_variant_tags((RuleLaw,))
        return self._get_variant_tags((TransferLaw,), stochastic=self._get_argument('rate') is not None)

    def _get_draws(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the agent form draws.

        It draws by its order, random pairs or partners, or a number of partners.
        """
        if self._get_argument('form') != 'agent':
            return self.draws
        drawn = self.pairing in ('random', 'pairs', 'neighbor-pairs') or not isinstance(self.pairing, str | None)
        return super()._get_draws() or drawn or self.partners is not None

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        source: Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ElementKind.ANY,))],
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ElementKind.ANY,))],
        state: str | Source,
        into: str | Sink | None = None,
        amount: Amount,
        flow: str = '',
        pairing: str | Pairing | PartnerSpec = 'members',
        legs: Sequence[Leg] = (),
        fallback: Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(elements=(ElementKind.ANY,))] = None,
        guard: Callable[..., object] | None = None,
        rate: Amount | None = None,
        reverse_rate: Amount | None = None,
        offset: int = 0,
        boundary: str = 'periodic',
        form: str = 'symbolic',
        schedule: str = 'random-sequential',
        actor: str = 'source',
        partners: int | None = None,
